title: Unclear volatility computation in composite oracles
exploit_path: Composite oracle ignores interim-token volatility, so quoted amountOut can be wrong; a trader can swap against the mispriced path, but magnitude and reachability are unproven.

title: Unused ERC20 tokens are not refunded, and can be stolen by attacker
exploit_path: Residual basket tokens from single-token joins are never refunded; attacker calls joinTokenSingle with a malicious output basket/swap and routes the leftovers to themselves.

title: previousPrices Is Never Updated Upon Syncing Token Price
exploit_path: LiquidityBasedTWAP previousPrices is never updated, so weights use stale initial prices; mispriced liquidity can be traded against, but the excerpt does not quantify the edge.

title: ConvexStakingWrapper, StakingRewards Wrong implementation will send concur rewards to the wrong receiver
exploit_path: MasterChef keys userInfo on _msgSender(), so rewards accrue to the wrapper caller; whoever calls the wrapper's deposit/withdraw path captures rewards owed to end users.

title: Strategy Migration May Leave Tokens in the Old Strategy Impacting Share Calculations
exploit_path: Strategy migration can strand tokens outside totalValue, understating shares; a new depositor then mints cheap shares and profits when the stranded tokens are migrated back.

title: Pendle Uses Wrong Return Value For swapExactTokensForTokens()
exploit_path: Pendle lend() reads index 0 (input amount) as output, so PTs are minted against the wrong value; attacker supplies a small input and receives over-minted PTs.

title: Migration::withdrawContribution falsely assumes that user should get exactly his original contribution back
exploit_path: withdrawContribution refunds the original deposit rather than a pro-rata share after buyout PnL; an early exiter can take more than their share and leave a deficit.

title: Auctions can end in epoch after intended, underpaying withdrawers
exploit_path: Auctions extended by late bids spill into the next epoch while liquidation accounting uses the old epoch; a bidder can settle on terms that underpay withdrawers.

title: Public vaults can become insolvent because of missing yIntercept update
exploit_path: beforePayment fails to reduce yIntercept, overstating public-vault totalAssets; a depositor can enter/exit at an inflated share price and dilute the vault.

title: Old stakers can steal deposits of new stakers in StakingFundsVault
exploit_path: updateAccumulatedETHPerLP counts newly deposited ETH as rewards before LP minting; an existing LP holder claims the new staker's deposit.

title: reentrancy attack during mint() function in Position contract which can lead to removing of the other user’s limit orders or stealing contract funds because initId is set low value
exploit_path: Position.mint() calls _safeMint before updating arrays; reenter via onERC721Received to cancel other users' limit orders and skew initId/interest in the attacker's favour.

title: Anyone can wipe complete state of any collateral at any point
exploit_path: ClearingHouse.safeTransferFrom does not require an active auction, so currentOfferPrice is zero; with the settleAuction &&/|| bug the caller can settle and wipe collateral state for free.

title: Issue H-10: Missing validation of snapshotId makes it possible for the investor to claim unlocked capitals from the same snapshot multiple times
exploit_path: Zero snapshotId is not rejected, so lastClaimedSnapshotIds resets to 0; the investor re-claims the same unlocked capital repeatedly.

title: Reward accounting is incorrect in BathBuddy contract
exploit_path: BathBuddy rewards are not checkpointed on BathToken mint/burn/transfer; a holder can enter just before a distribution and claim a disproportionate share.

title: Vault.mintYieldFee function can be called by anyone to mint Vault Shares to any recipient address
exploit_path: mintYieldFee has no access control on _recipient; any caller mints accrued fee shares to an arbitrary address, stealing them from the vault.

title: All assets of (m)TapiocaOFT can be stealed by depositing to strategy cross chain call with 1 amount but maximum shares possible
value_at_risk: all assets held by the (m)TapiocaOFT / its strategy and YieldBox positions
exploit_path: 1) Call sendToStrategy cross-chain with amount=1 and a huge attacker-supplied _share. 2) The source chain debits only 1 unit. 3) On the destination, strategyDeposit -> depositToYieldbox recomputes _amount from _share via yieldBox.toAmount, crediting the attacker with a large deposit. 4) Withdraw the credited amount from YieldBox.
preconditions: TOFT/strategy holds funds; attacker can send a LayerZero cross-chain message.

title: The getVertexBalance function should be improved
exploit_path: Duplicate tokens in withdraw inputs are not prevented, so accounting can be double-counted and the caller withdraws more than intended.

title: LP May Withdraw Excessive Liquidity
exploit_path: CoreVault.totalAssets() returns protocol-wide AUM while shares are per-vault; an LP of one vault redeems against combined AUM and takes other vaults' assets.

title: BptPriceWeightPool uses totalSupply() instead of getActualSupply() for newer weighted pools
exploit_path: BptPriceWeightPool uses totalSupply() instead of getActualSupply(), mispricing preminted-BPT pools; misvaluation can be exploited in Omnipool deposits/withdrawals, magnitude unproven.

title: BBLiquidation/SGLLiquidation::_updateBorrowAndCollateralShare liquidator can bypass bad debt handling to ensure whole liquidation reward
exploit_path: Liquidator sets a small maxBorrowPart so collateral always covers the repay slice, taking the full liquidation reward while leaving bad debt on the protocol.

title: Signatures can be replayed in withdraw() to withdraw more tokens than the user originally intended.
exploit_path: TimelockTokenPool.withdraw() recovers a signer from a hash with no nonce; the same signature is replayed to withdraw repeatedly.

title: Hourly Price Consists of a Single Trade
exploit_path: New hour bucket holds only the current trade but gets the largest TWAP weight; an attacker can skew the funding price with a single trade.

title: mergeTranches()/refinancePartial() lack of nonReentrant
exploit_path: mergeTranches/refinancePartial lack nonReentrant and validator callbacks can reenter, creating multiple live loans against one collateral NFT.

title: PrismaConnector can mint a position below the desired health factor
exploit_path: PrismaConnector checks getNominalICR instead of price-aware ICR, so an unhealthy trove can be opened; borrower can extract and leave bad debt.

title: Unassigned pool earnings can be stolen when a maturity borrow is liquidated by depositing at maturity with 1 principal
exploit_path: Liquidation path sets canDiscount=false and ignores unassigned earnings; attacker borrows then deposits at maturity with principal=1 and claims the ignored earnings.

title: updateAllPositionFromBalanceMargin function mistakenly increments positions "fromBalance"
exploit_path: updateAllPositionFromBalanceMargin adds the full change to each position, inflating fromBalance; may let the trader withdraw more than entitled.

title: H-15. ReseedBarn.sol doesn't initialize of `s.sys.fert.recapitalized`
exploit_path: Missing fert.recapitalized init misprices Unripe conversions and allows minting after debt is repaid; arbitrage value depends on post-migration state.

title: Incorrect accounting bug of the yDUSD vault leads to total loss of depositors’ DUSD assets
exploit_path: DUSD minted to yDUSD raises totalAssets with totalSupply=0, so a depositor gets 0 shares and the vault keeps the assets; an existing/first holder captures them.

title: Forcing Starknet handlers to be whitelisted on the same chain allows exploit of BurnUnlock mode to drain handler funds
exploit_path: Same-chain handler whitelisting enables Starknet-to-Starknet messages under BurnUnlock; attacker messages to self repeatedly unlock tokens from the handler.

title: Issue H-1: A Reserve Borrow Rate can be significantly decreased after liquidation
exploit_path: _repayDebtTokens writes burnt shares into nextDebtShares, so a small liquidation cuts the borrow rate; a borrower can suppress interest after a dust liquidation.

title: totalEarnings is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the Vault insolvent
exploit_path: totalEarnings mixes ETH-denominated protocol fees with share-scaled terms, overstating earnings; variable-side users withdraw more than the vault holds.

title: Malicious actors can exploit user-approved allowances on VaultRouter to drain their ERC20 tokens
exploit_path: VaultRouter PULL_TOKEN_FROM/PUSH_TOKEN_FROM let any caller move tokens from users who approved the router; attacker crafts commands to pull victim balances. Gate is the standing allowance.

title: ElixirStrategy wrong withdrawal accounting allows undercollateralized borrowing
exploit_path: withdrawnAmount is computed with balanceBefore=0, so pre-existing holdings count as yield; registry collateral inflates and the attacker borrows beyond collateral.

title: NAV calculation inconsistency due to underlying token position in pool configuration
exploit_path: computeNAV treats the underlying inconsistently, overstating NAV when it sits outside the pools; a depositor can mint/withdraw at the inflated price.

title: Reentrancy Vulnerability During Lock Cancelations
exploit_path: LockKeeper.cancelLock transfers before deleting the lock; a malicious recipient reenters and re-claims the same unclaimedAmount repeatedly.

title: Incorrect Uniswap V3 cardinality check uses observationCardinalityNext
exploit_path: validateCardinalities reads observationCardinalityNext, admitting pools whose current buffer is too small; an attacker can then move the TWAP used for pricing.

title: index-v3#claimTokens ignores refreshed USD valuations causing value leakage on price increases
exploit_path: claimTokens burns the historical usdAmount snapshot but transfers tokens at refreshed prices; after a price rise the user withdraws more value than recorded.

title: Reentrancy in Vesting.sol:claim() will allow users to drain the contract due to executing .call() on user's address before setting s.index = uint128(i)
exploit_path: Vesting.claim() calls the claimant before writing s.index; reentrancy repeats the claim until the contract is drained.

title: Incorrect user accounting in withdraw method
exploit_path: withdraw subtracts burned shares from user.amount (underlying) instead of the underlying withdrawn; accounting drifts and a user can over-withdraw over time.

title: [H-01] User can repeat calling `withdrawExodus()` to steal all tokens
value_at_risk: token balance held by the Nume settlement contract
exploit_path: 1) Obtain a valid signature/proof showing a pre-settlement balance. 2) Call withdrawExodus(); it pays the claimed balance but never tracks or decrements the withdrawn amount. 3) Replay the same proof until the contract's token balance is drained.
preconditions: Any account with a claim; signature has no per-user withdrawal counter.

title: [H-01] UniV3TokenizedLp can be attacked by an initial donation
exploit_path: Empty vault: first depositor mints 1 wei share, donates tokens, and later withdraws outsized value while later deposits mint zero shares.

title: [H-03] activeValidatorCount is never set or increased
exploit_path: activeValidatorCount never increments, so remainingProofs=0; _updateSnapshot can run twice and double-count creditedNodeETH, inflating a node's credit.

title: [H-01] Manipulatable oracle and breaking slippage protection
exploit_path: buy() prices off Uniswap V2 getAmountsOut with a fixed slippagePercent; attacker sandwiches the pool to force an unfavourable rate and captures the delta.

title: Cross-vault misattribution leads to incorrect OmoVaults valuation
exploit_path: OmoVault.totalAssets() sums agent positions from all vaults; a borrower can inflate one vault's share price and redeem against another vault's positions.

title: [H-04] Duplicate tokenId in delegate list may inflate votes
exploit_path: Duplicate tokenIds in delegate checkpoints inflate voting balance; an attacker can amplify governance weight with a small NFT position.

title: DELEGATECALL to staking precompile allows theft of all staked MON
entry_point: staking precompile precompile_delegate, reached via DELEGATECALL from an attacker contract
value_at_risk: all MON staked through the staking precompile / precompile-held balance
exploit_path: 1) Deploy contract C whose function DELEGATECALLs the staking precompile's precompile_delegate with a chosen input and msg.value. 2) DELEGATECALL preserves msg.sender/msg.value, so the precompile credits stake to the attacker without receiving the MON. 3) Repeat to build unbacked stake, then undelegate/withdraw the MON from the precompile balance.
preconditions: Monad client before the later fix commit (finding was found at 4cbb1742); attacker needs only a normal account and a contract.

title: Enable Mode Signature can be replayed
exploit_path: enableModeSignature has no nonce of its own; a captured enable-mode signature can be replayed to re-enable a module. Impact depends on module semantics.

title: VaultImplementation.buyoutLien does not update the new public vault's parameters and does not transfer assets between the vault and the borrower
exploit_path: buyoutLien does not update the new public vault's slope/yIntercept/epoch liens or settle the difference with msg.sender; vault accounting is left wrong, exploitable by a subsequent depositor/borrower.

title: Anyone can steal protocol's LLido assets and ether balance using its distributive functions
value_at_risk: LLido contract ETH balance and converted liquidity
exploit_path: 1) Call claimRevenueShareDevTeam or earningPulls directly; neither has access control. 2) The call triggers LLido.allToEth and transfers the contract's ETH to the caller or to an attacker-chosen bountyPullerTo_. 3) Repeat across both functions to sweep the balance.
preconditions: Controller holds ETH or convertible LLido liquidity.

title: Cloning a `subGauge` can result in an uninitialized proxy
exploit_path: A cloned subGauge proxy is left uninitialized; an attacker initializes it and controls the gauge's accounting/rewards.

title: GoldbarLogic.sol: Anyone can buy gold bar sold for ETH without paying AND/OR drain the whole contract
entry_point: GoldbarLogic ETH purchase path (function name not given in the report extract)
value_at_risk: entire ETH balance held by GoldbarLogic
exploit_path: 1) Attacker lists a gold bar at a price equal to the contract's ETH balance. 2) Calls the ETH buy path with msg.value=0; the contract never validates msg.value. 3) Because balance >= price, it pays the seller (attacker) and transfers the bar to the buyer (attacker), emptying the contract. 4) The minimum-amount check is also overflow-prone.
preconditions: Contract holds ETH and the attacker can be both seller and buyer.

title: Merkle.checkMembership allows existence proofs for the same leaf in multiple locations in the tree
exploit_path: Merkle.checkMembership accepts arbitrary indices for one leaf; a deposit output can be exited at multiple indices, double-spending the deposit.

title: Anyone can bypass faultDisputeGameIsResolved() storage proofs to drain protocol escrowed funds for Cannon-specific chains
value_at_risk: escrowed funds backing cross-chain intents on Cannon-specific chains
exploit_path: 1) Call proveWorldStateCannon with faultDisputeGameRootClaimStorageProof and faultDisputeGameStateRoot both chosen by the attacker. 2) Step (2)(b) uses the caller's proof against the caller's root for two storage proofs, so SecureMerkleTrie.verifyInclusionProof trivially succeeds. 3) An arbitrary L2 block is treated as valid and resolved. 4) Call proveIntent() for intents that were never fulfilled and claim the escrowed rewards.
preconditions: Cannon-specific chain with an intent/proof escrow; attacker can submit proofs permissionlessly.

title: buyExpiredCollateral Can Disincentivize Challenging
exploit_path: buyExpiredCollateral economics deter challenges; an attacker can let a position expire and buy the collateral cheaply without competition.

title: Ignoring the fee-on-transfer nature of the `pod` token
exploit_path: Fee-on-transfer behavior of the pod token is ignored, so credited amounts exceed received amounts; a depositor can extract the difference.

title: Any public vault without a delegate can be drained
value_at_risk: all assets in any public Astaria vault created without a delegate
exploit_path: 1) Find a public vault whose delegate is address(0). 2) Submit a commitment with an invalid signature (e.g. v not 27/28) so ecrecover returns address(0), equal to the stored delegate. 3) Signature validation passes for arbitrary terms. 4) Borrow the vault's funds against a worthless NFT and default.
preconditions: A public vault deployed without a delegate; attacker needs a valueless NFT and gas.

title: Claiming liquidationAccountant will reduce vault y-intercept by more than the correct amount
exploit_path: Claiming liquidationAccountant reduces the vault y-intercept by more than the correct amount; the resulting mispricing can be exploited by a depositor/withdrawer.

title: Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking
exploit_path: Staking immediately starts accruing rewards that belong to existing stakers because the reward index is not updated before the stake; the new staker claims a share of others' rewards.

title: Drained lender due to `LenderCommitmentGroup_Smart::acceptFundsForAcceptBid()` `_collateralAmount` by `STANDARD_EXPANSION_FACTOR` multiplication
exploit_path: acceptFundsForAcceptBid multiplies _collateralAmount by STANDARD_EXPANSION_FACTOR (1e18), so the borrower posts ~1e18 times less collateral and drains the lender.

title: Staker can manipulate lockedCoinAge and earn rewards in excess of the allowed maximum
exploit_path: lockedCoinAge can be manipulated to earn rewards above the allowed maximum; excess rewards are paid out of the pool.

title: Unfair Manipulation of Winning Chances Due to Stolen Yield on Blast
exploit_path: Stolen yield on Blast changes a depositor's effective balance and thus their winning chances; a depositor can bias the draw in their favour.

title: The same message can be marked as executing multiple times without being executed
exploit_path: The same interop message can be marked executing multiple times without being executed; replay lets the attacker extract the message's value more than once.

title: Flash Loan Sybil Attack to Boost Rewards (NibblerExpress)
exploit_path: Flash-loan/Sybil deposits boost veYFI reward weight; the attacker captures rewards disproportionate to capital locked.

title: Rebase affects swap amounts
exploit_path: A rebase between quote and execution changes swap amounts; the taker can trade against the stale quote.

title: Re-entrancy + flash loan attack can invalidate price check
exploit_path: TWAP check happens before the token transfer; a reentrant token or flash loan moves Uniswap price after the check and before Hypervisor.deposit, so the deposit is mispriced.

title: [H-01] LiquidStakingMain#unstake - Insolvency when multiple users stake and unstake tokens.
exploit_path: The astrAmount>totalStaked branch reduces rewardPool without decreasing totalStaked or transferring; the resulting insolvency lets the last unstaker over-withdraw.

title: [H-02] LFxKyoV3Vault0#redeem - Token Inflation on Vault Expiration Due to Incorrect Redeem Calculation
exploit_path: redeem() divides by a totalSupply that shrinks as others redeem, so later redeemers are overpaid from the pool; an attacker redeems last.

title: [H-02] sbIMF.sol - No locking mechanism results in exploit of stepwise jumps of rewards
exploit_path: No lock/qualification period: deposit immediately before a reward emission and withdraw after, capturing a full interval's rewards.

title: The vault can be drained one share at a time
entry_point: vault withdraw (internal withdraw with assets and shares)
value_at_risk: all assets deposited in the Pods volatility vault
exploit_path: 1) Call withdraw with an asset amount smaller than one share's value. 2) shares rounds down to 0 while assets stays non-zero, so the vault transfers assets without burning shares. 3) Repeat until the vault is empty; any asset amount also lets the caller burn rounded-down shares and extract the excess.
preconditions: Vault holds deposits and has no minimum-withdraw guard; fixed in PR#46 (commit 5ac5e3c).

title: [C03] Borrow rates can be severely miscalculated
exploit_path: Borrow rates are severely miscalculated; a borrower can exploit the wrong rate to pay less interest than owed.

title: Risk of user assets being stolen due to arbitrary execution of data
exploit_path: Arbitrary execution of caller-supplied data lets an attacker move user assets held by the contract.

title: Dust maker liquidity hides residual exposure from OI and margin checks
exploit_path: Dust maker liquidity hides residual exposure from OI/margin checks; a trader can hold more risk than the protocol believes.

title: Token Spooﬁng: Bridge Token X, Get Accounted For Token Y
exploit_path: Stargate composes messages independently of the token; an attacker bridges token X but gets accounted for token Y, or intercepts lzCompose to redirect the deposit.

title: Incorrect Decimal Scaling in usdValue calculation Causes Wrong USD Valuation
exploit_path: Incorrect decimal scaling in usdValue misprices collateral; a borrower can borrow against an inflated valuation.

title: Unrestricted call to destroyInstance
exploit_path: Unrestricted call to destroyInstance can destroy a live instance; the caller can then recreate/reinitialize it or strand its funds.

title: Closing a Position Can Create an In inite Bad Debt
exploit_path: Closing a position can create infinite bad debt; the closing trader walks away with value while the protocol absorbs the loss.

title: Swap operations are vulnerable to sandwich attack
exploit_path: token_out_min_amount is hard-coded to zero, disabling slippage protection; an attacker sandwiches the Osmosis swap and takes the delta.

title: Delegate allowance is not decreased after consumption
exploit_path: Delegate allowance is not decreased after consumption; the delegate can reuse the allowance to move the owner's tokens repeatedly.

title: Missing sender validation allows anyone to add and remove authenticators
exploit_path: Missing sender validation lets anyone add and remove authenticators; the attacker installs their own authenticator and takes over the account.

title: BasePortfolio.sol: Unprotected functions
exploit_path: Unprotected functions in BasePortfolio can move funds or change strategy state without authorization.

title: In lines 128, 178, 180 instead tx.origin should be msg.sender, otherwise
exploit_path: tx.origin used for authorization; a phishing contract can trigger the victim's transfer to the attacker.

title: Significant loss of system assets
exploit_path: Significant loss of system assets in Lyra Option Market; the excerpt is thin but the finding describes an attacker-triggerable asset loss.

title: `unstaking_pool` can be drained by reinitializing the `unstaking_request`
exploit_path: unstaking_request can be reinitialized, letting the caller repoint it and drain the unstaking_pool.

title: Double spending
exploit_path: Double spending in Liquorice: the same obligation/payment can be settled twice.

title: Missing CPI Guard
exploit_path: Missing CPI Guard on Solana leaves token operations exposed to CPI; an attacker can move tokens during a CPI.

title: Message Validation Bypass
exploit_path: Message validation bypass in Canopy lets a crafted message be accepted as valid, enabling unauthorized state changes/value movement.

title: Wrong variable initialization leads to debt write-off and under-
exploit_path: Wrong variable initialization leads to a debt write-off; the borrower's debt is erased while the borrowed funds remain with them.

title: Accumulated interest nullification
exploit_path: Accumulated interest can be nullified; a borrower resets/suppresses accrued interest before repaying.

title: DEPOSITING ON ANY POOL USING ANY TOKEN
exploit_path: Depositing into any pool with any token is accepted; the mismatch misprices the deposit and can be arbitraged.

title: Arbitrary memory manipulation
exploit_path: Arbitrary memory manipulation in Choise; the excerpt supports attacker-controlled execution/state, value at risk unquantified.

title: Attacker Can Get Infinite BVM_ETH Tokens to Drain the Protocol
entry_point: L1 deposit parsing (OptimismPortal.TransactionDeposited) and L2 ETH credit
value_at_risk: BVM_ETH supply and the L1 bridge backing it
exploit_path: 1) Submit an L1 deposit whose ETH value is not balance-checked (negative big.Int or equivalent malformed value). 2) On L2, common.BigToHash turns it into a positive value and the ETH balance is read/adjusted/written without over/underflow checks, crediting both sender and recipient. 3) Withdraw the minted BVM_ETH to L1.
preconditions: Permissionless L1 deposit path; L2 client before the fix.

title: amountOut Not Converted to shares
exploit_path: amountOut is in BentoBox amount units but _transfer expects shares; a swapper receives more tokens than intended when strategies have accrued profit.

title: [C-01] Withdrawing collateral and fees and bypassing trust safety mechanism
exploit_path: Beneficiary verification only checks the proxy codehash, not the Safe singleton; a malicious singleton fakes ownership/threshold and the attacker withdraws collateral and fees.

title: [C-02] Wrong‑Offset Ed25519 instruction introspection enables forged approvals
exploit_path: Ed25519 instruction introspection omits program_id/inline/offset checks; forged approvals are accepted and the attacker spends the victim's tokens.

title: Improper length validation in BLS signature library allows RNG manipulation
exploit_path: BLS library reads without length validation; the random beacon hashes the submitted signature, so an attacker pads signatures and front-runs to bias randomness.

title: Incorrect reward calculation scaling leads to 1,000,000x higher rewards than intended
exploit_path: Reward calculation scaling is off by 1e6; a staker claims rewards a million times larger than intended.

title: Key Registry Not Recognized as a Privileged Call Target
exploit_path: Key Registry is not treated as a privileged call target; an attacker can register/replace keys and act for the identity.

title: Anyone can steal tokens of shareholders
value_at_risk: tokens allocated to shareholders in an active distribution
exploit_path: 1) Call setShareholderAddress(distributionId, attackerAddress); the function has no access control. 2) The distribution's shareholder address now points at the attacker. 3) Claim the allocated tokens.
preconditions: An active token distribution exists; no role or capital needed.

title: Transfer of ZVL access control is unprotected
exploit_path: Transfer of ZVL access control is unprotected; an attacker can seize the role and the assets it controls.

title: Manipulation of vault proposals
exploit_path: Vault proposals can be manipulated by a depositor to favour their own withdrawal.

title: Liquidity incorrectly updated upon liquidation
exploit_path: Liquidity is incorrectly updated on liquidation; the mispriced pool can be arbitraged.

title: Multiplication overflow risk
exploit_path: Multiplication overflow in Mask Social redpacket; an attacker crafts amounts that overflow and claim more than deposited.

title: Improper Access Control in Staking
exploit_path: Improper access control in staking lets an unprivileged caller stake/unstake or claim on behalf of another user.

title: enterTransient is permissionless and executes enter with attacker-staged transient inputs High impact finding
exploit_path: enterTransient is permissionless and executes enter() with attacker-staged transient inputs; the attacker enters a position on terms meant to be internal.

title: Inflated voting balance due to duplicated veNFTs within a checkpoint
exploit_path: Duplicated veNFTs within a checkpoint inflate voting balance; governance weight can be amplified.

title: claimWait Can Be Circumvented
exploit_path: claimWait can be circumvented; an attacker claims before the intended wait and captures rewards.

title: Inflation caused by claimed credits
exploit_path: Inflation caused by claimed credits; the accounting error lets a claimer take more than their share.

title: WS Message Replay Due To Lack of Freshness Check
exploit_path: Withdrawal WS messages lack a freshness check; a captured message can be replayed to trigger a second withdrawal.

title: Second Challenge Period Can Be Bypassed
exploit_path: The second challenge period can be bypassed; a challenger/winner can finalize early and take the disputed value.

title: Sandwiched reports poison index EMA and enable wrongful taker backstops
exploit_path: Sandwiched reports poison the index EMA; the attacker then trades against the distorted index or triggers wrongful taker backstops.

title: Zero‑Price Settlement Can Create Immediate Bad Debt in Binary Markets
exploit_path: Zero-price settlement in binary markets creates immediate bad debt; the settler takes value while the market absorbs the loss.

title: Stolen Protocol Fees Due To Arbitrary Recipient
exploit_path: Protocol fees can be sent to an arbitrary recipient; the caller redirects the fee stream to themselves.

title: Wrong price scale for `GasOracle`
exploit_path: GasOracle price scale is wrong; mispriced gas feeds can be exploited in the dependent market.

title: StakedCitadel doesn't use correct balance for internal accounting
exploit_path: StakedCitadel uses the wrong balance for internal accounting; a depositor can mint/withdraw at a favourable rate.

title: openPosition() use stale feeGrowthInside0LastX128/feeGrowthInside1LastX128
exploit_path: openPosition uses stale feeGrowthInside values; the position's fee accounting is wrong and can be gamed.

title: calculate Loss is vulnerable to flashloan attack
exploit_path: calculateLoss is flash-loan manipulable; the attacker moves the loss estimate and settles at a favourable value.

title: Arbitrary transactions possible due to insufficient signature validation
exploit_path: Insufficient signature validation allows arbitrary transactions from the smart wallet.

title: Attacker could steal almost all the bonus tokens in BathBuddy Vesting Wallet
exploit_path: Attacker can steal almost all bonus tokens from the BathBuddy vesting wallet by triggering the vesting/claim path.

project: 45 Wardens contributed reports to the PoolTogether
title: Too many rewards are distributed when a draw is closed
exploit_path: Too many rewards are distributed when a draw is closed; a participant can claim more than the intended share.

title: Swaps are not split when trade crosses target price
exploit_path: Swaps are not split when crossing the target price; the taker gets a worse/better fill that can be arbitraged.

title: Index Pool always swap to Zero
exploit_path: Index Pool always swaps to zero, so the pool can be drained by trading at the broken price.

title: `UlyssesToken` asset ID accounting error
exploit_path: UlyssesToken asset-ID accounting error misprices shares; a depositor/withdrawer can extract the difference.

title: Ineffective ReserveRatio Enforcement
exploit_path: Reserve-ratio enforcement is ineffective; a borrower can take more than the allowed ratio.

title: Covering impermanent loss allows profiting off asymmetric liquidity provision at expense of reserve holdings
exploit_path: IL coverage lets an LP profit from asymmetric liquidity provision at the expense of reserves.

title: `twTAP.sol`: Reward tokens stored in index 0 can be stolen
exploit_path: Reward tokens stored at index 0 of twTAP can be stolen by a participant who triggers the claim path.

title: `SwapUtils.sol` Wrong implementation
exploit_path: SwapUtils wrong implementation misprices swaps; the difference is arbitrageable.

title: User can evade `liquidation` by depositing the minimum of tokens and gain time to not be liquidated
exploit_path: A borrower evades liquidation by depositing the minimum; the delay lets them exit with value before the price recovers against them.

title: Paymaster ETH can be drained with malicious sender
exploit_path: A malicious sender can drain the paymaster's ETH by crafting userOps that consume the deposit.

title: The use of spot price by CoreSaltyFeed can lead to price manipulation and undesired liquidations
exploit_path: CoreSaltyFeed uses spot price; an attacker manipulates it to force liquidations or borrow against inflated collateral.

title: A malicious user can set any contract as a local `hToken` for an underlying token since there is no access control for `_addLocalToken`
exploit_path: A malicious user can register any contract as a local hToken for an underlying; the fake token is credited and drained.

title: `triggerFee` is stolen from other auctions during `settleWithBuyout()`

exploit_path: 1) A position is liquidated and its debt written off. 2) The collateral is not locked. 3) The user can withdraw collateral that should back the written-off debt.
preconditions: liquidation occurred

title: Contract is drainable due to bypassing “in-range-check” with onPositionUse hook
exploit_path: 1) Attacker mints a double-sided option that bypasses the in-range check via onPositionUse. 2) The position is treated as in-range. 3) Attacker extracts the mispriced option value.
preconditions: CLAMM market with liquidity; hook must be approved by the market

title: Flaw within initiatorDeposit allows for draining the contract
exploit_path: 1) A refund happens. 2) callInitiatorDeposit can still be called afterwards. 3) The deposit is re-executed/reset, letting the attacker withdraw twice.
preconditions: refund occurred; owner-controlled deposit token

title: Gnosis Omnibridge rebalances bypass destination pool accounting
exploit_path: 1) A Gnosis Omnibridge rebalance arrives. 2) The destination path measures the received amount and calls deposit() but bypasses pool accounting. 3) Attacker can mint/claim against unaccounted liquidity.
preconditions: rebalance in flight

title: Missing accesscontrol in afterlockupdate
exploit_path: 1) afterLockUpdate has no access control. 2) Attacker calls it to update reward state for chosen users. 3) Rewards are re-accrued/duplicated and claimed.
preconditions: rewards funded

title: Per-Vault Oracle Overrides Ignored in Slippage Hooks
entry_point: Gauntlet slippage hooks / per-vault oracle overrides
exploit_path: 1) Hooks ignore per-vault oracle overrides. 2) A manipulated/default oracle is used for the limit check. 3) Attacker swaps past the intended slippage bound.
preconditions: vault with oracle override; attacker trades

title: Reentrancy in redeemValidityBond
exploit_path: 1) redeemValidityBond sends ETH before clearing validityBonds. 2) Recipient fallback re-enters and redeems again. 3) Bond is paid multiple times.
preconditions: attacker has a bond to redeem

title: Possible theft of OFT tokens from ShogunLzComposerV1
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sends a crafted LayerZero composable message. 2) The composer processes it without validating the OFT/amount. 3) Attacker receives OFT tokens held by the composer.
preconditions: composer holds OFT tokens; attacker can send LZ messages

title: Signatures can be replayed across deployments due to missing domain separation
exploit_path: 1) Relayer signatures have no domain separation (no contract/chain id). 2) Attacker replays a valid unlock/mint message on another deployment or chain. 3) Tokens are minted/unlocked twice.
preconditions: a valid relayer signature exists and is observable

title: Stale Oracle Cache Enables Protocol-Wide Price Exploitation
exploit_path: 1) cache_price is not called for long periods. 2) A stale cached price is used for borrows/liquidations. 3) Attacker trades against the stale price or liquidates at it.
preconditions: stale cache; market liquidity

title: Transferable shares allow duplicated side reward accrual
exploit_path: 1) Rewards are computed from the current xORO bank balance. 2) xORO is transferable. 3) Attacker moves xORO between addresses to accrue the same rewards twice.
preconditions: transferable xORO; reward index

title: User Can Call fileClaim() Without Paying Policy Premiums Assets ClaimManager.sol
exploit_path: 1) Attacker binds a policy, then defaults on premiums. 2) Still files a valid claim. 3) Receives a payout without paying premiums.
preconditions: policy bound; claim valid

title: Replay attack and revocation inversion on confidentialApprove
exploit_path: 1) A signature authorizing approve/revoke does not bind the status flag. 2) Attacker replays it to invert a revocation or grant. 3) Approval is restored/reused.
preconditions: a prior confidentialApprove signature

title: BuniCornPool.mint callable by anyone enables minting to arbitrary address
exploit_path: 1) Anyone calls mint() at a chosen time. 2) Attacker supplies a victim and an attacker-chosen recipient. 3) Victim's coins are minted to the attacker.
preconditions: pool has liquidity; timing

title: 4.2 Lack of reentrancy protection in token interactions
exploit_path: 1) Token transfer callbacks are not guarded by nonReentrant. 2) Attacker re-enters depositAndBorrow during a callback. 3) Position accounting is duplicated and funds extracted.
preconditions: callback token supported by Fuji

title: Malicious Users Can Exploit Residual Allowance To Steal Assets
value_at_risk: any user's residual approvals to BaseVault
exploit_path: 1) Victim has a residual approval to BaseVault. 2) Attacker calls batchDeposit with _from=victim and an attacker-controlled destination. 3) BaseVault pulls the victim's tokens and sends them to the attacker.
preconditions: victim approval outstanding

title: A malicious lien owner can exploit a reentrancy to steal LP funds
exploit_path: 1) Attacker is a lien owner. 2) endAuction calls decreaseYIntercept into external contracts. 3) Attacker re-enters via cancelAuction and reborrows; the new lien is removed when endAuction resumes. 4) Attacker keeps the funds.
preconditions: attacker holds a lien; auction flow

title: Extraordinary proposal can be used to steal extraordinary amounts of AJNA
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates an extraordinary proposal. 2) Calls voteExtraordinary for every address with delegated voting power (the account parameter is arbitrary). 3) Proposal passes immediately and executes, moving AJNA to the attacker.
preconditions: delegated voting power exists; proposal threshold met

title: Incorrectly implemented modifiers in LybraConfigurator.sol allow any address to call functions that are supposed to be restricted
exploit_path: 1) The modifiers call GovernanceTimelock.checkOnlyRole but ignore the return value. 2) Any address calls initToken/setProtocolReward/etc. 3) Attacker sets himself as fee receiver or mints.
preconditions: restricted functions reachable

title: Issue H-5: Curve V2 Vaults can be drained because CurveV2CryptoEthOracle can be reentered with WETH tokens
exploit_path: 1) The oracle enables read-only reentrancy checks only for the special ETH address, but Curve V2 pools use WETH. 2) Attacker triggers a raw ETH call during a Curve operation. 3) Re-enters the oracle while the pool price is manipulated and drains the vault.
preconditions: vault uses Curve V2 WETH pool; attacker can trigger ETH callback

title: Missing check on helper contract allows arbitrary actions and theft of assets
exploit_path: 1) Attacker supplies a malicious marketHelper. 2) It returns arbitrary calls (borrow, remove collateral) that Magnetar executes with its own authority. 3) Attacker takes the assets.
preconditions: Magnetar holds approvals/positions

title: Missing access control on Earning.update allows manipulation of ETH_Earning
exploit_path: Same as 100281: anyone calls update(); a pool owner avoids the trust-score penalty.
preconditions: attacker is a pool owner

title: Bypassing saleUserCap and whitelist
exploit_path: 1) Whitelist check uses msg.sender, but cap uses _receiver. 2) Attacker mints to many receivers from one whitelisted caller. 3) Bypasses saleUserCap and whitelist.
preconditions: attacker is whitelisted; NFT has resale value

title: Emergence - Signatures Can Be Replayed Across Deployments Or Chains
exploit_path: 1) Signatures have no domain separation and no nonce. 2) Attacker replays a valid signature across deployments/chains or repeatedly. 3) The operation executes again.
preconditions: a valid signature exists

title: EIP Standard Violation
exploit_path: 1) Signatures use EIP-191 instead of EIP-712. 2) The same signature can be replayed on another chain. 3) A proof is accepted twice.
preconditions: a valid signature exists

title: No access control on setIncentivesController()
exploit_path: 1) Anyone calls setIncentivesController. 2) Attacker points it at his own controller. 3) Incentive accrual is redirected/claimed by the attacker.
preconditions: incentives configured; pool has users

title: Stake Manipulation During Cooldown Period Allows Probability Gaming
exploit_path: 1) Attacker joins multiple times after the cooldown starts. 2) Stake is increased after the random outcome window is fixed. 3) Probability of winning is gamed.
preconditions: cooldown begun; prize pool funded

title: AstariaRouter.liquidate(...) can be called multiple times for an expired lien/stack
exploit_path: 1) A lien/stack is expired. 2) Attacker calls liquidate() multiple times for the same lien. 3) Collateral or vault funds are paid out more than once.
preconditions: expired lien; liquidation window

title: Permissions can drain approvals given to certain paymasters
entry_point: Coinbase Smart Wallet Permissions / paymaster approvals
exploit_path: 1) Permissions require an allowlisted paymaster. 2) A permissioned session can route userOps through a paymaster whose approvals are reachable. 3) Attacker drains the paymaster's approved funds.
preconditions: session permission; paymaster approval

title: Too generic calls in GenericBridgeFacet allow stealing of tokens
value_at_risk: tokens approved to the LI.FI diamond
exploit_path: 1) Attacker supplies arbitrary swap calldata through the generic bridge facet. 2) The facet executes calls to attacker-chosen targets with the diamond's approvals. 3) Tokens are transferred to the attacker.
preconditions: victim approvals to the LI.FI diamond; generic call path reachable

title: [BCCR] CDP closing can be used for whale sniping
exploit_path: 1) Attacker pre-opens a strong and a weak CDP. 2) On a price downtick, closes the strong CDP to push TCR near CCR. 3) The event triggers recovery mode and the weak CDP is liquidated; attacker profits as liquidator.
preconditions: price downtick/slashing; capital for two CDPs

title: Wrong tokensToCheck logic in BaseRouter enables attackers to steal funds
exploit_path: 1) The tokensToCheck loop is wrong, so a swap can be executed without validating the output token balance. 2) Attacker routes a swap that pays nothing/less. 3) Router funds are drained.
preconditions: router has token balances/approvals

title: Unset End Tick Allows Malicious Claims
exploit_path: 1) During a swap a position's end tick becomes unset. 2) Attacker claims fees against the unset range. 3) Claims more than entitled.
preconditions: position with unset end tick

title: Incorrect conversion from USD to asset during redemption
exploit_path: 1) Deposit converts asset->USD by multiplying the spot rate; redemption converts back differently. 2) Attacker deposits/redeems across the mismatch. 3) Receives more assets than deposited.
preconditions: spot rate source; vault liquidity

title: Uniswap's pool can be initialized with a different price
exploit_path: 1) Attacker initializes the token/WETH pool at an arbitrary price before the legitimate initialization. 2) The market starts mispriced. 3) Attacker arbitrages the pool.
preconditions: pool not yet initialized; attacker front-runs

title: addTidal , _updateUserTidal , withdrawTidal – Wrong Arithmetic Calculations
exploit_path: 1) Wrong arithmetic in the three functions. 2) Attacker deposits/withdraws to inflate his tidal balance. 3) Withdraws more than deposited.
preconditions: tidal contract funded

title: Signature Verification Bypass
exploit_path: 1) The Solana program verifies signatures incorrectly (instruction sysvar/ed25519 path). 2) Attacker submits a forged signed message. 3) Assets are released to him.
preconditions: bridge holds assets; attacker can submit a message

title: Premature Asset Claim in receiveAssets() Function due to Missing Closure Check
exploit_path: 1) A lot has not sold out/closed. 2) Attacker calls receiveAssets and claims early. 3) Winner selection fairness is broken; attacker can claim.
preconditions: lot open; attacker holds a ticket

title: Vulnerability in PositionInteractionFacet slippage control due to spot price
exploit_path: 1) amountInMaximum is computed from the Uniswap spot price. 2) Attacker moves the spot price before the swap. 3) The slippage check is ineffective and the swap executes at a bad rate.
preconditions: attacker can manipulate the pool; user swap

title: `StakedToken` is vulnerable to share inflation attack via donation
exploit_path: 1) All stakers redeem, leaving totalSupply near zero. 2) Attacker deposits 1 wei and donates a large amount. 3) The next staker's deposit mints zero/too few shares; attacker redeems the donation plus victim deposit.
preconditions: vault empty; attacker front-runs the next depositor

title: H-01 wstETH-ETH Curve LP Token Price can be manipulated to Cause Unexpected Liquidations
exploit_path: 1) The LP token price is read from Curve's virtual price/spot. 2) Attacker manipulates the pool. 3) Positions are liquidated at the wrong price; attacker profits as liquidator.
preconditions: Curve pool liquidity; attacker capital

title: `_listing` mapping not deleted when calling `Listings::reserve` can lead to a token being sold when it shouldn't be for sale
exploit_path: 1) reserve() does not delete _listing. 2) The token remains marked for sale. 3) A buyer can purchase a token that is no longer for sale, or the seller loses it.
preconditions: listing/reserve flow

title: MarginTrading.sol: Missing flash loan initiator check allows attacker to open trades, close trades and steal funds
entry_point: MarginTrading.sol flash loan callback (missing initiator check)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls the flash-loan callback directly (no initiator check). 2) Opens/closes trades with the pool's funds as if the loan were real. 3) Withdraws the proceeds.
preconditions: margin pool funded; callback reachable

title: Malicious users can steal swap fees from liquidity providers
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits just before fee accrual and withdraws after. 2) Fees are socialized across depositors. 3) Attacker captures a share of fees without providing liquidity over time.
preconditions: fee accrual; deposit/withdraw

title: Truncated reserves bypass price safety mechanism when no interest accrues
exploit_path: 1) When no interest accrues, truncatedReserves bypasses the price-change safety limit. 2) Attacker moves the price beyond the intended bound. 3) Liquidations/borrows at the manipulated price.
preconditions: no interest accrual; pool liquidity

title: A transaction can be executed without the required signatures
value_at_risk: all assets controlled by the multisig
exploit_path: 1) The threshold state variable is never checked at execution. 2) Attacker submits/executes a transaction with fewer than threshold signatures (or none). 3) Multisig assets are transferred to the attacker.
preconditions: multisig holds assets; execute entry point reachable

title: The deposit function of the Hypervisor contract should only be called from UniProxy
exploit_path: 1) Hypervisor.deposit is publicly callable. 2) Attacker front-runs with a price manipulation and deposits/withdraws. 3) Steals depositor value.
preconditions: Uniswap pool manipulable; Hypervisor live

title: Malicious pool owner can withdraw earnings without affecting trust score
exploit_path: 1) Pool owner reinvests earnings into a second pool with ~99% owner share. 2) Withdraws from the second pool immediately. 3) Original pool's fs/trust score is unaffected.
preconditions: attacker is a pool owner; can create a second pool

title: H-12. Fund Withdrawal Flaw in preMarket Allows Users to Avoid Settlement Obligations
exploit_path: 1) Seller withdraws SalesRevenue/TaxIncome credited at createTaker. 2) Chooses not to deliver point tokens at settlement. 3) Keeps the buyer's funds.
preconditions: pre-market sale; seller can avoid settlement

title: H-01. No protection implemented against listing clone NFTs
exploit_path: 1) Attacker clones an existing NFT's metadata and lists at 1 wei less. 2) AI-agent buyers pick the clone. 3) Attacker is paid for a worthless NFT.
preconditions: marketplace with automated buyers

title: Voting Power Delegation From Expired Lock Incorrectly Increases Delegatee's Power
exploit_path: 1) Delegation from a fully decayed lock uses stale multipliers. 2) Delegatee receives more voting power than allowed.
preconditions: expired lock; delegation

title: Credentials can be manipulated
exploit_path: 1) createCredential downcasts policyId/amounts to smaller types. 2) Values wrap. 3) Attacker creates a credential with inflated/incorrect limits and borrows against it.
preconditions: credential creation; lending market

title: Potential theft of funds due to the ability to manipulate the AVAX:stAVAX exchange rate
exploit_path: 1) The AVAX:stAVAX rate depends on the contract's balance. 2) Attacker donates/removes AVAX or flash-loans to shift the balance. 3) Mints or redeems at the manipulated rate.
preconditions: attacker can change contract balance; pool funded

title: EdDSA Signature Verification Is Satisfiable
exploit_path: 1) scalarMulFakeGLV accepts a prover-supplied hint and never constrains s2 != 0. 2) Prover sets s1=s2=0; both scalar multiplications are unconstrained. 3) VerifyEdDSAIf accepts a forged signature for any registered public key. 4) Attacker forges a recipient-claim proof and exits a wallet-bound gift.
preconditions: gift ciphertext/claim link public data; proof system accepts forged proof

title: Shares Can Be Transferred With Open Positions
exploit_path: 1) Shares can be transferred/redeemed while positions are open. 2) msg.sender is used where from/owner is required. 3) Attacker transfers shares away, leaving the position's risk with the buyer while keeping the collateral.
preconditions: open positions; share transfer

title: Insecure usage of abi.encodePacked for the signature verification
exploit_path: 1) The signed value uses abi.encodePacked with variable-length fields. 2) Attacker crafts colliding inputs. 3) A signature valid for one mint is reused for another.
preconditions: server signature; mint live

title: Drain All Pools With SuperPool As Collateral
exploit_path: 1) SuperPool shares use the wrong decimals. 2) Attacker deposits/withdraws to exploit the decimal mismatch. 3) Drains all pools used as collateral.
preconditions: SuperPool live; pools have liquidity

title: WRONG DEBT CALCULATIONS DURING WITHDRAWAL
exploit_path: 1) Debt is decreased outside the try block. 2) A failed withdrawal still reduces debt. 3) Attacker repeats to erase debt and withdraw collateral.
preconditions: withdrawal with failing transfer

title: Missing transfer hook in TalosStrategyStaked
exploit_path: 1) Strategy token transfers do not update staking accounting. 2) Attacker transfers to accrue rewards on the same tokens twice.
preconditions: strategy token transfer

title: Broken authentication in endpointCommitPacket
exploit_path: 1) endpointCommitPacket is permissionlessly callable with an arbitrary packet. 2) Attacker commits a forged packet. 3) The packet is executed/liveness disrupted or funds are misrouted.
preconditions: endpoint live; attacker can send packets

title: User's rewards are stored incorrectly during staking.
exploit_path: 1) _stake computes claimable rewards and adds them to userInfo.unclaimed. 2) Attacker stakes/unstakes around reward accrual. 3) Rewards are double-counted.
preconditions: reward pool funded

title: User’s rewards are stored incorrectly during staking.
exploit_path: Same accrual bug as 102581: claimable rewards are added to unclaimed on stake.
preconditions: reward pool funded

title: `SimplePriceOracle.price` is susceptible to integer overflow
exploit_path: 1) price is computed with unchecked arithmetic. 2) An extreme input overflows. 3) The oracle returns a wrong price to consumers.
preconditions: consumer uses the oracle; extreme value

title: Batch mechanism in Liquidation module’s BeginBlocker may allow malicious manipulations
exploit_path: 1) The batch mechanism processes liquidations in an order the attacker can influence. 2) Attacker positions for a favourable liquidation. 3) Captures liquidation value.
preconditions: batch liquidation; attacker capital

title: Stream status not saved after update allows contract funds being drained
value_at_risk: all funds held by the streamswap contract
exploit_path: 1) finalize_stream updates status in memory but does not save it. 2) Attacker calls finalize_stream repeatedly. 3) Each call triggers a BankMsg::Send, draining the contract.
preconditions: a finalized stream; contract holds funds

title: Quotation.sol : Signature verification is liable to signature replay attacks
exploit_path: 1) Signed messages are not unique (no nonce/domain). 2) Attacker replays a valid quotation signature. 3) A second quotation is accepted.
preconditions: a valid signature exists

title: Missing validations in PrivateAllowedAccount account
exploit_path: 1) process_thaw does not validate the account. 2) Attacker thaws a restricted account or redirects a thaw. 3) Transfers value out of a restricted account.
preconditions: permissioned token; attacker has an account

title: SimpleShares allows inﬁnite token creation
value_at_risk: all vault assets represented by SimpleShares
exploit_path: 1) SimpleShares.doTransferFrom calls super.doTransferTo instead of doTransferFrom. 2) Attacker calls transfer(attacker, balance) from his own address. 3) doTransferFrom credits the sender again, doubling the balance. 4) Repeat to mint infinite shares, then redeem vault assets.
preconditions: attacker holds any shares; vault holds assets

title: Deposited tokens are mixed with reward tokens
exploit_path: 1) Deposited CORK and reward CORK are held in the same contract. 2) Attacker stakes/unstakes around reward distribution. 3) Withdraws reward tokens as principal.
preconditions: pool 0 funded with CORK rewards

title: Malicious sqrtPrice when adding liquidity
exploit_path: 1) When the curve completes, the contract adds liquidity at a caller-influenced sqrtPrice. 2) Attacker sets a skewed price. 3) Arbitrages the pool.
preconditions: curve completion; attacker can influence sqrtPrice

title: Missing reward collateral id validations
entry_point: Reward collateral id validation / id-price mapping
exploit_path: 1) Reward token ids and prices are not validated. 2) Attacker manipulates the id-price mapping at any time. 3) Reward accounting is inflated and value is extracted.
preconditions: attacker can set/change the mapping

exploit_path: 1) reservedRegister processes a registration with a reverseRecord flag. 2) The reverse record is assigned to the wrong owner. 3) Attacker controls the victim's reverse name.

title: Malicious actor cause rebase to an old inflation multiplier

title: One side players have more probability of winning than the other.

title: minIn checks can be bypassed via different routes

title: A malicious user can inﬂate his voting power via merge()

title: Malicious users can settle asstes using settlement rates of other assets

title: MedianDeltaBreaker.shouldTrigger() allows any external actor to incorrectly update the medianRatesEMA

preconditions: attacker can call shouldTrigger() repeatedly around a rate update

title: Insufficient sanitation in uploadEpochRoot

exploit_path: uploadEpochRoot accepts a caller-supplied _vault and authorizes via _vault.owner(); an attacker deploys a vault that returns msg.sender from owner(), uploads an epoch root with a chosen token and amount, and claims the distributor's tokens.

title: All rewards in `StrategERC3525` can be stolen with a single token

title: Unchecked collection in ticket redemption

title: Race Condition: Changing paying token before setting new price
value_at_risk: mint revenue; the price paid per NFT

preconditions: owner switches the paying token before setting the new price

title: MEV Extractable From distribute() Function
value_at_risk: the reward distribution for a period
exploit_path: stake immediately before distribute() and withdraw immediately after in the same block to capture a share of the distribution disproportionate to time staked.

title: ERC777 and similar token implementations allow a stealing of funds when transferring tokens

exploit_path: an ERC777 sender reenters transferFrom via tokensToSend while the manager measures balance deltas, producing nested transfers and multiple cross-chain messages with inflated amounts; the attacker receives more tokens on the destination chain than were locked.

title: An attacker can massively inflate the share value

exploit_path: deposit an amount that mints zero shares while raising total assets, inflating the value of one share, then redeem the inflated share to take the first depositor's funds and DoS the pair.
preconditions: attacker must be first to a freshly created pair and control the donation/rounding

title: [Prover Protocol] Verifier Accepts Any Permutation Query
value_at_risk: soundness of the zkEVM proof system and the bridge/rollup funds it secures
exploit_path: the permutation query compiler compares table A with A instead of B, so any permutation query is accepted; a malicious prover can therefore produce a proof the verifier accepts for an invalid state transition and withdraw or mint against the rollup.
preconditions: attacker must be able to submit a proof to the on-chain verifier

value_at_risk: the collateral NFT and the auction proceeds
exploit_path: a lender and a liquidator collude to block the auction and seize the collateral at a discount to its value.
preconditions: attacker must be both the lender and the liquidator (two protocol roles)

title: All funds can be stolen from FixedStrikeOptionTeller using a token with malicious decimals
value_at_risk: payout and quote tokens held by the teller for all deployed options
exploit_path: a token with malicious decimals makes the teller's payout/quote accounting overstate the amount due, letting the attacker drain collateral held for every option the teller issued.
preconditions: the teller must accept the malicious token as payout or quote asset

title: Exposure to sandwich attack
value_at_risk: the value lost to price impact on a user swap
exploit_path: a sandwich around a user's swap captures the price impact as profit.
preconditions: attacker can order transactions around the victim swap

title: Total MGP in vote is not decreased during unvote.
value_at_risk: governance voting power in the Magpie vote escrow
exploit_path: unvote() does not decrement the total MGP counted in the vote, so repeated vote/unvote cycles leave the account's effective voting power inflated.

title: Combination of several issues and occurrences allows users the creation of almost risk-free and permanent staking position
value_at_risk: staking rewards funded by other stakers
exploit_path: combining several issues lets a user open a staking position that earns rewards with no effective lock and no risk, then exit at will.
preconditions: several reported issues must co-exist in the deployed deployment

title: tokenToXtz sends the tokens to the user
value_at_risk: all XTZ held by the Dexter contract
exploit_path: tokenToXtz transfers tokensSold to the caller-supplied `to` address instead of the contract, so the caller keeps the tokens and still receives tezos, draining Dexter's XTZ.
preconditions: Dexter holds XTZ liquidity

title: Bonus multiplier abuse
value_at_risk: the staking pool's share supply and the tokens backing it
exploit_path: deposit mints base + lock bonus + stakingBonusHandler bonus shares, but withdraw burns only base + lock shares; repeat lock-for-MIN_LOCK_DURATION then withdraw to mint unlimited bonus shares and dilute the pool.

title: trustedForwarder can be used to impersonate any account or contract
value_at_risk: any account or contract that trusts the forwarder for msg.sender
exploit_path: the trusted forwarder is trusted for msg.sender recovery, so whoever controls or can call it can impersonate any account; the publisher withheld the body, so the concrete call path is not established locally.

title: no-revert-on-transfer ERC20 tokens can be drained
value_at_risk: the buyer's ETH/premium and the vault's claimed NFT collateral
exploit_path: create a vault with an ERC20 token but TokenType.ERC721; createVault calls ERC721.transferFrom on the token, which for a no-revert-on-transfer ERC20 returns false without moving tokens, so the vault is created unbacked while the creator collects the buyer's payment.
preconditions: a no-revert-on-transfer ERC20 (e.g. ZRX) and a buyer for the vault

title: Vault._update_debt sets last update before accruing, resulting in zero interest
value_at_risk: interest owed by borrowers to the vault's lenders
exploit_path: _update_debt writes last_debt_update before computing elapsed time, so elapsed time is zero and no interest accrues; a borrower can roll debt indefinitely without paying interest.
preconditions: attacker is a borrower in the vault

title: Pool.buyNFT() Accepts Any Collection Address
value_at_risk: pooled funds held by the NFT pool
exploit_path: buyNFT takes collectionAddress_ as a parameter although each pool is bound to one collection, so a caller can have pooled funds buy an NFT from a collection they control at a self-set price.
preconditions: attacker can list an NFT from an arbitrary collection and call buyNFT

title: NoyaValueOracle.getValue returns an incorrect price when a multi-token route is used
value_at_risk: collateral valuations that depend on the oracle
exploit_path: multi-hop valuation reuses the original asset instead of the running quoting token, so the returned price is wrong; a user who spots the mispricing can borrow or withdraw against misvalued collateral.
preconditions: a multi-token route must be configured for the asset

title: Signature Replay Attack Possible Between Stake, Unstake and Reward Functions Enabling Unauthorized Token Claims
exploit_path: stake, unstake and reward verify the same keccak256(abi.encodePacked(userWallet, rewardAmount, orderId)) digest, so a signature issued for one action can be replayed in another to claim rewards or unstake without authorization.
preconditions: attacker needs one valid signature from any user for any of the three actions

title: [H-01] BETH#spendCoin - Complete loss of BETH when spendCoin() is called more than once
value_at_risk: BETH backing held by the contract
exploit_path: spendCoin reads the recipient from coinOwner[coin], which is only ever written for the root coin, so calling spendCoin more than once pays out repeatedly and drains the BETH backing.
preconditions: attacker holds a coin whose owner mapping is unset/root

title: Underconstrained circuit in length proofs for transaction
value_at_risk: soundness of transaction-trie length proofs and the bridge funds they gate
exploit_path: the transaction length circuit is underconstrained, so a prover can satisfy it for a transaction index/count that is not in the trie; the forged proof is accepted by the verifier that gates withdrawals.

title: BoxNFT.sol - Exploitable random rarity with gas limit
value_at_risk: the value of rare NFTs minted from the box
exploit_path: rarity is derived from a value the minter can influence (gas limit and block data), so the attacker mints only boxes that roll a rare outcome.
preconditions: mint remains open and rarity depends on execution context

title: Invalid Comparisons on Fixed-Point Values are Accepted by the Circuit Verifier
value_at_risk: assets shielded in the Penumbra shielded pool
exploit_path: enforce_cmp() accepts many invalid fixed-point input pairs, so the in-circuit check that a spend does not extract more than the source holds is ineffective; a malicious spender can prove an invalid spend and withdraw more assets than they own.
preconditions: attacker must be able to submit a spend proof to the Penumbra chain

title: Missing slippage protection
value_at_risk: Output of the protocol fee-converter swap (bounded by fee size)
exploit_path: swapExactTokensForTokens is called with amountOutMin=1, so a searcher can sandwich the fee-converter swap and capture the price impact.
preconditions: IoTex has no private mempool; converter swap routes through a public AMM.

title: Incorrect initialization causes VADER emission rate of 1 second instead of 1 day in Vader.sol
value_at_risk: VADER emission schedule and USDV peg
exploit_path: secondsPerEra is initialized to 1 instead of 86400, so emissions accrue 86400x too fast; a staker farms the inflated VADER and sells before the peg collapses.
preconditions: Deployment retains the test parameter and the VADER pool has exit liquidity.

title: Sandwich attack to accruePremiumAndEx- pireProtections()
exploit_path: Buy shares just before accruePremiumAndExpireProtections() raises totalSTokenUnderlying, then redeem after the exchange rate steps up; the premium is diluted from existing holders.
preconditions: Attacker can enter and exit around the permissionless accrual call.

title: Call and Vault implementations can be arbitrarily changed by anyone.
value_at_risk: All assets held by Hook Call and Vault proxies
exploit_path: initializeBeacon is public with no initializer guard, so anyone can re-point the beacon to a malicious implementation that returns attacker-controlled Call/Vault logic and drains proxy funds.
preconditions: Hook beacon proxy deployed without a one-shot initializer; attacker pays gas only.

title: Decimals are not accounted for in calculation of main_token_amount
exploit_path: buy_amount * invitation_price is computed without normalizing token decimals, so a buyer pays less main_token than the intended price when decimals differ.
preconditions: Tokens with differing decimals; purchase path live.

title: One operator key is installed on every chain, so each deployment signs the same one-time leaf
entry_point: one-time leaf claim / operator signature check
value_at_risk: Rewards or claims gated by the one-time leaf
exploit_path: The same operator key signs the same one-time leaf on every chain deployment, so a leaf/signature observed on one chain can be replayed on another to claim twice.
preconditions: Multiple chain deployments share the operator key and the signature lacks chain-id domain separation.

title: Allowing extra upper bits for indexes allows invalid proofs to pass in BeaconStateVerifier
value_at_risk: RocketPool beacon-state proofs used for validator/withdrawal accounting
exploit_path: _validatorIndex is uint256 but only 40 bits are meaningful; upper bits overwrite the gIndex prefix, letting an attacker substitute a different BeaconState field so an invalid proof verifies.
preconditions: Verifier reachable with attacker-supplied index and proof.

title: Incorrect handling of point doubling can allow signature forgery
entry_point: signature verification in Telepathy light client
value_at_risk: Bridge messages and funds secured by the light client
exploit_path: Point doubling is handled incorrectly, so a crafted signature verifies for an arbitrary message; the attacker submits a forged light-client update and executes a cross-chain message.
preconditions: Attacker can submit updates to the Telepathy light client; body withheld.

title: Missing group validation for the input points of Groth16 circuit
exploit_path: G1/G2 input points are not checked for prime-order subgroup membership, so invalid points pass pairing and a forged Groth16 proof is accepted.
preconditions: Attacker can submit proofs to the verifier; the compressed path also lacks the check.

title: Improper Implementation of Slippage Tolerance
value_at_risk: SOL paid per token purchase (user slippage)
exploit_path: buy caps the amount at real_token_reserves but only checks max_sol_cost, so a front-run that drains reserves changes the per-token price and the buyer overpays.
preconditions: Public mempool on Solana; bonding curve with thin reserves.

title: Incorrect Loan Amount
exploit_path: denormalize divides by cumulative_rate then truncates to u64, so a small normalized loan rounds to zero debt while USH is still minted - a free mint without liability.
preconditions: Collateral with non-zero interest rate; repeatable small loans.

title: Missing Subgroup and Identity Checks for Ed25519 Public Keys
entry_point: Ed25519 signature verification in relay contracts
exploit_path: Ed25519 public keys are accepted without subgroup or identity checks, enabling small-order/rogue-key signatures that verify for attacker-chosen messages.
preconditions: Attacker can register or supply a public key to the verifier.

exploit_path: Register does not check LibP2PKey ownership and overwrites existing entries, so anyone can set themselves as Owner of another operator's key and redirect its rewards.

title: Redemption functions do not honor the minimal output values that users provide

title: Randomness can be manipulated

title: Cross contract reentrancy during ElixirStrategy.withdraw() swaps allows an attacker to double account collateral
entry_point: ElixirStrategy.withdraw -> _swapExactInputMultihop with attacker-controlled path -> malicious token callback -> HoldingManager.deposit

exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates a holding and invests in ElixirStrategy. 2) After cooldown, calls claimInvestment with a swap path that routes through a pool for an attacker-created token. 3) During the swap, the malicious token's _update callback calls HoldingManager.deposit(USDT, amount), adding collateral to the same holding. 4) ElixirStrategy computes withdrawnAmount as IERC20(tokenIn).balanceOf(recipient) - balanceBefore, so the mid-swap deposit is counted as swap yield. 5) The holding's collateral is credited twice; attacker borrows/mints jUSD against it. 6) The report notes the msg.sender == tx.origin check is obsolete under EIP-7702, so holding creation can be reached from a contract.
preconditions: Attacker can create a holding (whitelisted contract; bypassable via EIP-7702 per the report); a Uniswap V3 pool for an attacker token; cooldown period

title: _checkAndLockForSuperPosition does not lock assets in the vaultBank
