title: PLP transfer or balance updates do not update reward index
entry_point: PLP ERC20 transfer / partial withdrawLiquidity, then claimRewards -> _getPendingRewards
value_at_risk: Reward tokens owed to other PLP holders (reward index under-accrual is socialised across LPs)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker holds a small PLP position whose usrRwdIndexQ128 was last synced at time T0. 2) Rewards accrue in rewardsPerLPQ128 while the attacker holds little or nothing. 3) Attacker acquires a large PLP balance by transfer from a second wallet; the transfer does not update usrRwdIndexQ128. 4) Attacker calls claim; _getPendingRewards computes lpBalance * (rewardsPerLPQ128 - staleIndex), paying rewards on the full new balance for the whole accrual window. 5) Repeat with fresh wallets. Over-claim dilutes the reward pool of honest LPs. (A partial withdraw also leaves the index stale, but that under-pays the withdrawer rather than over-paying, so it is not the attack.)
preconditions: PLP is freely transferable and the reward index is only written on first deposit, full exit and claim; attacker needs a second wallet holding PLP acquired before the claim

title: Lack of Access Control
value_at_risk: The vault's trading account: positions and collateral
exploit_path: 1) The vault module exposes a public function returning a reference to the trading Account associated with a Vault. 2) If the mutable variant account_mut is equally public, any caller can borrow &mut Account and call the Dof/account entry points to change trade positions or withdraw collateral. 3) The attacker routes the account's assets to themselves. 4) The report's remediation (change the modifier to public(package)) implies the function is currently public.
preconditions: account_mut must be public (the body explicitly names it but only shows account); attacker can pass the Vault object

title: Approvals can be exploited due to insufficient checks in _exitPositionAndRemoveCollateral
value_at_risk: A victim's oTAP/liquidity ERC721 and the unlocked liquidity proceeds
exploit_path: 1) Victim has at some point approved Magnetar for their oTAP position (common for Magnetar users). 2) Attacker calls _exitPositionAndRemoveCollateral with exitData.exit=false and unlockData.unlock=true, setting tokenId to the victim's. 3) Because exit is skipped, tOLPId stays 0 and the mismatch check is bypassed; there is no ownerOf check on unlockData.tokenId. 4) unlock(tOLPId, singularity, user=attacker) burns the victim's token (Magnetar is approved) and sends the proceeds to the attacker.
preconditions: Victim has a live ERC721 approval to Magnetar; attacker knows the tokenId

title: Unvalidated Fallback Enables Proﬁt Theft
value_at_risk: Intermediate route tokens temporarily held by the router during an in-flight swap
exploit_path: 1) A legitimate swap is in progress; the router holds intermediate route tokens and has entered LOAN_CALLBACK_TYPE_ONGOING. 2) Attacker calls the router fallback with calldata that the fallback interprets as a transfer to msg.sender. 3) The fallback does not validate that msg.sender is the expected pool, so it pays out the intermediate tokens. 4) Attacker completes the arbitrage independently and returns just enough for the router's own flow to finish with zero profit. 5) Attacker keeps the MEV.
preconditions: A swap/loan callback is in flight and the router holds tokens; attacker can call the fallback in that window (same block, ordering)

title: TradableStaking: rewards accounting is corrupted
value_at_risk: Reward pool owed to other stakers
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes after rewards have already accrued (cumulativeRewardPerTokenStored > 0). 2) previousRewardPerToken[attacker] is never initialised, so it reads 0. 3) On first claim, the reward is computed as balance * (cumulative - 0), as if the attacker had been staked since the contract launched. 4) Attacker receives far more than their share; the reward pool is diluted. 5) Repeat with new addresses.
preconditions: Rewards have accrued before the attacker's first stake; reward pool is finite

title: Approvals can be exploited due to insufficient checks in `_exitPositionAndRemoveCollateral`
value_at_risk: Victim's oTAP ERC721 and the unlocked liquidity proceeds
exploit_path: Same mechanism as CID 332: exit=false, unlock=true, unlockData.tokenId = victim tokenId. The skipped exit leaves tOLPId = 0, the mismatch check is bypassed, and unlock() burns the victim's approved token and sends the proceeds to the attacker. The github body adds the explicit ownerOf check that is missing.
preconditions: Victim has approved Magnetar for the oTAP token; attacker knows the tokenId

title: _deductRoyalty1155 leaves part of the royalties in the contract, allowing others to withdraw them
entry_point: NFTX _deductRoyalty1155 underpay, then a residue-sweep flow such as _allWethToETHResidue
value_at_risk: WETH royalties stranded in the NFTX market contract
exploit_path: 1) A sale of `amounts[i]` ERC1155 units computes netRoyaltyAmount = royaltyAmount * amounts[i] but transfers only royaltyAmount to the royalty receiver. 2) The difference, royaltyAmount * (amounts[i] - 1), remains as WETH in the contract. 3) Any caller triggers the residue-conversion flow (_allWethToETHResidue) that converts the contract's WETH balance to ETH and sends it to the caller. 4) Attacker repeats after each sale.
preconditions: ERC1155 sales with amount > 1 and a nonzero royalty; a permissionless residue-sweep function exists

title: User can inflate number of rewards by staking additional amount of rewards right before claiming them
entry_point: StakingManager.stake then claim (rewardIntegralFor not updated on stake/withdraw)
value_at_risk: Reward tokens owed to other stakers
exploit_path: 1) Alice stakes 1000 USDC at the start of a reward period. 2) Halfway through, she stakes another 1000 USDC. 3) rewardIntegralFor is not updated on stake, so her claim is computed on the new 2000 balance for the whole period. 4) She claims and receives roughly double the rewards she earned; the reward pool is diluted. 5) Repeat with fresh addresses each period.
preconditions: Reward period in progress; reward pool funded; stake/withdraw do not checkpoint

title: Premature Access To Unsettled PnL During USDC Withdrawals
entry_point: Bullet handle_withdraw_msg(USDC) -> UsdcLedger::apply_balance_update deducts unsettled_perp_profit first
value_at_risk: The USDC PnL pool / other users' funds backing unsettled profits
exploit_path: 1) Attacker opens a perp position and accumulates unsettled_perp_profit (paper profit). 2) Attacker holds a nominal spot USDC balance. 3) Calls withdraw for the profit amount. 4) apply_balance_update deducts the withdrawal from unsettled_perp_profit before touching real assets, and the transfer pays out USDC. 5) The profit was never settled against the PnL pool, so the attacker exits before the pool can net it; if the position later loses, the loss is unbacked. 6) Repeat.
preconditions: Attacker has unsettled USDC perp profit and a nominal spot balance; withdrawal path does not require settlement

title: Minting rate uses manipulable Honey–BNB price allowing reward inflation via flashloans
entry_point: Grizzly.fi reward minting rate -> Honey-BNB DEX pair price; deposit/withdraw/changeStrategy
value_at_risk: Reward token supply / pool value (dilution of existing holders)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker flash-loans and swaps to move the Honey-BNB pair price just before calling deposit/withdraw/changeStrategy. 2) The minting rate is derived from the manipulated spot price, so the call mints disproportionately high rewards. 3) Attacker unwinds the swap and claims/sells the inflated rewards. 4) Repeat while the pool is funded.
preconditions: Minting rate reads a DEX pair spot price; flash loan; the reward pool pays out at the inflated rate

title: _deductRoyalty1155 will leave part of the royalties in the contract and it can be taken out by other users
value_at_risk: WETH royalty residue in the NFTX marketplace contract
exploit_path: Same as CID 472: royaltyAmount * amount is deducted from the seller but only royaltyAmount is paid to the receiver; the remainder stays as WETH. A later sale triggers the residue flow, which converts all WETH to ETH and sends it to the caller. The attacker times a sale and sweeps the accumulated residue.
preconditions: ERC1155 sale with amount > 1; permissionless residue sweep

title: Premature Access To Unsettled PnL During USDC Withdrawals
exploit_path: Same as CID 822: USDC withdrawals deduct from unsettled_perp_profit before settled spot balance, so a user can withdraw paper perp profit before the PnL pool settles it. The HF excerpt adds the exact helper call (process_balance_update_for_user_helper -> UsdcLedger::apply_balance_update).
preconditions: Unsettled USDC perp profit + nominal spot USDC

title: No price impact might lead to loss of funds
entry_point: Strat order.move order placement/fill at oracle price with no price impact
value_at_risk: Liquidity providers / the vault on the opposite side of the trade
exploit_path: 1) Attacker observes an oracle update that will move the price in their favour (oracle latency / public mempool). 2) Opens a large position at the stale oracle price with no price impact. 3) The oracle updates; the position is immediately in profit. 4) Closes and takes the profit from the LP/vault side. 5) Repeats on each oracle update, or uses a one-way whale bet to drain LPs.
preconditions: Oracle updates are predictable/observable; no price-impact function; position size within open-interest caps; funding fee capped/delayed

title: Pending payouts excluded from total balance cause incorrect share calculations
value_at_risk: Other stakers' principal in the Coinflip Staking pool
exploit_path: 1) Attacker is the winner of a game and controls the payout recipient; the recipient is a contract that rejects the token, so transferPayout's low-level call fails and the amount is booked to pendingPayouts[token][recipient]. 2) The Staking contract still counts the full token balance in totalOwed/lockLiquidity/finalizeUnstake. 3) Attacker (also a staker) unstakes at the inflated share price and receives more than their share. 4) Attacker later claims the pending payout too, or leaves the pool short. 5) Remaining stakers/new depositors absorb the deficit.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to make the winner payout fail (contract recipient that reverts on the token) and hold staking shares; game must complete

title: `borrow()` should decrease `totalAssets` value
value_at_risk: Other OmoVault depositors' assets (share price overstated by borrowed assets counted twice)
exploit_path: 1) The agent calls borrow(), which transfers assets out but does not decrement _totalAssets. 2) totalAssets() therefore counts the same assets both in the vault/UniV3 position accounting and in the agent's borrowed position. 3) Share price is inflated. 4) A holder redeems immediately after a borrow and receives more assets than their fair share. 5) Remaining holders are diluted. The attacker cannot trigger the borrow (onlyAgent), but can time redemption around legitimate agent borrows.
preconditions: An agent borrow has occurred and the attacker holds vault shares; borrow is onlyAgent so the attacker cannot initiate it

title: Swap Reentrancy Lock Is Ineffective
entry_point: GnoSwap pool Swap -> swapCallback -> re-enter Swap / IncreaseLiquidity
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls Swap with a callback contract. 2) Slot0 returns a copy, so SetUnlocked(false) mutates only the local copy and the stored unlocked flag stays true. 3) During swapCallback the attacker re-enters Swap or calls IncreaseLiquidity. 4) The post-callback balance check (safeSwapCallback) is evaluated against balances the attacker has manipulated, so the repayment check can be satisfied with the pool's own funds. 5) Attacker exits with more than they put in. The report states the repayment check can be bypassed but does not give the exact profit equation.
preconditions: Pool with a swap callback; attacker contract as recipient; no other global lock

title: claimReceipts() market Parameter is Unchecked
entry_point: Tracer Account.claimReceipts(market, ...) with receipt.tracer not validated against market
value_at_risk: Legitimate tracer markets' funds and insurance pools
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates or controls a malicious tracer market. 2) Attacker obtains receipts whose receipt.tracer points at the malicious market but submits them to claimReceipts for a legitimate market. 3) The function does not check that the market parameter matches receipt.tracer, so the claim is priced/withdrawn against the legitimate market's funds or insurance pool. 4) Attacker withdraws more than the malicious market could back.
preconditions: Attacker can create a tracer market and mint receipts; claimReceipts is permissionless; a legitimate market shares the accounting

title: Router/Gateway - Reentrancy in inbound/outbound transfer allows arbitrary creation of L2 tokens
value_at_risk: Unbacked L2 tokens minted against an under-escrowed L1 deposit
exploit_path: 1) Attacker bridges a callback token (ERC777 or a custom token with a transfer hook) through the L1 gateway. 2) outboundEscrowTransfer reads prevBalance, calls safeTransferFrom, and reads postBalance. 3) During transferFrom the token calls back into the attacker, who re-enters outboundTransfer and escrows again. 4) The inner call mints an L2 credit for 50; the outer call then sees postBalance 100 and mints another 100, so 150 L2 tokens are created for 100 escrowed. 5) Attacker sells the extra L2 tokens.
preconditions: A registered callback token on the bridge; attacker holds some of it; L1 gateway path (L2 custom gateway variant needs an L2 callback token)

title: Platform Fee Inclusion in Pool Accounting Creates Inconsistent Fund Tracking
entry_point: Blockstreet contribute_usd1 -> finalize/refund pro-rata (gross recorded, net transferred)
value_at_risk: Pool vault's USD1; over-refund funded by other contributors / the project
exploit_path: 1) Attacker contributes X USD1; only X - fee is transferred to the vault, but pool.usd1_raised and contribution.usd1_amount record X. 2) At finalization/refund, the pro-rata calculation uses the inflated total and the inflated individual amount. 3) The attacker's refund (or token allocation) is computed on X while the vault only holds X - fee. 4) The PoC shows total inflated refunds exceeding the vault balance. 5) The attacker withdraws more than they contributed; other contributors/project absorb the shortfall.
preconditions: Pool ends oversubscribed or cancelled; attacker contributes before the cap; platform fee > 0

title: [C-01] Decreasing position size via leverage update can be abused to steal from diamond
entry_point: GainsNetwork decrease position size via leverage update -> handleTradePnl (negative available collateral)
value_at_risk: The diamond's vault balance; the closing fee is paid to the trader instead of the diamond
exploit_path: 1) Trader opens a position. 2) Calls updateLeverage/decrease position size; partial PnL is realized and closing fees computed. 3) If available collateral in the diamond is negative, handleTradePnl sends the closing fee from the vault to the trader rather than to the diamond. 4) The trader is overpaid by the fee each time. 5) Repeat with small decreases to accumulate.
preconditions: Position with a size decrease; diamond collateral negative at the moment of the call (or the branch can be forced)

title: Any referrer can steal others scores
value_at_risk: Victim's referral score / the rewards it entitles the referrer to
exploit_path: 1) Victim has a BunniToken balance with referrer A recorded in the packed balance slot. 2) Attacker deposits 1-2 wei with recipient = victim and referrer = attacker. 3) _mint overwrites the victim's referrer field with the attacker's id. 4) Future referral score accrues to the attacker; the victim's referrer loses it. 5) Attacker repeats for many victims. The PoC shows scoreOf(referrerA) 1e18 -> 0 and scoreOf(referrerB) -> 2e18 for a cost of 2 wei token0 + 10 wei token1.
preconditions: BunniToken uses ERC20Referrer packed balances; attacker can deposit dust to any recipient; referral score maps to a reward

title: Promo claim race condition allows double payment
entry_point: Telegram promo claim handler -> BullMQ job -> transferUsdc
value_at_risk: Promo USDC budget (double payment to one user)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker triggers duplicate Telegram webhook deliveries for the same promo button press (retry / replay). 2) Both handler invocations read status = 'pending' and each enqueues a job with a random BullMQ jobId. 3) Both workers call transferUsdc before claimPromo's WHERE status='pending' guard runs. 4) The second on-chain transfer succeeds even though the DB write is rejected. 5) Attacker receives 2x the promo amount.
preconditions: Attacker can cause duplicate webhook delivery; promo budget funded; no idempotency key

title: Inconsistent Accounting
entry_point: GMX position decrease -> pendingImpactUsd recalculation -> liquidation check
exploit_path: 1) Attacker opens a position with pendingImpactAmount/pendingImpactUsd. 2) The index price changes; on a partial decrease, proportionalPendingImpactUsd is recomputed as proportionalPendingImpactAmount * currentPrice instead of prorating the stored USD value. 3) pendingImpactUsd can exceed its initial value or go negative while pendingImpactAmount stays positive. 4) The liquidation check consumes the corrupted value and may classify a healthy position as liquidatable. 5) A keeper/liquidator closes it and collects the bonus.
preconditions: Position with pending price impact; index price move between increase and decrease; attacker can act as liquidator

title: Double-spend attack in CREDIT mode through collateral-withdrawal race
value_at_risk: Card settlement funds (the operator cannot recover the purchase amount)
exploit_path: 1) User supplies collateral and requests a collateral withdrawal; the operator approves it. 2) User makes a card purchase. 3) Before the operator processes the authorized borrowing, the user calls executeApprovedServiceAction to withdraw the collateral. 4) The operator's borrow fails and cannot settle the card payment. 5) User calls requestWithdrawal; in CREDIT mode, with the token no longer collateral, it executes instantly without operator approval. 6) User keeps the goods and the collateral.
preconditions: Operator has approved the withdrawal but not yet processed it; card payment authorized; backend does not check pending withdrawals

title: Malicious users can transact NFTs with zero deltas, causing a loss of profit for pool owners
entry_point: Stargaze infinity-swap SwapNftsForTokens / SwapTokensForAnyNfts with a failing second swap
value_at_risk: Pool owners' inventory/profit; the attacker acquires or sells NFTs without updating the pool delta
exploit_path: 1) Attacker submits SwapNftsForTokens (or SwapTokensForAnyNfts) crafted so the second swap fails. 2) The break statement skips self.pools_to_save, so the reused pool is not persisted and its spot price/deltas are not updated. 3) The NFT/token leg that already executed stands, so the attacker has bought or sold at the old price. 4) Attacker repeats, each time avoiding the price impact. 5) The loss accrues to pool owners.
preconditions: Reused pool; ability to make the second swap fail (e.g. slippage/insufficient liquidity); CosmWasm message flow

title: Missing oracle staleness validation before using price data in Solana programs
entry_point: maxbtc-solana custody_aum -> doves_oracle.price/expo (no timestamp check) -> liquidity ops
value_at_risk: Pool AUM pricing / minimum output calculations; LPs on the other side
exploit_path: 1) Oracle price goes stale during volatility. 2) Attacker calls a liquidity operation that uses custody_aum or the price without a freshness check. 3) The operation is priced at the stale value, so the attacker deposits/withdraws/trades at a favourable rate. 4) The difference is borne by the pool. The report says the client claims Jupiter Perpetuals already checks staleness, which is not independently verifiable.
preconditions: Stale oracle feed (no timestamp validation in the program); attacker can act before the next update; pool has liquidity

title: User-Controlled swapCallData in swapTo Function
value_at_risk: Tokens held/approved by the Kelp Delta vault to the aggregator
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls swapTo with exchangeAddress = attacker contract and swapCallData = transferFrom(vault, attacker, amount) (or an equivalent pull). 2) The function executes a low-level call to exchangeAddress with caller-controlled calldata. 3) If the vault has approved the aggregator (or the aggregator holds tokens), the call moves them to the attacker. 4) The report warns that a malicious exchangeAddress can cause unauthorized transfers.
preconditions: exchangeAddress is caller-controlled and not whitelisted; the aggregator/vault has a live token balance or allowance

title: Large oracle confidence can incorrectly trigger liquidations
entry_point: Templar liquidation check with Pyth price ± confidence
value_at_risk: Liquidation bonuses from positions that are healthy at true price
exploit_path: 1) During a volatility spike, Pyth confidence widens. 2) Collateral is valued at price - confidence and debt at price + confidence, so a healthy position appears liquidatable. 3) A keeper can liquidate it and collect the bonus. 4) The opportunity is created by the oracle, not by the attacker; there is no action the attacker can take to force the confidence widening.
preconditions: Pyth confidence/price ratio spikes (external market event); attacker is a keeper/liquidator

title: REENTRANCY
entry_point: Livecore.claimBetToken(uint256 betId) -> AzuroBet.mint() ERC1155 receiver hook
value_at_risk: Azuro LP liquidity that backs resolved AzuroBet payouts
exploit_path: 1) Hold a winning bet on a resolved condition. 2) Call claimBetToken(betId); azuroBet.mint() calls the ERC1155 receiver before delete bets[betId]. 3) Re-enter claimBetToken for the same betId from the hook; each pass mints another full-size winning AzuroBet token. 4) Redeem every minted token for payout against the LP.
preconditions: attacker holds a resolved winning bet; can receive ERC1155 (contract wallet)

title: An attacker can force 0 shares to be minted for a liquidity provider
value_at_risk: the victim LP's deposit (minted as 0 shares and absorbed by the pool)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker already holds LP shares. 2) Front-run a victim addLiquidity with a max-size short so shareReserves z becomes 0. 3) Victim call hits _updateLiquidity with z=0, the scaling block is skipped and lpShares computes to 0; _mint accepts 0. 4) Victim capital stays in the pool and accrues to existing LP shares; attacker withdraws.
preconditions: no outstanding longs; attacker capital for the max short; mempool visibility

title: The Hypervisor.deposit function does not check the msg.sender
entry_point: Hypervisor.deposit(...) with attacker-chosen from and to (no msg.sender check)
value_at_risk: ERC20 balances of any user holding a standing allowance to the Hypervisor
exploit_path: 1) Find a user with a live ERC20 allowance to Hypervisor (approvals persist after their deposit). 2) Call deposit(amount, from=victim, to=attacker). 3) The contract pulls the victim tokens and mints LP shares to the attacker. 4) Redeem shares immediately.
preconditions: victim allowance to Hypervisor; vulnerable implementation (deposit unrestricted)

title: Early self liquidations receive a portion of future fees to be paid by other creditors
attacker: external unprivileged EOA (creditor of a distressed debt position)
value_at_risk: future repay fees owed to other creditors of the same debt position
exploit_path: 1) Hold a credit position in a distressed debt. 2) Self-liquidate first; assignedCollateral uses the debt position total collateral and ignores the repay fees that later creditors will pay. 3) The attacker takes a pro-rata claim on collateral that includes those unpaid fees, leaving later creditors short.
preconditions: distressed debt position; attacker is a creditor

title: Inﬁnite withdrawals using function withdrawAllWithRedirect(uint256
value_at_risk: all balances of a stream token held by the LlamaPayV2Payer contract, including other payers' streams
exploit_path: 1) Be the payee of any stream (a self-created stream suffices). 2) Call withdrawAllWithRedirect(id); the function pays redeemables[_id] but never zeroes it. 3) Call it again (same or later block); redeemables is still positive, so it pays again. 4) Repeat until the contract balance of that token is zero.
preconditions: attacker is payee of >=1 stream; contract holds other streams in the same token

title: Flat keeper reward can be used to bankrupt an attacker-controlled user and steal quote
entry_point: Drift trigger_order / fill_spot_order flat keeper fee path
value_at_risk: Drift insurance fund and socialized bad debt; report estimates ~$250k/day
exploit_path: 1) Open maker and filler accounts; maker deposits ~33c USDC. 2) Maker opens 32 reduce_only TriggerLimit buy orders (position-increasing but flagged reduce-only, so no margin check). 3) Filler triggers all 32 and collects 32c of flat keeper fees from the maker. 4) Filler calls fill_spot_order on each; the program cancels the invalid reduce-only orders and pays another 32c. 5) Maker is now ~31c insolvent; resolve bankruptcy so the loss is socialized/covered by the insurance fund. 6) Repeat with the same account, parallelize.
preconditions: permissionless cranking; bad-debt socialization or insurance fund; ~$0.33 capital per iteration

title: Cross-contract signature replay allows users to inflate rewards
value_at_risk: staking reward pool of the three NFTStaking contracts
exploit_path: 1) Own the same tokenId in two collections (e.g. Worlds legendary weight 100, Grayboys common weight 1). 2) Get a valid signature for the legendary staking and use it legitimately. 3) Replay the same signature on the Grayboys contract: the hash omits address(this), so the common NFT is staked with the legendary multiplier. 4) Claim inflated rewards.
preconditions: same tokenId in two collections; one valid signature

title: OmoOracle `getLiquidityAmounts()` uses spot price making it manipulatable
exploit_path: 1) Flash-borrow and move the Uniswap V3 pool sqrtPriceX96. 2) getLiquidityAmounts values the position at the manipulated spot price. 3) Borrow against the inflated position value or liquidate an under-valued one. 4) Restore the price and repay the flash loan.
preconditions: flash-loan capital; pool deep enough to move within one tx

title: Stale share price usage leading to fund loss and unfair distribution
exploit_path: 1) Wait until the share price is stale relative to accrued Lido/sDAI yield. 2) Deposit at the stale price to mint too many nETH/nUSD shares. 3) Withdraw after the price is refreshed, capturing the difference from other holders.
preconditions: stale share price window; cross-chain message latency

project: Oku's New Order Types Contract Contest
title: Lack of nonReentrant modifier in fillOrder() and modifyOrder() allows attacker to steal funds
value_at_risk: WETH/token balances backing other users' pending OracleLess orders
exploit_path: 1) Place orders A1/A2 with recipient = attacker contract. 2) Call fillOrder(A1) with malicious txData; execute() calls the attacker contract. 3) Re-enter: pull tokenIn of A1, return 1 wei tokenOut, call modifyOrder(A1) down to the minimum (crediting M WETH), then modifyOrder(A2) up to park the WETH so the contract balance check passes. 4) Withdraw the credited WETH.
preconditions: attacker orders in range; OracleLess holds other pending orders

title: Auto-compound strategy can have its rewards stolen
attacker: external unprivileged EOA holding any valid Merkl claim
exploit_path: 1) Obtain any valid Merkl claim (it only needs to exist in the root; it may already have been used). 2) Call claimAndSwap with _actions encoding Distributor.claim([autoCompounder],[rewardToken],[amount],[proof],[attacker]) followed by a transfer. 3) Because the strategy registered Swapper as operator, the claim succeeds and the reward is paid to the attacker.
preconditions: attacker has a Merkl claim; strategy has unclaimed rewards

title: Fee Theft via Arbitrary Contract Impersonation in collect() Function in DaosLocker
value_at_risk: Uniswap V3 swap fees accrued to any DaosLive LP position
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a fake contract whose token() returns a real DaosLive token and whose lpTokenId() returns its live tokenId; set owner() to the attacker. 2) Call collect(fakeDao). 3) DaosLocker collects all fees for that tokenId and transfers them to owner() = attacker.
preconditions: know a live DaosLive tokenId; no identity check on the dao argument

title: H-01. A user can steal an already transfered and bridged reSDL lock because of approval
value_at_risk: a reSDL lock NFT that is bridged out and later returns
exploit_path: 1) Obtain an ERC721 approval on a reSDL lock (e.g. as a prior marketplace/operator approval). 2) The owner bridges the lock out; handleOutgoingRESDL deletes amount and ownership but leaves the approval. 3) When the lock returns, the stale approval is still active; transfer the NFT to the attacker.
preconditions: a prior approval exists on the lockId; lock is bridged out and back

title: An attacker can steal debt tokens by using the user's gtID
value_at_risk: victim's GT position and the debt tokens issued against it
exploit_path: 1) Wait for a user to approve their gtId to TermMaxRouter. 2) Front-run and call borrowTokenFromGt with the victim gtId and recipient = attacker, supplying only the XT tokens. 3) Debt tokens are issued to the attacker while the victim position is consumed as collateral.
preconditions: victim gtId approval to the router

title: External Call to Permit2 Allows Stealing Users' Tokens
entry_point: Beefy Zap order execution with stepTarget = Permit2
value_at_risk: all tokens of any user with an outstanding Permit2 signature
exploit_path: 1) Observe a benign user's Permit2 permit/order signature (mempool or public order). 2) Submit an order whose step targets Permit2 and whose calldata replays that signature. 3) The router calls Permit2, which transfers the victim's tokens to the router during the attacker's execution. 4) A later step sweeps them to the attacker.
preconditions: a valid victim Permit2 signature is observable and unspent

title: No Access Control on ReserveFeed Contract
value_at_risk: all collateral and borrow liquidity in Ion Protocol markets
exploit_path: 1) Call setExchangeRate(collateral, arbitrarily high rate) - no access control, no validation. 2) Deposit a minimal amount of that collateral. 3) Borrow the maximum against the inflated rate. 4) Do not repay.
preconditions: none

title: Asset removal triggers excess withdrawals
entry_point: SBTC Bera Vault asset removal -> withdraw
value_at_risk: vault assets attributable to other holders
exploit_path: 1) Trigger or wait for an asset removal. 2) The removal updates accounting so a withdrawal pays out more than the position is worth. 3) Withdraw the excess.
preconditions: asset removal event

title: Negative Price Impact Bypassed For Consistent Proﬁts
value_at_risk: BFP market LP funds paid out as fill-price/skew incentives
exploit_path: 1) Open a 10 USD position. 2) Open a 100k USD position that consumes ~1% of skew, so its fill price deviates and carries an unrealized loss. 3) Merge the large position into the small one; mergeAccounts computes margin only for the `to` account and resets entry price to the oracle, erasing the fill-price loss. 4) Close at oracle price and collect the skew incentive.
preconditions: capital; skewed market; merge hooks enabled

title: spTKN Oracle Can Be Manipulated With Donation
exploit_path: 1) Pick a low-liquidity pod. 2) Donate underlying tokens directly to the pod, inflating the balanceOf-based spTKN price. 3) Use the inflated aspTKN as collateral in FraxPairLend and borrow more than the donation cost. 4) Default.
preconditions: low-liquidity pod; capital for the donation

title: STEALING ETH USING REENTRANCY IN MINTING PASS
value_at_risk: ETH held by the minting contract
exploit_path: 1) Mint a pass; the mint path makes an external call before state is finalized. 2) Re-enter and mint/refund again. 3) Extract ETH.
preconditions: mint live

title: Lack of instantiation authorization in the lease contract allows attackers to instantiate it with arbitrary parameters and hence prevent liquidation and use arbitrary prices
exploit_path: Report says an attacker can instantiate the lease contract with arbitrary parameters, preventing liquidation and using arbitrary prices; the extracted text does not give the exact message sequence.
preconditions: ability to instantiate a lease contract on the chain

title: UniTradeOrderBook.sol: Order maker or executor can drain funds contract - STATUS: FIXED
attacker: external unprivileged EOA (order maker or executor)
value_at_risk: ETH and ERC777 token reserves of the order book
exploit_path: 1) As maker, call updateOrder() which performs an external value transfer before updating totalEthDeposited. 2) Re-enter and withdraw again. 3) Repeat to drain the ETH reserve; the executor fee path is equivalent.

title: `EUSD.mint` function wrong assumption of cases when calculated sharesAmount = 0
value_at_risk: EUSD share accounting; value of existing holders
exploit_path: EUSD.mint calls getSharesByMintedEUSD; if the computed sharesAmount is 0 it assumes a 1:1 share/EUSD ratio and mints _mintAmount shares. exploit_path: 1) Clear the order book so subsequent orders can settle at arbitrary prices. 2) Account A places a limit order priced to create immediate bad debt on settlement. 3) Account B fills A's order; because A has no existing position in that asset, isLiquidatable does not see the new position and A is left with debt while B books unrealized PnL. 4) Account C places an order that closes B; B fills C, converting unrealized PnL into realized profit. 5) Abandon A and C and keep the proceeds in B.
preconditions: Maker has no existing position in the filled asset market; order book can be cleared; attacker controls several margin-funded accounts; no volume cap.

title: ERC-6492 implementation allows draining wallet funds by manipulating ownerIndex
value_at_risk: All native and ERC20 funds in any Coinbase SmartWallet that has granted a spend permission and has the manager as an owner
exploit_path: 1) Obtain an owner-signed SpendPermission (the normal app/spender flow gives this to the spender). 2) Unwrap the SignatureWrapper, set ownerIndex to the wallet's nextOwnerIndex, and rewrap so the ERC-1271 check fails. 3) Build prepareTo = the SmartWallet and prepareData = executeBatch([transfer all native/ERC20 to the attacker, removeOwnerAtIndex(0, owner), addOwnerAddress(owner)]). 4) Wrap the signature in the ERC-6492 magic value and call approveWithSignature. 5) Validation takes the ERC-6492 side-effect path, calls executeBatch with the manager's owner rights, resets ownerIndex, and the second signature check passes. 6) The wallet is drained.
preconditions: The SpendPermissionManager is an owner of the SmartWallet; a valid owner-signed spend permission exists (any granted allowance); attacker controls the spender or has the signed permission.

title: Missing Authorization in `withdraw()` and `redeem()` Allows Theft of Any User's Funds
entry_point: PearVault.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner) and PearVault.redeem(shares, receiver, user); _withdrawWithFee passes user as both caller and owner
value_at_risk: All assets of the vault, i.e. every depositor's shares; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Find a victim with vault shares. 2) Call redeem(victimShares, attacker, victim) or withdraw(assets, attacker, victim). 3) The override checks only balanceOf(user) and _canDirectWithdraw, then _withdrawWithFee calls super._withdraw(user, receiver, user, ...). 4) Because caller == owner in the base call, the ERC-4626 allowance check is skipped; the victim's shares are burned and the assets go to the attacker.
preconditions: Vault is active; direct withdrawals are enabled (_canDirectWithdraw returns true); victim has shares.

title: An adversary can claim any NFT from any user (Project self-injected exploit)
entry_point: SFT418Core._claim(target, id) exposed through a public claim() wrapper
value_at_risk: Any wrapped NFT (ERC-721) held by another user; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Wrap any NFT to obtain eligible chunks (>0). 2) Call claim(victimTokenId). 3) _getEligibleChunks passes, and because _chunkToOwners[id].owner != TOKEN_POOL the else branch transfers the NFT from the victim to the attacker. 4) Unwrap the stolen NFT.
preconditions: Attacker has at least one eligible chunk; victim has a wrapped NFT; claim is externally reachable.

title: Incentive rewards may be stolen
entry_point: VotingReward.getRewardForPeriod(_period, _tokenId, _token) has no check that _period <= current period
value_at_risk: Incentive tokens deposited for future periods; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Watch incentivize() for a pool and note the next period X. 2) Be the first/only voter for that pool in period X. 3) Call getRewardForPeriod(X, tokenId, token) immediately; with no other voters the call pays the whole period's incentives. 4) Repeat each period.
preconditions: Attacker holds a veKitten position and can vote; an incentive has been added for the next period; attacker is first voter.

title: Incorrect price calculation in WBTC Oracle
entry_point: WbtcOracle price calculation: btcUsdPrice * 10**decimals / wbtcBtcPrice (division instead of multiplication)
value_at_risk: WBTC-collateralized lending/stablecoin pools; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deposit WBTC as collateral in a market that consumes WbtcOracle. 2) The oracle divides BTC/USD by WBTC/BTC instead of multiplying, so the reported WBTC/USD price is inflated by the inverse of the WBTC/BTC ratio times the 1e18 scale (with an 18-decimal output and a 1.0e8 WBTC/BTC feed, roughly 1e10x). 3) Borrow the maximum against the inflated collateral and walk away. 4) Alternatively sell the inflated claim to another integration.
preconditions: WbtcOracle is used as the collateral price by a lending/stablecoin market with borrowable liquidity; feed values as described.

title: The contract can be drained of its sonic via reentrancy
entry_point: Eggs.borrowMore has no nonReentrant and calls sendSonic before updating Loans[msg.sender]
value_at_risk: SONIC balance of Eggs; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Open an over-collateralized position. 2) Call borrowMore; during sendSonic, reenter borrowMore. 3) Each reentry borrows again before the loan record is updated; safetyCheck stays non-decreasing because backing and totals offset. 4) Repeat until the contract's SONIC balance is drained; abandon the position.
preconditions: Over-collateralized position; SONIC native transfer with a callback/reentrancy window; contract holds SONIC.

title: Multiple staking_states can be created for the same stake-mint, letting attackers steal rewards and principal
entry_point: IndexTokenStaking stake/unstake/withdraw_stake/claim_rewards; staking_state PDA includes authority, user_staking_account PDA does not
value_at_risk: Reward vaults of every pool sharing the stake mint, plus principal in parallel pools; amount not stated
exploit_path: Reward path: 1) Alice creates pool P0. 2) Bob creates P1 with the same stake mint but Bob as authority. 3) Bob stakes N in P1; the shared user_staking_account records staked_amount = N. 4) Bob calls claim_rewards/withdraw_rewards on P0; P0 sees N staked against its smaller total_staked and overpays Bob. Principal path: 1) unstake in pool A. 2) call withdraw_stake but supply pool B's vault; the instruction never checks that the vault matches the staking_state, so B's vault pays out. 3) Pool A looks closed while B is insolvent.
preconditions: Two pools can share the same stake mint; attacker has stake tokens (recoverable); a victim pool with rewards or principal exists.

title: Native Token is not refunded after Uniswap trade
entry_point: PrintrTrading.buy / PrintrTrading.spend: partial fill on Uniswap leaves unused native in the contract
value_at_risk: Unused native ETH from partial fills; amount per trade not stated
exploit_path: 1) Monitor for a partial fill where the buyer's unused native stays in PrintrTrading. 2) Immediately buy a not-yet-graduated token with msg.value = 0 (or a small amount); the contract's native balance subsidizes the trade. 3) Sell/receive tokens backed by the stuck ETH. 4) Repeat after each partial fill.
preconditions: A prior user trade is partially filled and leaves native in the contract; attacker can trade before the balance is consumed.

title: Attacker Can Exploit Fulfillment Callback to Cancel Request and Steal Tokens from Fulfiller
entry_point: SingleOutputRequestImpl.fulfilRequests -> receiver callback -> cancelRequest before $.fulfilledRequests[requestHash] is written
value_at_risk: The fulfiller's output tokens plus a refund of the attacker's input on the source chain; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Create a SingleOutputRequest whose receiver is an attacker-controlled contract. 2) An RFQ transmitter fulfills the request and transfers the output token to the receiver. 3) The receiver callback calls cancelRequest while fulfilledRequests[requestHash] is still uninitialized, so the cancellation succeeds. 4) The cancellation sends a message to the source chain; _validateAndWithdrawRequest refunds the input token to the request sender (the attacker). 5) The attacker keeps both the output tokens and the refund; the fulfiller loses the output.
preconditions: A fulfiller fills the request; attacker controls the receiver contract; RFQ route enabled.

title: Missing access control for Multicall
value_at_risk: Root bridge tokens transferred to Branch; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a fake contract implementing the VirtualAccount interface. 2) Call anyExecuteSignedDepositMultiple with userAccount = fake contract and funcId 0x02/0x03. 3) The fake account's call() succeeds because the real approval check is bypassed. 4) _approveAndCallOut/_approveMultipleAndCallOut use attacker-controlled params to move tokens from Root to Branch and send/mint to the attacker's receiver.
preconditions: Root has token balance/liquidity; the encoded RLP structures can be crafted; no PoC in the report.

title: LMSR Spot Price Used as Parlay Probability Oracle Enables Sandwich Manipulation
entry_point: GoMarket create_parlay (create_parlay.rs:136) reads lmsr::price_yes; AMM buy_shares/sell_shares mutate q_yes/q_no
value_at_risk: Parlay vault, up to max_payout and the 80% per-parlay exposure cap; PoC shows 267.51 USDC net on a 1 USDC stake
exploit_path: 1) Buy NO shares on each leg's AMM to push price_yes toward the 5% floor. 2) Call create_parlay with those legs; the low probabilities multiply into an inflated payout (two legs at ~6% => ~277x). 3) Sell the NO shares back; LMSR is path-independent, so the round trip costs only ~2x fee. 4) Wait for the expected YES outcome and call settle_leg/claim_parlay to collect the inflated payout.
preconditions: Parlay market open; enough capital to move each AMM's price (depends on b/liquidity); max_payout and exposure caps bound the take.

title: Refund logic allows already fulfilled requests to be reimbursed, allowing double spends and prematurely refunded deposits, resulting in locked liquidity
value_at_risk: Bridge vault liquidity; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Create a request-for-funds that will be fulfilled near its expiry. 2) Ensure the destination-chain fulfillment executes just before expiry. 3) Before the vote-extension pipeline sets rff.Fulfilled, call RefundReq. 4) Receive the deposited funds back while the destination payout is already final. 5) Repeat.
preconditions: Fulfillment lands in the window between destination execution and vote-extension state update; request is near expiry.

title: Insuﬃcient validations allow attackers to steal by increasing refundable fee amount with- out any transfer fees
entry_point: LingoToken transfer_hook / execute; check_is_transferring only verifies the source account's transferring flag
value_at_risk: Accumulated refundable fees in LingoToken/AccountWhitelist; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deploy an exploit program implementing the transfer-execute interface. 2) Create token P with Transfer Fee and Transfer Hook extensions and set the hook to the exploit program. 3) Mint P to accounts A and B. 4) Transfer P from A to B; Token2022 sets A.transferring = true and calls the exploit. 5) The exploit calls Lingo's transfer_hook with source_token A, mint P, destination B, owner Eve, an attacker whitelist account, and amount u64::MAX. 6) check_is_transferring passes because A.transferring is true; the hook adds the fee to refundable_amount. 7) Claim refundable_amount in Lingo tokens.
preconditions: Attacker has a Lingo whitelist account; the hook does not validate the mint or the caller; fees have accumulated.

title: redeemNative() Reentrancy Enables Permanent Fund Freeze, Systemic Misaccounting, and Liquidation Cascades
entry_point: AbstractYieldStrategy.redeemNative -> _redeemShares -> _executeTrade (Uniswap V2) -> malicious token transfer -> ILendingRouter.initiateWithdraw
value_at_risk: Vault yield tokens and collateral; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a malicious ERC20 and UniV2 pools forming yieldToken -> malicious -> asset. 2) Enter a position and approve the malicious token to call initiateWithdraw. 3) Hold native shares without an open position. 4) Call redeemNative with instant redemption and the malicious path. 5) During the swap the malicious token reenters initiateWithdraw; the request manager moves N yield tokens while _burnShares runs on a stale snapshot. 6) s_yieldTokenBalance is reduced twice; health factors drop; liquidate the affected position or exploit the mispriced shares.
preconditions: Malicious token and UniV2 liquidity; instant redemption enabled; attacker has shares; lending router approval.

title: Public trigger enumeration enables rebate theft via overwrite
entry_point: Scheduler execute(Create): trigger_id = hash(condition, msg, contract_address); an existing trigger is deleted and its execution_rebate sent to info.sender
value_at_risk: Execution rebates deposited by trigger creators; PoC example 12,345 RUNE
exploit_path: 1) Query the scheduler's public trigger list. 2) For each trigger with a non-empty execution_rebate, recompute trigger_id from its public fields. 3) Submit Create with identical fields and zero funds. 4) The contract deletes the existing trigger and refunds the stored rebate to the attacker. 5) Automate across all triggers.
preconditions: At least one trigger exists with a rebate; trigger fields are publicly queryable.

title: Duplicate Claim Prevention Logic Is Invalid Assets ClaimManager.sol
entry_point: ClaimManager.fileClaim -> _fileClaimWithMetadata: claimId = claimCount, duplicate check on claim.status, then claimCount++
value_at_risk: Coverage pool up to the policy limit; report example $30M policy with a $1M loss
exploit_path: 1) Hold a policy with coverage limit L. 2) File one legitimate loss claim; it is approved and paid. 3) File the identical loss again; claimCount has incremented, so a new claimId passes the status == None check. 4) Repeat until the coverage limit is exhausted.
preconditions: Attacker is a policyholder with at least one legitimate loss; claims are auto-approved or curator approval is not required at the audited revision.

title: [C-02] Attacker can drain all ETH from IPSeed due to malicious `IIPSeedCurve` implementation
entry_point: IPSeed.spawn(..., IIPSeedCurve priceCurve, ...) -> getBuyPrice/getSellPrice on the caller-supplied curve
value_at_risk: All ETH held by IPSeed; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a malicious IIPSeedCurve that returns 0 from getBuyPrice and an inflated value from getSellPrice. 2) Call spawn with that curve in the token metadata. 3) Buy the new token for ~0 ETH. 4) Sell it back to IPSeed at the inflated price. 5) Repeat until IPSeed's ETH balance is drained.
preconditions: spawn is callable by anyone and accepts an arbitrary curve; IPSeed holds ETH from other tokens.

title: Instant-unstake fees are not reflected in controller staked-redemption settle-
entry_point: Controller.redeem transfers the full collateral_amount, then StakedAsset.instantUnstake returns assetFee and the controller burns only asset_amount - assetFee
value_at_risk: Instant-unstake fee, e.g. 10e18 on a 100e18 redemption; paid by the collateral pool
exploit_path: 1) Stake 100e18 asset and receive 100e18 shares at price 1. 2) Submit a staked redeem order with asset_amount = 100e18 and collateral_amount = 100e18. 3) Controller.redeem pays the full 100e18 collateral. 4) instantUnstake diverts 10e18 to feeRecipient and returns 90e18; the controller burns only 90e18. 5) The attacker keeps the 10e18 fee that should have been charged.
preconditions: instantUnstakeFee > 0; controller holds INSTANT_UNSTAKER_ROLE and has capacity; the signed order is priced on gross staked value (permissive oracle backstop).

title: Malicious tokens can be deployed at deterministic addresses on other chains to steal funds
exploit_path: 1) Predeploy a malicious SuperchainERC20 at the deterministic address on a potential interop chain (the address is CREATE2-derived from the factory, salt and init code). 2) When interop is enabled, the legitimate token's address on that chain is the attacker's contract. 3) relayERC20 calls crosschainMint on that address; the attacker's contract can mint unlimited tokens or redirect bridged funds. 4) Bridge the legitimate token and sell the minted/redirected amount.
preconditions: Token addresses are assumed identical across chains; attacker can deploy at the deterministic address on the destination; a bridge message is sent.

title: _claim function should update userYieldSnapshot
entry_point: Megapool._claim(_holder, _ignoreRewards) pays curr-last but never updates userYieldSnapshot
exploit_path: 1) Stake to get shares and accrue yield. 2) Call claim; the function pays curr - last but leaves userYieldSnapshot unchanged. 3) Call claim again; the same reward is still positive and grows. 4) Repeat until the reward token balance is drained.
preconditions: Attacker has shares and rewards have accrued; claim is callable repeatedly.

title: Attacker can manipulate the protocols AUM
entry_point: Fyde AUM update (off-chain bot writes an absolute AUM) combined with deposit/withdraw
value_at_risk: Other depositors' share of AUM; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Watch the mempool for the bot's AUM update. 2) If the update will lower AUM, withdraw before it lands at the old higher AUM. 3) If it will raise AUM, deposit before it lands. 4) The attacker captures the difference from the remaining depositors.
preconditions: Bot transaction is visible in the mempool; attacker can front-run; AUM change is material.

title: First depositor inflation attack via missing _decimalsOffset() override in
value_at_risk: First victim depositor's assets; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Be the first depositor with 1 wei. 2) Donate assets directly to the vault to inflate totalAssets. 3) The next depositor's shares round down to zero or are heavily diluted; the attacker owns the donated value. 4) Repeat on a fresh vault.
preconditions: Attacker is first depositor; a victim deposits soon after; vault uses virtual shares with offset 0.

title: Malicious actor can steal funds using dex and data arguments in swapFromDexAndBond
value_at_risk: User token approvals outstanding to the Zapper; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Users approve tokens to the Zapper for swaps. 2) The attacker calls swapFromDexAndBond with dex = token contract and data = transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount). 3) The Zapper's low-level call executes the token transfer using the users' approvals. 4) Repeat for all approved users/tokens.
preconditions: Users have outstanding approvals to the Zapper; the function accepts an arbitrary dex and calldata.

title: Oracle returns underlying asset price without accounting for LST exchange rate
entry_point: LST price feed returns the underlying asset price without the LST/underlying exchange rate
value_at_risk: Bold lending market; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Wait for or trigger an LST depeg (market price below underlying). 2) Buy the LST at the discounted market price. 3) Deposit it as collateral; the oracle values it at the underlying price. 4) Borrow Bold against the inflated value and sell it. 5) Default, leaving bad debt.
preconditions: LST trades below underlying; the market uses the flawed feed; borrowable liquidity exists.

title: Missing Access Control for setDestinationSettler
value_at_risk: Filler funds on the destination chain; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Call setDestinationSettler(chainId, maliciousSettler). 2) A filler on the destination chain constructs the fill using the malicious settler and gives it token approvals. 3) The malicious settler pulls the filler's approved tokens. 4) Repeat for each chain/filler.
preconditions: Fillers give approvals to the destination settler; the setter is publicly callable; the attacker can choose/front-run the chain id.

title: Reentrancy in ERC20Delegatable
entry_point: St1inch.deposit -> mint -> ERC20Delegatable._beforeTokenTransfer -> attacker delegation updateBalances -> reentrant deposit
value_at_risk: St1inch token supply/value; report shows ~4.5x mint inflation
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a contract that registers itself as a delegation topic in St1inch. 2) Call deposit(10 1INCH, 365 days); during _beforeTokenTransfer the contract reenters deposit 7+ times. 3) Each deposit mints based on balanceAt - balanceOf, so the attacker receives ~4.5x more St1inch than a single 80 1INCH deposit. 4) Sell or use the inflated St1inch.
preconditions: Attacker can register a delegation; 1INCH deposit; the 200k gas cap still allows enough reentries.

title: Missing Access Control In sendMessage Function
value_at_risk: Vault funds across chains; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Craft an arbitrary cross-chain payload accepted by the receiving vault logic. 2) Call sendMessage directly; there is no trusted-contract check. 3) The destination executes an unauthorized withdrawal/deposit to the attacker. 4) Repeat for each supported chain.
preconditions: Receiver contract trusts messages from the manager without sender validation; manager is deployed and funded.

title: Missing validatePosition After Fee Deduction
entry_point: MultichainOrderRouter.sol:133 fee deduction from position collateral with no validatePosition afterwards
value_at_risk: Position collateral and protocol bad debt; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Open a position with a pending order. 2) Update/cancel the order and set a high feeAmount, paying the Gelato relay fee from the position's collateral. 3) The collateral is removed without a solvency check. 4) Front-run liquidation: withdraw all collateral before the liquidation lands, leaving bad debt.
preconditions: Pending order; position collateral sufficient; relay-fee path enabled.

title: Refund claiming mechanism can be used to steal funds
value_at_risk: Any asset held by the RemoteOrder contract; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Create an order with a low-value rewardAsset and transfer a lot of it to the contract. 2) Let the order become refundable. 3) Call claimRefundV2 specifying a high-value asset; checkIsRefundableWithEscrow fails the hash check, then isClaimable does not compare the refund asset to the original. 4) The contract pays the high-value asset to the attacker.
preconditions: Attacker can create an order; the contract holds high-value assets; refund path is open.

title: Signature clash allows calls to transferReserve to steal NFT
value_at_risk: NFT collateral held by Voyage vaults; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Find a vault holding an NFT collateral. 2) Call transferReserve with _currency = ERC721 contract, _to = attacker, _amount = tokenId. 3) The vault calls transferFrom on the ERC721; the signature matches ERC20 transferFrom. 4) The NFT moves to the attacker without repaying the debt.
preconditions: Vault holds an NFT; transferReserve is callable by the attacker; no NFT/ERC20 type check.

title: Public pullToken function allows to steal ERC20 tokens for
entry_point: PeripheryPayments.pullToken(token, amount, from, recipient) (public, no access control)
value_at_risk: ERC20 tokens for which Voyage has approvals; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Identify tokens for which Voyage has outstanding allowances. 2) Call pullToken(token, amount, victim, attacker). 3) safeTransferFrom pulls the tokens from the victim to the attacker using Voyage's allowance. 4) Repeat.
preconditions: Voyage holds approvals; pullToken is public.

title: Funds can be stolen after wrong approve.
entry_point: Treasury.refund / withdrawFees / distributeWithoutFee: approve(to, amount) before safeTransfer
value_at_risk: Treasury tokens; 2x the intended payout per call
exploit_path: 1) Arrange to be the `to` address of a treasury refund or fee distribution (e.g. as a legitimate fee recipient). 2) Receive X tokens plus an X allowance. 3) As a contract, call safeTransferFrom(treasury, attacker, X) to pull the approved amount again. 4) Net 2X.
preconditions: Attacker is a recipient of treasury funds; the approve is left in place; token is standard ERC20.

title: Reentrancy attack on `Loans.pull` can lead to draining funds
entry_point: Loans.pull(loan, sec, fund) has no reentrancy guard and sets bools[loan].off at the end
value_at_risk: Loans contract balance of the auction token; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Use an ERC777/ERC223 auction token whose transfer calls the recipient. 2) As lender or agent, receive funds in pull; the token callback reenters pull before bools[loan].off = true. 3) Each reentry transfers the loan principal/fee again. 4) Repeat until the token balance is drained.
preconditions: Auction token has a transfer callback; attacker is lender/agent; loan is in the pullable state.

title: Unauthorized pool liquidation threshold modification
value_at_risk: Borrowers' collateral via liquidation; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Call set_liquidation_threshold to a low value for a pool. 2) Borrowers become liquidatable; the attacker liquidates them and collects the liquidation bonus. 3) Alternatively raise the threshold above 100% to protect the attacker's own position.
preconditions: Borrower positions exist; liquidation bonus exceeds gas; the setter is public.

title: Static price calculation allows price manipulation and unfair trading
entry_point: calculate_price (price depends only on circulating supply, not trade size) -> buy/sell
exploit_path: 1) Accumulate tokens across multiple addresses at the static price. 2) Sell a large block at the same price instead of sliding down the curve. 3) The reserve pays out at the inflated price; legitimate holders absorb the loss. 4) Repeat.
preconditions: Token has launched and holds reserve; attacker has capital; no per-trade slippage limit.

title: Unauthorized price oracle configurations
value_at_risk: Lending pool collateral/debt; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Call _set_fixed_price for a pool asset, setting the collateral price arbitrarily high or the debt asset price low. 2) Deposit the asset or borrow against it. 3) Withdraw the borrowed funds and abandon the position. 4) Alternatively trigger liquidations of others.
preconditions: Fixed-price oracle mode is enabled; the setter is public; the pool has liquidity.

title: Multiple unstake() calls at the same position can drain the vault
entry_point: Oro Inti unstake() does not close or zero the position
value_at_risk: Vault Gold tokens; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Stake a position. 2) Call unstake(); the function pays the staked amount plus interest but leaves the position open. 3) Call unstake() again on the same position. 4) Repeat until the vault is drained.
preconditions: Attacker has a staked position; unstake is callable repeatedly.

title: Attackers can arbitrage using the withdraw_all feature
entry_point: UserAccount.withdraw_allocation(..., withdraw_all = true) allows withdraw_supply > deposited_supply
value_at_risk: Protected pool assets; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Deposit 50k USDC (40k PUSD, allocation 37.5k) and 100k USDT (80k PUSD, allocation 85k). 2) Call withdraw_protected_pool with withdraw_all = true; the check allows withdrawing more than deposited. 3) The exchange-rate mismatch lets the attacker withdraw more value than deposited. 4) Repeat or arbitrage across allocations.
preconditions: Pools with differing exchange rates; attacker has deposits; withdraw_all path enabled.

title: Attacker can double its PowerToken balance and voting power through bootstrap()
entry_point: PowerToken._bootstrap() via transfer()/delegate() to self, callable twice before _sync()
value_at_risk: Governance power / treasury control; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) After deployment or a RESET, call transfer()/delegate() to self to enter _bootstrap() twice before _sync(). 2) The attacker's PowerToken balance and voting power double without totalSupply updating. 3) Use the inflated voting power to pass a proposal that moves treasury funds.
preconditions: Post-deploy/RESET window before _sync; attacker can call transfer/delegate.

title: Mishandling of `LoanOffer` struct after signature validation enables stealing lender funds
exploit_path: 1) A lender signs an offer with a non-zero nftCollateralAddress and tokenId plus validators. 2) The attacker submits an OfferExecution with a different _nftCollateralAddress; the code overwrites the signed field before checkValidators. 3) Because nftCollateralTokenId != 0, the validator loop is skipped and the collection check passes against the overwritten address. 4) The attacker borrows against a worthless/different NFT and keeps the principal.
preconditions: A signed lender offer with validators/non-zero tokenId exists; attacker can submit the execution.

title: claim_rewards allows multi-counting the same vault via duplicate remaining accounts
entry_point: claim_rewards iterates ctx.remaining_accounts and sums vault weights without deduplication
exploit_path: 1) Stake via a vault before the snapshot. 2) Call claim_rewards with the same vault PDA repeated in remaining_accounts. 3) Each occurrence adds the vault weight; total_user_weight is inflated up to snapshot.total_global_weight. 4) Claim a disproportionate share of the snapshot rewards.
preconditions: Attacker has a staked vault; snapshot exists; duplicate accounts are allowed by Solana/Anchor.

title: accountingCurveFacet() uses curve's calc_withdraw_one_coin() to price LPs which can be manipulated by attackers
value_at_risk: Vault share price / LP deposits; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Imbalance the Curve pool with a large trade to move spot balances. 2) calc_withdraw_one_coin returns an inflated/deflated LP value. 3) Deposit or withdraw from the MORE vault at the manipulated price. 4) Reverse the Curve trade and keep the difference.
preconditions: Curve pool liquidity; attacker capital; vault uses the facet for accounting.

title: Invalid Asset/Share Conversion via Message Bouncing
entry_point: tsusde-wallet send_timelocked_jettons -> bounceable internal_transfer -> on_bounce refunds `balance` instead of `timelocked_balance`
value_at_risk: tsUSDe vault USDe; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Hold timelocked USDe in the wallet. 2) Trigger send_timelocked_jettons so the internal_transfer bounces. 3) on_bounce adds the amount to `balance` (tsUSDe shares) instead of `timelocked_balance` (USDe). 4) Redeem the newly credited tsUSDe shares for USDe; the vault pays out more than the timelocked amount.
preconditions: Attacker has timelocked USDe; can cause the transfer to bounce; vault has USDe liquidity.

title: Failure to Update Reward State
entry_point: Plume staking stake() does not set userValidatorRewardPerTokenPaid/lastPaidTimestamp; claim does not update global reward state
exploit_path: 1) Stake after rewards have accrued; the contract treats the attacker as staked from the start. 2) Claim unearned rewards for the pre-stake period. 3) Call claim repeatedly for the same elapsed window because the global cumulative state is not updated. 4) Drain emissions.
preconditions: Staking active; rewards accrued; claim callable.

title: Attacker can steal tokens from pods with rebasing tokens by abusing weight handling
entry_point: WeightedIndex.bond() initial-deposit branch keyed on _tokenAmtSupplyRatioX96 == Q96
value_at_risk: Pod tokens / index assets; amount not stated
exploit_path: 1) Wait for a rebasing token to shift the pod's weights so the initial-deposit condition is met again. 2) Bond at the configured weights, receiving more index tokens than the asset value. 3) The excess is borne by existing pod holders.

title: [C-02] Missing asset index check allows any token to mint shares

The router treats the token as USDC and mints shares based on the USDC value, while TVL does not increase. 4. Redeem the shares for real USDC.
preconditions: the router accepts arbitrary tokens; USDC index 0

title: Attacker captures unclaimed fees by timing deposit with range re-entry and price manipulation

preconditions: out-of-range state; accumulated fees; capital

title: Malicious merchant can siphon subscriber funds indefinitely by deleting and recreating a plan with an extended end_ts

The merchant keeps pulling the subscriber's funds.
preconditions: a subscriber; merchant controls the plan

title: Malicious merchant can drain subscriber funds by deleting and recreating a plan with an inflated per-period amount
exploit_path: 1. Merchant creates a plan and a subscriber subscribes to a 1,000/period limit. 2. Repeat.
preconditions: a subscriber; merchant controls the plan

exploit_path: 1) Deposit ~1e-11 ETH as collateral. 2) Call FutureCash.takeCollateral with futureCashAmount=1000 fCash payer tokens and take ~900 USDC. 3) _convertToETHWithHaircut divides by Common.DECIMALS=1e18 instead of the token's 6 decimals, so the 1000 USDC debt is valued at ~2.2e-12 ETH. 4) freeCollateralView sees the account as over-collateralised, so takeCollateral succeeds. 5) Call Escrow.withdraw for the 900 USDC (same mis-scaled check passes). 6) Repeat with G_MAX_TRADE_SIZE until the market's USDC is gone.
preconditions: A USDC-denominated fCash market with liquidity; a dust ETH balance; no special role. Fixed in PR #47, so historical on live deployments only if the fix was not deployed.

title: [C01][Fixed] An attacker can steal all the collateral assets
entry_point: Controller.operate([{actionType: Redeem, asset: maliciousOtoken, amount: max, ...}]) -> _runActions -> _redeem
value_at_risk: All collateral assets held by the Opyn Controller
exploit_path: 1) Deploy a malicious oToken contract that mimics a real oToken (same underlying/collateral, expiry in the past, settlement allowed). 2) Call Controller.operate with a Redeem action whose asset is the fake oToken and amount is the maximum redeemable. 3) _redeem checks only now > expiry and isSettlementAllowed(fakeOtoken); both are controlled by the fake contract. 4) The Controller burns the fake tokens and pays out the real collateral asset from the pool. 5) Repeat to take all collateral.
preconditions: The Controller holds collateral from real oTokens; the attacker can deploy a contract that satisfies the two checks. No role.
