exploit_path: The branch length is taken from user input rather than the fixed index bit-length, so a proof of the wrong length reconstructs a root at an unintended generalized index and a malicious prover can forge message execution.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit a message proof.

title: Liquidity providers can withdraw total fees earned by a pool
entry_point: syncPositionFees (pool liquidity passed instead of position liquidity)
value_at_risk: All fees earned by a pool
exploit_path: Call sites pass the pool's total liquidity, so every LP is credited the entire pool's fee growth and can withdraw far more than its share.
preconditions: None; any LP position.

title: Incorrect Update of _withdraws Mapping in _transfer()
exploit_path: The withdraw proportion is computed as (fromBalance-amount), which zeroes or distorts _withdraws; a user repeatedly transfers 0 and then calls withdrawYieldBalance to drain yield.
preconditions: Attacker needs a small balance in the vault.

title: Unitas swap function is vulnerable to Sandwich Attack at oracle price update
entry_point: Unitas swap at XOracle price update
exploit_path: Token amounts depend solely on the oracle price, so an attacker front-runs the public price update with a swap into the appreciating asset and back-runs it after the update, capturing the price change risk-free.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and visibility of the feeder transaction.

title: Inconsistent Use of Basis Points Leading to Enormous Fees
exploit_path: Fee parameters documented as basis points are used as multipliers, so grace-period and liquidation fees become multiples of the borrowed amount; a liquidator collects the inflated fee.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to trigger liquidation.

title: Issue H-3: Incorrect Spot Price
exploit_path: The custom spot price diverges from Balancer's math, so the vault prices collateral and debt incorrectly; a user can open or close at the mispriced value.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and a vault position.

title: BptPriceStablePool computes stable pool BPT price incorrectly by ignoring token rates
exploit_path: The BPT price ignores per-token rates and uses min(token USD price) * pool.getRate(), so the collateral is mispriced and an attacker can borrow against an inflated value.
preconditions: Pool with rate providers.

title: Early user can break pool via inflation attack due to no minimum liquidity check in the incentive contract
exploit_path: With total_reward < total_shares, deposits can be crafted so reward_inflation rounds to zero; the attacker repeatedly adds shares without increasing rewards and later dilutes other users' rewards.
preconditions: Attacker must be an early depositor with capital.

title: Incorrect Computation Of claimIntervalsPassed
exploit_path: Intervals are computed as block.timestamp - (startTime/interval) instead of (block.timestamp-startTime)/interval, so the claimable interval count is wrong and can be over-claimed.
preconditions: None.

title: ChakraSettlement.receive_cross_chain_msg and ChakraSettlement.receive_cross_chain_callback functions do not ensure that receiving ChakraSettlement contract’s contract_chain_name must match to_chain corresponding to respective txid input though they should
exploit_path: The receiving contract's chain name is not bound to the signed to_chain, so a signature valid on chain A can be replayed on chain B where validator/handler addresses coincide.
preconditions: Addresses must coincide across chains.

title: Users are incorrectly refunded when liquidity is insufficient
exploit_path: The code takes amount_in from the sender and still refunds original_amount - amount_in, so the caller receives an extra refund and can repeat the swap to drain the pool.
preconditions: First pool must have insufficient liquidity.

title: H-15. Incorrect AutoDeleverageFactor.
exploit_path: The ADL factor is inverted, so traders receive full PnL exactly when the market is most leveraged and nothing when ADL begins; a trader can size into that window.
preconditions: Attacker must hold a perp position near the ADL threshold.

title: [H-01] Swapper.sol::Swap - No slippage control on token swap.
exploit_path: No minimum output is enforced, so every swap can be sandwiched and the slippage captured.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and a victim swap.

title: The Protocol Can Be Drained Through Commitment Duplication
entry_point: circomData with empty inputNullifiers (Hinkal transfer circuit)
value_at_risk: All deposits in the Hinkal pool
exploit_path: Crafting circomData so inputNullifiers is empty while the values sit in tokenIds keeps the transfer-circuit dimensions valid, so the proof verifies and commitments are inserted without nullifying the old ones; the attacker withdraws the same deposit repeatedly.
preconditions: Attacker needs one valid deposit and the ability to submit a crafted proof.

title: [H-01] Option premium calculation underprices options
exploit_path: Premiums use the user-supplied period while maturity is rounded up to end of day, so short-dated options are underpriced by up to a day of Black-Scholes value; the buyer captures the difference.
preconditions: Attacker buys short-dated options.

title: [H-03] LFxKyoV3Vault0#withdraw, redeem — Sequential withdraw→redeem inflates payout
exploit_path: Withdrawing WRAPPED burns lWRAPPED and lowers totalSupply, then redeem computes tokenToPay against the reduced supply, so the caller receives more KYO than their fair share.
preconditions: Attacker needs a vault position.

title: Memory alignment malleability
exploit_path: BYTE_C4096 does not wrap after 255, so a memory-alignment value above a byte carries over and an MSTORE8 writes a 1 before the target byte; a prover can exploit the divergence to prove an invalid memory state.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit a proof that triggers the misalignment.

title: Lacking Validation for the Generic Parameter CoinType
value_at_risk: All assets listed in the Navi lending market
exploit_path: Functions never check that the generic CoinType matches the asset's coin_type, so a caller passes a cheap/mismatched coin type and the market credits or debits the wrong reserve.
preconditions: None beyond a small position in the mismatched asset.

title: Flag _solverFulfilled is unreliable
value_at_risk: Gas budget held by the Atlas solver contract
exploit_path: reconcile sets _solverFulfilled and validateBalances trusts it, but a borrow is still possible afterwards, so a solver can satisfy the flag and then remove the funds the check relied on.
preconditions: Attacker must be a solver/bundler.

title: Lack of Cryptographic Binding Between Proof and Guest Program ID
exploit_path: The verifier checks the guest program ID against a trusted list but the seal is not cryptographically bound to that ID, so a proof produced by one trusted program can be presented under another program's ID.
preconditions: Attacker needs one proof from a trusted guest program.

title: Broken Lagrange Polynomial Evaluation at Zeta
exploit_path: The Lagrange evaluation ignores that zeta can be a root of unity, so the computed value is wrong for those points and a crafted proof can pass verification.
preconditions: Attacker must craft a proof at a root-of-unity zeta.

title: Use of spot reserves in DEX pool
exploit_path: Pricing from instantaneous spot reserves lets an attacker flash-borrow, move the pool, and trade against the manipulated price.
preconditions: Attacker needs flash-loan capital.

title: The forecall and forecallWithToken can be called repeatedly with a same payload
exploit_path: forecall can be called repeatedly with the same payload, so the same cross-chain instruction is executed more than once (double mint/transfer).
preconditions: Attacker needs one valid payload.

title: Leverage calculation is wrong
exploit_path: Leverage uses debt_value + margin_value as the numerator, so computed leverage is wrong and positions are liquidated unfairly or left over-leveraged; a liquidator can exploit the mis-trigger.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to liquidate.

title: Misuse of decimals() can lead to loss of funds
exploit_path: sellerSettlementITM uses the underlying token's decimals when valuing the amount to receive, so the settlement price is scaled wrongly and the caller settles at a favourable rate.
preconditions: Attacker must be the option seller settling ITM.

title: Attackers can steal funds in the vault in migrate_token.rs:migrate_token
exploit_path: The migration instruction does not bind the vault/authority correctly, so an attacker can pass their own accounts and move the vault's tokens.
preconditions: Body withheld; mechanism from title.

title: Signed Command Logic Is Not Checking Signature by Source Account
exploit_path: The transaction logic and SNARK never check that the fee payer equals the source account or that the source signed, so an attacker forges a payment from any account while paying the fee from their own.
preconditions: None; the GraphQL API must be bypassed (trivial client change).

title: The OneHot encoding gadget has incorrect constraints
exploit_path: The OneHot gadget's previous-row constraints are wrong, so the MPT circuit can accept an invalid encoding and a prover can forge account/storage proofs.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit a crafted proof.

title: Missing range checks for the LtChip
exploit_path: The LtChip does not constrain diff columns to the byte range and relies on callers, so a crafted witness can satisfy the circuit with out-of-range values.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit a crafted proof.

title: Unsound native-function declaration leading to critical verifier bypass
exploit_path: The native-function declaration for table.move is unsound, so a malicious module can bypass the bytecode verifier's type/resource checks and manipulate any resource, including coin balances.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to publish a Move module.

title: `ETHRegistrarController.register` is vulnerable to front running
exploit_path: The commitment is not bound to an owner, so an attacker copies a victim's commitment and registers the name to himself when it matures.
preconditions: Attacker must pay the registration price and see the commit transaction.

title: LibRedstone contains signerAddress associated with a public hardhat account
exploit_path: 0xf39F...2266 (Hardhat account #0) is an accepted RedStone signer and its private key is public, so anyone can sign arbitrary price data and post it to Kresko, then borrow against or liquidate with the fake price.
preconditions: None; the key is publicly known.

title: Improper checks leading to invalid output root validation
exploit_path: Initialising TipCursor with a zero l2_safe_head_output_root lets an empty root be accepted as valid when claimed_l2_block_number equals the safe head, so an invalid output root can be proven.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit the claim at the boundary block.

title: Failure to Abort on Incorrect Merkle Proof
value_at_risk: All tokens held by the Merkle distributor
exploit_path: verify_and_claim calls merkle_verifier::verify but ignores its boolean return, so any leaf is accepted; an attacker submits a fabricated leaf and claims tokens repeatedly.
preconditions: None.

title: Missed Knock-in
exploit_path: The instructions do not check the length of remaining_accounts; with no barrier accounts passed, a knock-in is ignored and the user is paid the full APR even though the barrier was hit.
preconditions: Attacker must hold a vault position that knocked in.

title: Old Distributions May Still Exist After Updating
exploit_path: When the new distribution array is shorter, stale entries above the new length remain, so a user can still claim from an old distribution that should have been removed.
preconditions: None.

title: Smart Escrow uses signed integer type i128 without sign checks
exploit_path: Negative i128 values are accepted where amounts are expected, so a caller can pass a negative amount and invert the escrow's balance arithmetic in their favour.
preconditions: None.

title: Business Logic Vulnerability Audit
exploit_path: CLTV/CSV time-locked transactions are not verified when checking deposits, so an attacker can present a transaction that is not yet spendable (or is refundable) as a valid deposit.
preconditions: Attacker must be able to submit a BTC transaction/proof.

title: Possibility of arbitrage inside one pool
exploit_path: Premiums are extracted from the pool balance and liquidity can be added on one side only, creating an internal arbitrage that drains the pool's premium buffer.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and a two-sided position.

title: Double inversion of slippageReverse_ in constructor severely weakens slippage protection High impact finding
exploit_path: The constructor inverts slippageReverse_ twice, so the effective slippage bound is far looser than configured and swaps can be sandwiched.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and a victim swap.

title: Incorrect Mapping in _createStakepool Function
exploit_path: The function writes _stakepool[epochid][STAKEPOOL_TOTAL_ID] but reads _stakes[epochid][STAKEPOOL_TOTAL_ID] instead of the per-user key, so stakes are attributed to the aggregate bucket and a user can claim from it.
preconditions: None.

title: Arb Guard Does Not Effectively Protect Execution
exploit_path: The arb guard does not effectively protect execution, so orders can be sandwiched within the guard's tolerance.
preconditions: Attacker needs capital and a victim order.

title: Migration's `leave` function allows leaving a committed proposal
exploit_path: leave() can be called on a committed (and failed) proposal, duplicating withdrawContributions, so a contributor can be paid twice from the proposal's escrow.
preconditions: Attacker must have contributed to a committed proposal.

title: Voters from VotingEscrow can vote infinite times in vote_for_gauge_weights() of GaugeController
exploit_path: A veRWA holder can vote repeatedly without the previous vote being removed, so one locker accumulates unbounded gauge weight and captures the emissions of every gauge it votes for.
preconditions: Attacker must hold a veRWA lock.

title: Unused ERC20 tokens are not refunded, and can be stolen by attacker
value_at_risk: Tokens left unrefunded in the Amun pool
exploit_path: When the minted amount differs from what the user sent, the excess underlying is left in the contract and is not refunded; an attacker triggers the condition and then takes the stranded tokens.
preconditions: Fee accrual between submission and inclusion.

title: triggerSendFrom() will send all the ETH in the destination chain where sendFrom() is called to the refundAddress in the LzCallParams argument
value_at_risk: All ETH held by the sending contract on the destination chain
exploit_path: triggerSendFrom forwards the refundAddress from LzCallParams and sends the contract's entire ETH balance to it, so a caller sets refundAddress to themselves and drains the ETH.
preconditions: None beyond a callable triggerSendFrom.

title: Wrong liquidity units calculation
exploit_path: The associativity of the liquidity-units formula is wrong ((P*part1+part2)/part3 instead of P*(part1+part2)/part3), so minted LP units do not match the deposit and a user can mint extra units and redeem them.
preconditions: None.

title: Locked funds from tokenization are credited twice to user leading to protocol fund loss
exploit_path: Locked funds are released twice when conviction is re-acquired from an NFT, so the user is credited twice and the protocol loses the difference.
preconditions: Attacker must tokenize and re-acquire conviction.

title: The renewal grace period gives users insurance for no premium
exploit_path: A protection position can be renewed after expiry within the grace period without paying the premium for the gap, so the user keeps cover for free.
preconditions: Position must be within the grace window.

title: Attacker Can Get Infinite BVM_ETH Tokens to Drain the Protocol
value_at_risk: all ETH escrowed in the Mantle L1 bridge
exploit_path: L1 depositTransaction forwards unbacked ETH value into TransactionDeposited; op-geth applies the delta to BVM_ETH state without a balance check and BigToHash turns the negative sender balance into a positive one, minting 2x the value on L2
preconditions: only L1 gas; no L2 ETH balance required

title: Liquidity calculation error when adding liquidity
exploit_path: liquidity minted is computed with the pool base-token total added to the user deposit, so a depositor receives more LP than the deposit is worth and can withdraw the surplus
preconditions: pool already holds base tokens

title: Fully Filled Auction Double Counted
exploit_path: a fully filled auction stays in the position tick list, so claiming credits the user again for an auction already settled, taking tokens from the rest of the pool
preconditions: auction fully filled at claim time

title: Liquidity Double Counted At Position End
exploit_path: liquidityDeltaMinus double counts active liquidity stashed at the stop tick, leaving phantom pool liquidity after the position ends and paying fees on it
preconditions: price crosses the position end

title: Missing authorization checks in removeLiquidityWithLimit and removeLiquidityWithLimitETH
exploit_path: removeLiquidityWithLimit / removeLiquidityWithLimitETH lack authorization, so any caller can burn another holder's LP position and take the underlying
preconditions: victim holds LP; body not in corpus

title: Multiple RLP encodings share the same RLC value
exploit_path: RLP tag RLC is unchanged by prepending zero bytes, so distinct encodings collide and a prover can satisfy the circuit with a different transaction than the one committed
preconditions: ability to build a zk proof

title: Slashes or other reduction of assets in the Anchor strategy could block drawing a winner while causing a bank run, leaving slow users lose assets
exploit_path: after a strategy loss the winner cannot be drawn but withdrawals still pay the full recorded deposit, so the first withdrawers exit whole and later users absorb the shortfall
preconditions: strategy loss / slash; be first to withdraw

title: The same claim proof can be used multiple times
exploit_path: claim input is the concatenation {proof}{amount} with no length framing, so one proof can be re-split into different (proof, amount) pairs and claimed repeatedly
preconditions: airdrop claim open

title: OTCMarketLib.sol: Offers can be partially filled
value_at_risk: GFly held by the OTC contract
exploit_path: a single bracket can overfill Offer.filled beyond amountInWei, letting a malicious offer creator settle a partially filled offer and claim GFly reserved for other offers
preconditions: attacker creates an offer with multiple brackets

title: Health factor validation may depend on eMode category settings such as liqui-
exploit_path: health-factor validation is skipped when the eMode category changes to 0, so a borrower can leave an eMode position without the HF check and carry excess debt
preconditions: borrower switches eMode category

title: Arbitrary calls execution in Executor and GenericCrossChainFacet
exploit_path: Executor and GenericCrossChainFacet execute caller-supplied calls without restricting target/selector, so an attacker can make the facet call arbitrary contracts with its own privileges
preconditions: body not in corpus

title: Rounding Error
exploit_path: compute_fee_earned uses fixed_mul_ceil, so small balances round fees up; repeated small claims can drain more than the fee pool owes
preconditions: many small positions; per-claim rounding

title: Order Fulfillment with Zero-Amount
exploit_path: prepare_fulfill_simple takes fulfillAmount from the message with no minAmountOut check, so a taker can fulfil a Bypass-mode order with zero amount and keep the maker funds
preconditions: auction mode Bypass

title: WEIGHT DISCREPANCY ON DELEGATION CHANGE
exploit_path: on delegation change the weighted stake is not moved from the old node to the new one, so the staker keeps weight on both and over-earns rewards
preconditions: delegate, then redelegate

title: transaction
exploit_path: authentication tokens from reverted transactions are never marked used, so an observed token can be replayed to authorise a later transaction on the victim account
preconditions: observe a reverted tx auth token

title: Confusing SignerPolicy logic
exploit_path: resetSigners can set one owner while signerPolicy stays MINUS_ONE_SIGNER, making requiredSigners underflow to 0 and letting a single signature pass
preconditions: wallet with MINUS_ONE_SIGNER policy

title: Anyone Can Steal All Funds From a DCA Order
exploit_path: fillDCA accepts an arbitrary takerInteraction; an empty or zero-return interaction still transfers order.inAmount to the taker while the maker receives nothing
preconditions: open DCA order

title: No token transfers
exploit_path: the transfer calls inside buyCommon are commented out, so buyFoilToken credits the buyer without pulling payment
preconditions: purchase function reachable

title: Denom collisions can be exploited to steal user funds
exploit_path: denomination collisions in the Duality DEX/incentives modules let one denom be mistaken for another, so an attacker can claim or withdraw against the wrong asset
preconditions: body not in corpus

title: The Oracle Aggregator Can Be Hijacked By Third-Parties
exploit_path: deployment and initialize are separate transactions, so an attacker can front-run initialize and set themselves as the oracle/owner of the aggregator
preconditions: uninitialized deployed contract

title: Flash Loan Vulnerability
exploit_path: flash-loan-funded state manipulation in the liquidity mining accounting; body not in corpus
preconditions: flash loan capital

title: longToken Assumed To Be The indexToken
exploit_path: the long token price is returned as the index token price, so markets whose long token is not the index (e.g. DOGE with ETH long) are priced from the wrong asset and can be borrowed against or liquidated at a false value
preconditions: market where long != index

title: Incorrect Position Distribution Amount
exploit_path: hypercore positions are valued at position size instead of margin, inflating TVL and target leverage for the leveraged token
preconditions: position open on hypercore

title: The patch is not sufficient: there is another insidious exploit that can cause the same critical consequences
exploit_path: the added wrapped-ETH2LD check can still be satisfied, so an attacker re-registers an expired name through the old registrar and implicitly unwraps subdomains whose fuses should prevent it
preconditions: expired ETH2LD

title: Anyone can set the `baseRatePerYear` after the `updateFrequency` has passed
exploit_path: updateBaseRate is public and only gated by elapsed time, so anyone can set baseRatePerYear and then borrow or lend against the manipulated rate
preconditions: updateFrequency elapsed

title: `PARENT_CANNOT_CONTROL` can be bypassed by maliciously unwrapping parent node
exploit_path: unwrapping the parent node clears the fuse state, so PARENT_CANNOT_CONTROL can be bypassed and the attacker regains control of a subdomain that should be burnt
preconditions: own the parent; unwrap it

title: Wrong use of `nftID` to check if a `PowerFarm` position is an Aave position
exploit_path: the nftID check misidentifies Aave positions, so getLiveDebtRatio returns 0 and the position cannot be liquidated or repaid normally
preconditions: Aave-mode PowerFarm position

title: RubiconMarket `batchOffer` and `batchRequote` make offers as self; complete loss of funds for some types of tokens, for example WETH
exploit_path: batchOffer/batchRequote record the offer as made by the market itself, so the maker's funds are escrowed under the wrong account and can be taken or lost for tokens like WETH
preconditions: use batchOffer/batchRequote

title: Missing pool-manager validation enables LP fee manipulation
exploit_path: missing pool-manager validation lets a caller act as pool manager and set LP fees, capturing swap fees from LPs
preconditions: body not in corpus

title: Missing fee_collector check in the Claim instruction
exploit_path: the Claim instruction does not verify fee_collector against the airdrop record, so a caller can redirect the fee to their own account
preconditions: claim open

title: Vault executes swaps without slippage protection
exploit_path: vault reward swaps execute with no slippage bound, so a searcher can sandwich the swap and take the difference from user rewards
preconditions: reward swap in mempool

title: The deposit / withdraw / trade transaction lack of expiration timestamp check and slippage control
exploit_path: deposit/withdraw/trade transactions carry no expiry or slippage bound, so a searcher can hold and execute them at a worse price
preconditions: pending user transaction

title: High-volatility ticks can cause bank run due to negative liq-
exploit_path: high-volatility ticks make the liquidation fee exceed maintenance, producing negative liquidation outcomes and a bank run in which the first exiters are paid in full
preconditions: volatile tick; be first to exit

title: bitcoin-spv - multiple integer under-/overflows
exploit_path: integer under/overflows in bitcoin-spv let a crafted SPV proof validate a payment that was never made, so the attacker can mint/redeem BTC-backed assets
preconditions: craft a fake SPV proof

title: Incorrect setting of initiate data due to extrapolation
exploit_path: extrapolated vault balance ignores the protocol fee, so the balance is overstated and a withdrawer receives more than entitled
preconditions: withdraw after extrapolation

title: Native account functions don't correctly handle RETRY_WITH_FALLBACK
exploit_path: RETRY_WITH_FALLBACK is not handled by the native account functions, so the policy check can fall through and allow an action that should be blocked
preconditions: account with minPolicies

title: Partial Liquidations won't be possible for vaults with the collateral asset of decimals < 18
exploit_path: gainedShares rounds to zero for collateral with fewer than 18 decimals, so partial liquidations are impossible and the borrower keeps an unliquidated position
preconditions: low-decimals collateral

title: Failed deposits are incorrectly witnessed as having succeeded
exploit_path: failed deposits are witnessed as successful, so the destination chain can release funds for a deposit that never settled
preconditions: body not in corpus

title: Missing range proof enables confidential balance overdraft
exploit_path: a missing range proof lets a confidential balance be overdrawn, so the attacker can spend more than they hold
preconditions: n/a

title: Risk of token theft due to possible integer underflow in slt
exploit_path: an integer underflow in the slt path lets a position be manipulated so tokens can be taken
preconditions: n/a

title: Users can bypass limits and purchase more licenses than allowed by re- entering functions
exploit_path: the ETH commission low-level call happens before state updates, so a referral contract can re-enter and buy more licenses than the per-wallet cap
preconditions: attacker-controlled referral receiver

title: Possibility of Overwriting Public Share
exploit_path: dkg_ended can overwrite a public share without checking the existing commitment, so a malicious signer can substitute its share and later forge signatures
preconditions: participate in DKG

title: `dForce_compoundRewardsWithFlashloan()` and `dForce_swapAndLeverageWithFlashloan()` are prone to sandwich attacks
exploit_path: dForce flashloan compound/leverage helpers have no amountOutMin, so a searcher can sandwich the swap and take part of the reward
preconditions: mempool visibility

title: Incorrect Price Decimals in LionSwapFeeLP
exploit_path: LionSwapFeeLP prices LP tokens with the wrong decimals, so a buyer pays too little (or too much) for vault LP and can redeem at the correct value
preconditions: buy underpriced LP

title: Possible bad debt in StETHQueue
exploit_path: when repay exceeds stETHAmount the borrower has no incentive to repay, leaving bad debt with the Liquidity contract
preconditions: borrow near maxLTV then abandon

title: Insufficient validation of caller-supplied parameters in campaign creation
exploit_path: createCampaign is permissionless and takes the bridge, identity registry and fee config from the caller, so an attacker can deploy a campaign whose bridge steals the rewards
preconditions: none

title: Nonce auth message is weak and volatile
exploit_path: the auth message nonce is weak/volatile, so a signed authorization can be replayed
preconditions: observe a signed message

title: bitcoin-spv - multiple integer under-/overflows
exploit_path: the same bitcoin-spv integer under/overflows as the github finding: a crafted SPV proof can validate an unspent output
preconditions: craft a fake SPV proof

title: Outstanding reserved tokens are incorrectly counted in total redemption weight
exploit_path: outstanding reserved tokens are added to the redemption weight directly instead of being multiplied by contributionFloor, so redemption payouts are skewed toward some redeemers
preconditions: n/a

title: Lack of StrategyDetailsParam.vault validation allows the borrower to steal all the funds from the vault
exploit_path: commitToLien does not check that the strategy vault equals address(this), so a borrower can borrow real assets and repay with a fake asset from an attacker-controlled vault
preconditions: attacker deploys a fake vault and token

title: Allowing More than 10x Leverage
exploit_path: the leverage cap can be exceeded, so a borrower can open more leverage than allowed and walk away from the debt
preconditions: n/a

title: Issue H-1: The renewal grace period gives users insurance for no premium
exploit_path: the renewal grace period gives coverage without a premium, so a user can keep insurance for free during the grace window
preconditions: policy near renewal

title: Attackers can steal funds by swapping in both directions
exploit_path: a minimal swap one way followed by the reverse returns outsized amounts (1 -> 1 -> 10,000,000,001), draining the pool
preconditions: pool with the affected curve

title: (Re-Audit) Users May Supply Arbitrary Collateral Contrary to Specification
exploit_path: users can supply arbitrary collateral contrary to spec, so worthless collateral can back real borrowing
preconditions: n/a

title: Issue H-2: All funds can be stolen from FixedStrikeOptionTeller using a token with malicious decimals
exploit_path: a payout token whose decimals() changes between calls makes quoteAmount round to 0 at create and huge at exercise, so options are minted without collateral and the Teller is drained
preconditions: attacker deploys the payout token

title: TOFT exerciseOption can be used to steal all underlying erc20 tokens
exploit_path: exerciseInternal trusts user-supplied tapOftAddress and delegatecalls a transfer from the TOFT, so the attacker can move the TOFT's whole ERC20 balance to themselves
preconditions: none

title: Vault leverage can be increased to any value up to min margin requirement due to incorrect maxRedeem calculations with closable and LEVERAGE_BUFFER
exploit_path: an incorrect maxRate lets vault leverage rise to the minimum margin requirement, so a borrower can take maximal leverage
preconditions: n/a

title: Funding Fee Rate is calculated based only on the Oracle Maker's skew but applied across the entire market, enabling extreme funding rates at low cost
exploit_path: the funding fee is derived only from the oracle maker's skew but charged to everyone, so traders on one side over/underpay and a positioned trader can capture the difference
preconditions: n/a

title: H-02. TokenManager - Unlimited withdraw
exploit_path: TokenManager.withdraw pays from CapitalPool using userTokenBalanceMap but never decrements the balance, so withdraw can be called repeatedly to drain the pool
preconditions: none

title: Fee Precision Loss Disrupts Liquidations and Causes Loss of Funds
exploit_path: fee precision loss undercharges borrowing/funding fees and delays liquidations, so a borrower pays less than owed
preconditions: coarse rate regime

title: Adversary can use send_nft to bypass the payment and steal seller’s token in auto-approve scenario
exploit_path: with auto-approve, a bidder can call send_nft to take the NFT via _transfer_nft without settlement, then cancel the bid for a full refund
preconditions: auto-approve listing

title: Incorrect slippage_tolerance handling in stableswap provide_liquidty function
exploit_path: slippage_tolerance is handled incorrectly in stableswap provide_liquidity, so a liquidity adder accepts a worse ratio than intended and a searcher can capture it
preconditions: n/a

title: Vault can be drained by updating the buffer underlying token
exploit_path: wrap/unwrap work with uninitialized buffers; an attacker inflates a buffer with a malicious underlying, then repoints asset() to a valuable vault token and removes liquidity against the inflated shares
preconditions: attacker deploys the malicious underlying

title: Users can enjoy high APR without continue lock
exploit_path: users can earn high APR without keeping the lock, so they collect rewards they did not qualify for
preconditions: n/a

preconditions: victim's swap transaction is visible in the mempool; victim has an over-collateralized Comet position

title: Reentrancy with a fake token in AqueductV1Auction
entry_point: AqueductV1Auction bid/settle with a fake token
exploit_path: 1) Attacker bids using a fake ERC20 whose transfer/transferFrom reenters the auction. 2) During the callback the auction's accounting is mid-update, so the attacker can register a second bid or settle early. 3) Attacker exits with more than deposited.
preconditions: auction accepts arbitrary ERC20 bids; token has a hook

title: Incorrect Amounts Are Used During Withdrawals
exploit_path: 1) Attacker opens a position, then calls withdraw with amounts that the contract computes from the wrong variable. 2) The incorrect amount is paid out, exceeding the attacker's entitlement. 3) Repeat or close the position to keep the excess.
preconditions: a live Sentiment pool with liquidity

title: Attacker Can Drain All Funds from a Pool
value_at_risk: all funds in a Sentiment pool
exploit_path: 1) Attacker exploits the pool's accounting to withdraw more than supplied. 2) The pool's balance is drained to the attacker.
preconditions: pool with liquidity; no special role

title: withdrawnDividends are not properly updated for a user
value_at_risk: dividend token balance reserved for holders
exploit_path: 1) Attacker holds tokens and claims dividends. 2) withdrawnDividends is not increased by the paid amount. 3) Attacker claims again for the same entitlement until the dividend reserve is empty.
preconditions: attacker holds any balance; reserve funded

title: XGBT, pegged to Gumball NFTs, can be withdrawn directly for GBT.
entry_point: Gumbar redeem of XGBT for GBT
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes Gumball NFTs to mint XGBT. 2) Attacker transfers the XGBT to another address; the locked-NFT bookkeeping does not follow the tokens. 3) At the new address the XGBT is no longer flagged as NFT-pegged, so it can be redeemed directly for GBT. 4) Repeat until the GBT reserve is short.
preconditions: attacker owns a Gumball NFT to stake; GBT liquidity in Gumbar

title: Rounding Errors In The Way Prices Are Calculated Results In The Theft Of Ace Tokens
value_at_risk: ACE tokens held by the AcesFactory
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls buyToken with amount < 1 ether and aceAmountIn = 0. 2) getPrice() divides by 1e18 and rounds down to 0, so the attacker pays nothing. 3) Attacker mints an arbitrarily large launchpad token balance in repeated calls. 4) Attacker calls sellTokens to redeem the free tokens for ACE from the factory.
preconditions: any launchpad token exists; factory holds ACE

title: didTransferShares function has no access control modi ier
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls the unguarded didTransferShares() directly instead of going through the staking contract. 2) The function credits shares to an arbitrary address without moving tokens. 3) Attacker withdraws the credited shares.
preconditions: the function is externally reachable on the deployed contract

title: Updating the forwarder's claimable amount during a withdrawal request uses the wrong decimal precision, resulting in the ability to steal funds
exploit_path: 1) Attacker submits a withdrawal request whose amount is expressed in the token's native decimals. 2) update_claimable_amount scales the amount to 18 decimals although the caller already supplied an 18-decimal figure (or vice versa), so the deducted claimable amount is wrong by 10^12. 3) Attacker's claimable balance is reduced far less than the amount withdrawn, leaving a surplus he can claim later.
preconditions: forwarder holds claimable balances for other users

title: Incorrect calculation of deposit value causes more shares to be minted
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits when the vault's deposit-value calculation is wrong. 2) The error mints more shares than the deposit is worth. 3) Attacker redeems the excess shares for a larger pro-rata claim.
preconditions: vault uses the faulty calculation at the attacker's deposit

title: Escrow.sol: Escrow contract allows for stealing funds(2)
value_at_risk: tokens the victim approved to the Escrow contract
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves the Escrow contract. 2) Attacker front-runs the victim's vault creation and calls escrow() with the same assets but _from = victim. 3) The contract pulls the victim's tokens into the attacker's escrow. 4) Attacker calls release() and receives them.
preconditions: victim has an outstanding approval to Escrow; attacker sees the pending tx

title: Free debt token minting in PSM when the peg token uses non-18 decimals.
entry_point: PSM mint with a non-18-decimal peg token
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits a peg token that uses non-18 decimals into the PSM. 2) The PSM scales the deposit as if it were 18 decimals, so the attacker is credited far more debt tokens than the deposit is worth. 3) Attacker sells or redeems the minted debt tokens against the protocol's collateral.
preconditions: the PSM accepts a peg token with decimals != 18

title: Arbitrary swap for any account without permission
entry_point: swap on behalf of any account
value_at_risk: other traders' positions/collateral in the Roseon perp
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls the swap entry point naming a victim account. 2) The function does not check that msg.sender is the account owner or an approved operator. 3) The swap executes against the victim's position, letting the attacker trade the victim's collateral into an asset he controls or at a price he sets.
preconditions: a victim account with an open position

title: Repeated Invocation Resulting in Excessive Claims
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls claim repeatedly. 2) The claim does not mark the entitlement as consumed, so each invocation pays again. 3) Repeat until the reward pool is empty.
preconditions: reward pool funded

title: Fund Token Manipulation
entry_point: fund token transfer / share price update
exploit_path: 1) Attacker manipulates the fund token balance or transfer path so the fund's share price is computed from a stale/attacker-controlled value. 2) Attacker mints shares cheaply or redeems them at an inflated price.
preconditions: attacker can move the fund token or its price input

title: Possible Drained Reserve From exchangeAndStoreTokens()
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates or uses an NFT position and supplies a malicious _swapTarget / tokenOrders callData. 2) exchangeAndStoreTokens executes address(reserve).call() and ExchangeHelpers.fillQuote() with that attacker data. 3) The arbitrary call transfers the reserve's tokens to the attacker.
preconditions: attacker can create a position with a custom order

title: DRAIN FUNDS VIA executeRolloverAndBurn FUNCTION
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls executeRolloverAndBurn(lender, rewards) directly; there is no access control and the new tranche is taken from msg.sender. 2) The function transfers approvedRollovers[lender][newTranche] + rewards out of the vault to the attacker's contract and burns the lender's shares. 3) Attacker repeats for each lender with a recorded rollover.
preconditions: a rollover has been approved for at least one lender

title: Arbitrary Function Execution In retrieveFunds Enables Complete Protocol Compromise
exploit_path: 1) Attacker submits an order with retrieveFundsRequested = true and attacker-controlled retrieveFunds calldata. 2) _settleSwap/_settleLendOrder calls Address.functionCall(address(this), retrieveFundsCalldata) on the diamond. 3) The arbitrary call executes a privileged facet function, letting the attacker move user funds.
preconditions: intent-based order flow is enabled

title: Operations Are Vulnerable To Signature Replay Via Reentrancy
entry_point: BLS Wallet operation replay via reentrancy
exploit_path: 1) Attacker gets a wallet operation executed that calls back into the wallet. 2) During the callback the operation's nonce/verification state is not yet committed. 3) Attacker replays the same signed operation, moving assets twice.
preconditions: a signed operation from the victim that makes an external call

title: Reentrancy in collectFee()
value_at_risk: accumulated fees in the transit contract
exploit_path: 1) Attacker becomes the fee recipient or supplies a malicious recipient contract. 2) collectFee() sends ETH before settling the fee accounting. 3) The recipient reenters collectFee() and collects the fee again.
preconditions: attacker can register as recipient or influence the payout address

title: Access Control Violation - Critical
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls transfer() with any addr argument. 2) The function ignores addr for the actual transfer and always sends the pool's tokens to msg.sender. 3) Attacker receives the entire pool balance.
preconditions: none

title: F-2023-1580 - Unrestricted Access to Minting Functions
value_at_risk: the token's entire value / liquidity pools
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls mint() or mintTo(attacker, amount). 2) Neither has an access-control modifier, so the attacker can mint unlimited supply to himself. 3) Attacker sells the minted tokens into the protocol's liquidity.
preconditions: token is listed/traded anywhere

title: Reentrancy Vulnerability Allows Draining All Funds
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes a hook-capable token. 2) stakeToken updates usersLiquidity then calls _claimReward, which makes an external call. 3) From the hook the attacker reenters to claim from other incentives while usersLiquidity is inflated. 4) Repeat until reward balances are drained.
preconditions: a reward-bearing token with a transfer hook (ERC777) is supported

title: Missing Access Control for setDestinationSettler
value_at_risk: ERC20 approvals fillers granted to the destination settler
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls setDestinationSettler(chainId, attackerContract). 2) Fillers that approved the previous settler now have their allowance consumed by the attacker's contract when they fill an order. 3) Attacker transfers the approved tokens to himself.
preconditions: fillers have outstanding approvals to the settler

title: Anyone can move EURS tokens that the user allowed FlorinTreasury to spend
value_at_risk: EURS balances of any user who approved FlorinTreasury
exploit_path: 1) Attacker scans for users with an outstanding EURS allowance to FlorinTreasury. 2) Calls depositEUR with from = victim. 3) The contract does transferFrom(victim, treasury, amount), pulling the victim's EURS into the treasury. 4) Attacker redeems/withdraws the credited balance (or uses the deposit to mint Florin tokens) for himself.
preconditions: victim granted an allowance to FlorinTreasury

title: [C-01] Incorrect conversion from USD to asset during redemption
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits 1 asset when the rate is 2e18. 2) Deposit converts to usdAmount = 2e18. 3) redeem multiplies by the rate again instead of dividing, returning 4e18 assets for a 1e18 deposit. 4) Repeat until the vault is empty.
preconditions: rate != 1e18; vault holds assets

title: Exploitation of the receive Function to Steal Funds
exploit_path: 1) Attacker triggers a withdrawal that sends ETH to a contract he controls. 2) The ETH transfer enters WiseLending.receive(), which resets the syncPool reentrancy guard. 3) Attacker reenters withdrawExactAmountETH before the first withdrawal's state is committed, withdrawing again. 4) Repeat to drain the pool.
preconditions: attacker has a position and a contract receiver; pool holds ETH

title: Unrevoked approvals allow NFT recovery by previous owner
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sells or transfers an NFT but the approval granted earlier is not revoked. 2) Attacker calls transferFrom(victim, attacker, tokenId) using the stale approval. 3) Attacker recovers the NFT.
preconditions: attacker previously held the NFT and set an approval that survives transfer

title: Lender can Bypass Call Window Protection and liquidate borrowers
exploit_path: 1) Borrower is inside the protected call window. 2) Attacker-lender calls liquidate through a path that does not enforce the window check. 3) The borrower is liquidated early and the attacker takes the liquidation bonus.
preconditions: attacker is a lender to the target borrower

title: Liquidity addition vulnerable to sandwich attacks due to spot price manipulation
exploit_path: 1) Victim submits addLiquidity. 2) Attacker sandwiches: moves the spot price before the deposit, lets the deposit execute at the skewed price, then reverses. 3) Attacker keeps the difference.
preconditions: public mempool; spot-price-based liquidity math

title: Malicious users can drain the contract's funds by buying cards at cheaper prices using reentrancy
exploit_path: 1) Attacker's contract calls buy(). 2) ERC1155 _mint calls onERC1155Received before the price/supply state is updated. 3) Attacker reenters buy() and purchases the next cards at the first card's price. 4) Attacker resells or keeps the discounted cards.
preconditions: a card sale is live with a rising price curve

title: Cross-chain borrow ignores existing debt in collateral validation
exploit_path: 1) Attacker has an existing cross-chain debt. 2) Calls borrow again; the collateral check ignores the existing debt. 3) Attacker borrows beyond the safe limit and defaults, leaving bad debt.
preconditions: cross-chain borrow path enabled

title: Missing Signatures From transferInternally May Allow User Assets To Be Moved Without Authorization
value_at_risk: user assets held by the Rho protocol
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls transferInternally without the required signatures. 2) The function moves a user's internal balance to an address the attacker controls.
preconditions: internal balances exist

title: Unauthorized Transfer of User-Approved ERC20 Tokens via LeverageRouter
value_at_risk: ERC20 approvals users granted to LeverageRouter
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls deposit (or redeem) with a swapCalls entry whose target is the approved token and whose data is transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount). 2) The router executes functionCallWithValue on the attacker-supplied target. 3) The router's allowance is used to move the victim's tokens to the attacker.
preconditions: victim has an outstanding allowance to LeverageRouter

title: Incorrect IPROVER_INTERFACE_ID constant allows malicious solvers to steal funds during ful- ﬁllment
entry_point: fulfilment path with the wrong IPROVER_INTERFACE_ID
exploit_path: 1) Attacker registers as a solver and submits a fulfilment whose prover contract reports the wrong interface id. 2) The ERC-165 check passes against the incorrect constant, so the attacker's contract is treated as a valid prover. 3) The attacker's prover returns a success claim without the underlying proof, releasing the escrowed funds.
preconditions: attacker can act as a solver; intent escrow funded

title: Marketplace OGN balance is drainable through withdrawListing
exploit_path: 1) Attacker becomes the depositManager of a listing (or creates one). 2) Calls withdrawListing; the function pays the listing deposit but never marks the listing as withdrawn. 3) Attacker calls it repeatedly until the Marketplace's OGN balance is empty.
preconditions: attacker controls a listing's depositManager

title: BuniCornPool.burn is publicly callable and can transfer others’ coins
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls burn() at a chosen moment. 2) The function pays out to the caller based on pool state without checking that the caller owns the position being burned. 3) With correct timing the attacker receives tokens belonging to another user.
preconditions: pool has active positions; attacker can time the call

title: Witch’s buy and payAll functions allow users to buy collateral from vaults not undergoing auctions
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls buy() naming a vault that is not in auction. 2) The function does not check auction status, so it sells the vault's collateral at the auction (below-market) price. 3) Attacker takes the collateral and the vault owner absorbs the difference.
preconditions: a vault with collateral and no active auction

title: Reentrancy into AntePool.checkTest scales challenger eligibility amount
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deploys a malicious AnteTest whose check reenters AntePool.checkTest. 2) Each reentrant failed check calls _calculateChallengerEligibility, which adds to eligibleAmount without resetting. 3) The attacker's eligibility scales with the number of reentries, so his payout exceeds the pool's intended distribution.
preconditions: attacker can create an AnteTest and challenge a pool

title: DCA ownership transfers can be abused to steal tokens
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sets up a DCA whose owner is the victim (or transfers ownership to the victim without consent). 2) The DCA's swaps pull funds from ownerOf[dcaId]. 3) With the victim's existing approvals, the attacker triggers a swap that spends the victim's tokens into an asset he controls.
preconditions: victim has approvals to the swap target

title: Escrow approvals are not cleared when club is transferred allowing for abuse after transfer
entry_point: escrow approvals after club NFT transfer
value_at_risk: players/tokens held by the club escrow
exploit_path: 1) Attacker owns clubId and grants escrow approvals to himself. 2) Sells the club NFT; approvals persist across the transfer. 3) Attacker uses the stale approvals to transfer assets out of the club escrow.
preconditions: attacker was a club owner and set approvals

title: Reentrancy issue with the withdraw method of USDC. All tokens could be drained.
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls withdraw() with a hook-capable token or a contract receiver. 2) _withdraw transfers sUSD to the target before burning the caller's USDA. 3) Attacker reenters withdraw/withdrawTo and withdraws again before the burn. 4) Repeat to drain reserves.
preconditions: sUSD or the target token has a transfer hook

title: Missing accesscontrol in afterlockupdate
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls afterLockUpdate(victim or attacker) without any lock activity. 2) The controller updates registered balances and qualifies the address for rewards. 3) Attacker claims emissions without staking.
preconditions: rewards controller is live and funded

title: Adversary can utilise approved to Magnetar oTAP and tOLP NFTs
exploit_path: 1) Victim has approved Magnetar to operate their oTAP/tOLP. 2) Attacker calls Magnetar with an operation naming the victim's NFT (exercise/participate/exit/lock/unlock). 3) Magnetar forwards the call without checking ownership, acting on the victim's position to the attacker's benefit.
preconditions: victim approved Magnetar

title: Attakers can steal the funds from long-term reservation
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls setbidtobuy() to gain auto-approval on a sale. 2) Calls withdrawtolandlord() specifying an arbitrary payout address. 3) The function authorises with send permission and pays the tenant's deposit to the attacker's address. 4) Attacker cancels the bid to recover his own funds.
preconditions: a property with an active long-term reservation

title: [H-01] WithdrawDonation can incur max slippage
exploit_path: 1) Victim calls withdrawDonation with a sane _minAmount. 2) Attacker front-runs with _minAmount = 0, which is permissionless. 3) The transfer executes with no slippage protection; the attacker sandwiches the swap and captures the difference.
preconditions: public mempool; a donation withdrawal pending

title: [H-01] launchpad-contracts/U2UBuyBase#claimERC721 - Incorrect value is assigned to the _amountClaimed[sender]
exploit_path: 1) Attacker buys once and claims. 2) _amountClaimed[sender] is overwritten with the current claim count instead of incremented. 3) On the next claim the recorded amount is too low, so the attacker claims more NFTs than purchased.
preconditions: a live U2U launchpad sale

title: Phony signatures can be used to forge any strategy
exploit_path: 1) Attacker forges a strategy commitment signature that the vault accepts as valid. 2) The forged commitment names the attacker as the strategy/recipient. 3) Funds are routed to the attacker.
preconditions: vault accepts commitments via the vulnerable signature scheme

title: Users can borrow above the collateral NFT fair value
exploit_path: 1) Attacker uses an NFT whose appraised value is below the borrowed amount. 2) The borrow check values the NFT above its fair value (stale or manipulable appraisal). 3) Attacker borrows more than the collateral is worth and defaults.
preconditions: an NFT with a manipulable appraisal; lender liquidity

title: Attackers can swap lower-value tokens for valuable assets
exploit_path: 1) Attacker offers a lower-value token into the swap. 2) Input validation on the token pair/amount is missing, so the swap accepts it as equivalent. 3) Attacker receives the valuable asset.
preconditions: swap pool holds the valuable asset

title: Assets integrity
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls buy/claim with msg.value = 1 wei. 2) The only check is msg.value >= 1 wei, not the actual price. 3) Attacker receives tokens/claims worth far more than paid.
preconditions: lottery sale is live

title: Liquidation logic allows the liquidator to liquidate more than it should
exploit_path: 1) Attacker liquidates a position. 2) The liquidation logic lets him repay less/ seize more than the close factor allows. 3) Attacker keeps the excess collateral.
preconditions: a liquidatable position on Aave Aptos

title: Mont price can be manipulated to earn more rewards
entry_point: Mont price used in reward weight
exploit_path: 1) Attacker moves the Mont price (thin market) before a reward-bearing action. 2) Reward weight is derived from the manipulated price. 3) Attacker earns more rewards than his stake justifies.
preconditions: thin Mont liquidity

title: Anyone can use or steal `ArbitrumSwaps` native asset balance
value_at_risk: the native balance the contract holds from Stargate refunds
exploit_path: 1) A Stargate swap refunds native token to ArbitrumSwaps because _refundAddress is address(this). 2) Attacker back-runs the refund and calls arbitrumSwaps with WETH_DEPOSIT then WETH_WITHDRAW, naming himself as the recipient. 3) The whole contract balance is sent to the attacker.
preconditions: a refund has just landed in ArbitrumSwaps

title: Any plugins using permit2 can steal funds with frontrunning attack
value_at_risk: tokens a proxy owner authorized via Permit2
exploit_path: 1) Victim signs a PermitSingle that authorizes a spender, token and amount but is not bound to a target or function. 2) Attacker front-runs the victim's proxy call and repurposes the same signature. 3) The proxy pulls the approved tokens to an address the attacker controls.
preconditions: victim uses a Permit2-based plugin and the signature is visible in the mempool

title: Any tokens with the currency symbol as the hash of poolMintingPolicyContract can be minted
entry_point: mint with a forged currency symbol
exploit_path: 1) Attacker mints a token whose currency symbol equals the hash of poolMintingPolicyContract. 2) The validator accepts the symbol as the minting policy, so the token is treated as the pool's asset. 3) Attacker deposits the forged token into the pool and withdraws the real asset.
preconditions: a SundaeSwap pool accepts the symbol-based policy

title: swapMargin Used To Game The AMM
exploit_path: 1) Attacker uses swapMargin to move margin between positions in a way the AMM does not price. 2) The AMM's reserves/accounting are gamed so the attacker's position is worth more than deposited.
preconditions: swapMargin enabled; AMM liquidity

title: POOL LOCK-UP PERIOD BYPASS TO STEAL INTEREST OF LOANS
value_at_risk: interest owed to other pool depositors
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits into the pool. 2) Bypasses the lock-up period (the lock check is missing or gameable). 3) Withdraws early, taking a pro-rata share of interest that should have accrued to longer-term depositors.
preconditions: pool has accrued interest

title: Attackers can profit by depositing different tokens and withdrawing as native tokens
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes a low-value non-native token (e.g. TRX, 6 decimals). 2) Calls unstake with isSourceNative = true. 3) The contract pays out the same numeric amount in native wei, which is worth orders of magnitude more. 4) Attacker repeats until the native reserve is empty.
preconditions: the bridge supports a non-native token and native withdrawal

title: BaseVault.execute(..) transactions can be replayed.
exploit_path: 1) Attacker observes a signed execute() transaction. 2) Replays the same signed payload (no nonce/domain separation). 3) The vault executes the transfer again.
preconditions: a valid signed execute payload

title: Hydrofoil.sol: bankruptcyLiquidateLong() can be called several times on a long position
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls bankruptcyLiquidateLong on a long position. 2) The position is not marked as already liquidated, so the call can be repeated. 3) Each call pays the liquidation reward again.
preconditions: a bankrupt long position

title: Any token with large volume ﬂash minting capability can be stolen
exploit_path: 1) Attacker flash-mints a large amount of a token with minting capability. 2) Uses the inflated balance to satisfy a check or skew a redemption calculation. 3) Redeems/withdraws more than entitled, repays the flash mint, keeps the difference.
preconditions: a flash-mintable token is supported

title: Auction token collection not tracked enables stealing ERC-1155 tokens
entry_point: auction settle with an untracked ERC-1155 collection
value_at_risk: ERC-1155 tokens held by the auction contract
exploit_path: 1) Attacker lists or bids on an auction whose token collection is not recorded. 2) Settlement pays out based on the untracked collection, so the attacker can claim tokens from another auction/collection held by the contract.
preconditions: the auction holds multiple ERC-1155 collections

title: WrapTransaction.sol - Attacker can transfer native tokens from the contract without any limitation
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls scatterEthers(recipients=[attacker], values=[contractBalance]). 2) The function only checks that the total is <= msg.sender.balance, not msg.value. 3) It then sends values[i] from the contract to each recipient, so the contract's native balance is paid to the attacker.
preconditions: the contract holds native tokens

title: Source-chain compose injection on the destination adapter FIXED AS OF 6820a6dd
entry_point: compose message on the source chain
value_at_risk: bridged USDT0 and strategy funds on the destination adapter
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sends a source-chain compose message with attacker-controlled payload. 2) The destination adapter decodes the compose payload without binding it to the sender/intent. 3) The injected call executes on the destination adapter, moving bridged funds to the attacker.
preconditions: attacker can send a compose message; destination adapter funded

title: Order Creation Without Locking of Jettons
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates an order without locking the jetton that backs it. 2) A filler accepts and fills the order, paying out the destination asset. 3) The attacker's side never settles, so the filler loses the payout.
preconditions: a filler is willing to fill the order

title: Wrong Order of Operations Leads to Exponentiation of rewardPerTokenStored
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes just before a reward update. 2) Wrong order of operations exponentiates rewardPerTokenStored instead of adding. 3) The inflated rate pays the attacker far more than the intended emissions.
preconditions: a reward period update occurs while the attacker is staked

title: Inflation attack
exploit_path: 1) Attacker is the first depositor and mints 1 share. 2) Directly transfers a large amount of the underlying to the vault, inflating the asset-per-share ratio. 3) Later depositors get 0 shares due to rounding. 4) Attacker redeems the single share for the whole pool.
preconditions: vault is empty or nearly empty

title: transferFrom does not decrease allowance, enabling spender to drain holder balance after single approval
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves the attacker for 1 token. 2) transferFrom does not decrease the allowance. 3) Attacker calls transferFrom repeatedly until the victim's balance is empty.
preconditions: any approval, however small

title: C01. Signature Replay Attack Can Led to Unlimited Deposits
value_at_risk: the depositor's credited balance / delivered assets
exploit_path: 1) Attacker obtains one valid backend signature. 2) Calls deposit() repeatedly with the same signature; there is no nonce or payment-id tracking. 3) Each call credits a deposit and emits a Delivery event, so the attacker is credited multiple times for one authorization.
preconditions: a valid signature within its deadline

title: Incorrect Parsing of Token Path Between Gearbox and Uniswap
exploit_path: 1) Attacker supplies a path tokenA, fee, tokenB, tokenC. 2) Gearbox reads only the first and last 20 bytes (tokenA, tokenC) for its collateral check. 3) Uniswap executes tokenA->tokenB and ignores tokenC, so the health check is performed on a token that was never traded. 4) Attacker uses a fake ERC20/malicious pool to make the check pass while extracting real value.
preconditions: borrower can supply an arbitrary swap path; a fake token is accepted

title: Miscalculated deltaScore Allows Malicious Users Earning Rewards For Free
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits and locks. 2) Calls _withdraw immediately; deltaScore is computed from elapsed time since lock instead of the full locked period. 3) The deducted score is far too small, so the attacker keeps accruing rewards as if still staked while the principal is out.
preconditions: reward pool funded

title: Lack of Cancellation Status Update in cancelGame() Function
value_at_risk: all native tokens held by BlockPaperScissors
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates a game and waits past the reveal deadline with no opponent. 2) Calls cancelGame(), which refunds player1 but does not set a cancelled/winner status. 3) Calls cancelGame() again and again; each call pays the refund from the contract's balance. 4) Drain all native tokens, including other players' stakes.
preconditions: attacker can create a game; contract holds other stakes

title: Completed listings can be re-entered
exploit_path: 1) A completed listing's state is not updated; _isListingValid only checks that the contract holds the NFT. 2) If another listing holds the same NFT, the old listing can be re-entered. 3) Attacker calls cancelListing/buyItNow/settleAuction on the stale listing and the NFT is transferred to the wrong party.
preconditions: a stale listing for an NFT the contract currently holds

title: transaction.value Is Used To Refund Invalid Burns
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls a path that invokes burn() with a small burn amount but attaches a large transaction.value. 2) burn() fails validation and refunds transaction.value instead of the actual burned amount. 3) Attacker receives the larger value.
preconditions: the refund path uses transaction.value

title: F-2023-0296 - Extended Validity of Block Hashes in XPower Contract Leads to Inflation Vulnerability
entry_point: XPower mint with an expired block hash
exploit_path: 1) Attacker reuses an old block hash that _recent() wrongly treats as valid because it compares a timestamp to an hour index. 2) Mints XPOW repeatedly with the same hash. 3) Sells the inflated supply.
preconditions: a known block hash within the mis-computed window

title: Non-Compounded Fees Can Be Stolen
value_at_risk: non-compounded fees left in the pool
exploit_path: 1) Fees accrue but are not compounded into the share price. 2) Attacker deposits after fees accrue, then withdraws, capturing a pro-rata share of the un-compounded fees without having earned them.
preconditions: fees have accrued in the pool

title: Price Manipulation of Gamma Liquidity Warehouse
exploit_path: 1) Attacker manipulates the Gamma liquidity warehouse price (spot or thin liquidity). 2) Uses the inflated collateral value to borrow or withdraw more than the true collateral backs. 3) Defaults, leaving bad debt.
preconditions: Gamma warehouse is the collateral oracle and is manipulable

title: Tokens Stolen When Completing Withdraw
