preconditions: pool has liquidity

title: Accounting error allows for arbitrary share price increase
exploit_path: 1) Deposit; totalPooled += msg.value. 2) instantUnlock before submitBatch: batchDepositRequests.assets decreases but totalPooled does not. 3) Repeat to inflate totalPooled arbitrarily. 4) convertToAssets/share price rises; redeem shares for the whole pool.
preconditions: instantUnlock enabled before submitBatch

title: Attacker can inflate his PowerToken balance by repeatedly claiming historic inflation with sync() function
exploit_path: 1) _getLastSync can be gamed: with _lastSyncs[alice] = [20,30], call sync(alice,29) repeatedly. 2) _getUnrealizedInflation computes epochs (20..29) each time; _addBalance records the event at the current epoch instead of 29. 3) The attacker repeatedly claims the same historic inflation, inflating the PowerToken balance.
preconditions: account has a sync history gap

title: Paymaster signatures can be reused
attacker: any user who obtains one paymaster signature
exploit_path: 1) A user obtains one paymaster signature; the hash covers only validUntil, validAfter, chainid, paymaster and sender. 2) Reuses it on any number of userOps with arbitrary calldata. 3) The paymaster pays gas each time; the attacker can self-bundle with a high priority fee to convert the deposit into fees.
preconditions: one valid paymaster signature; paymaster funded

title: `distribute_epoch_rewards()` can be abused to mint infinite 4real tokens
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls distribute_epoch_rewards with conversion_rate set arbitrarily high. 2) The program computes rewards_in_token = rewards_in_sol * conversion_rate / 10_000 and adds it to position.rewards_amount. 3) The attacker claims/redeems the inflated 4real or sells it into liquidity. No access control on the conversion rate.
preconditions: a staking position; function permissionless

title: Malicious lender can reuse borrower's executionData signature for profit
exploit_path: 1) Borrower signs executionData for a loan. 2) Malicious lender backruns with refinanceFromLoanExecutionData using the same signature. 3) The signature is not bound to loanId/operation/nonce, so the lender can refinance repeatedly in the same block before expiry. 4) Borrower pays lender fees multiple times; lender profits.
preconditions: attacker is the lender; a borrower signature exists

title: CamelotLiquidity.sol - Anyone can call collectAllFess to steal pool fees
value_at_risk: all uncollected fees on the strategy's Uniswap V3 positions
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls collectAllFees(tokenId) for any NFT position the strategy approved to CamelotLiquidity. 2) The function calls NonfungiblePositionManager.collect with recipient = msg.sender and amount0Max/amount1Max = max. 3) All accrued fees go to the attacker.
preconditions: tokenId has accrued fees; strategy approved the NFT to CamelotLiquidity

title: Yield Distribution Share Inflation
attacker: any user who can enter/exit around a yield distribution
exploit_path: 1) receiveYield increments yieldPerTokenStored and totalAssets. 2) The same yield is counted both in the per-token accumulator and in the share price. 3) A user who deposits before a distribution and withdraws after receives more than their entitled yield; the excess comes from other holders/protocol.
preconditions: a yield distribution occurs; attacker can enter/exit around it

title: Arbitrage Vulnerability Due to Imbalance in EMA Price
entry_point: mint hyUSD (ExchangeContext.mint_conversion) using the Pyth EMA price
exploit_path: 1) When EMA > spot by more than fees (report uses 148 vs 146), buy SOL at spot. 2) Mint hyUSD using the higher EMA valuation. 3) Sell/repay to capture the spread. 4) Repeat while the EMA lags.
preconditions: EMA-spot spread > fees; mint enabled

title: Missing Validations and Lack of Access Control
exploit_path: 1) Anyone calls transitionAll(user, minGasLimit, targetUSD, minAmountOut) for any user. 2) Attacker sets targetUSD to a poorly handled token and minAmountOut very low. 3) Front-runs the conversion to move the rate, then lets the victim's transition execute at the bad rate. 4) Captures the difference.
preconditions: transition enabled; victim has a balance

title: Wrong variable initialization leads to debt write-off and under-collateralization
value_at_risk: borrowed ReUSD plus the retained collateral
exploit_path: 1) Attacker borrows near max LTV. 2) Makes the position liquidatable with a small price move. 3) Calls liquidate; _collateralForLiquidator is initialized to itself (0), so the handler receives no collateral and processCollateral returns early without burning debt. 4) Attacker keeps the collateral and the borrowed stablecoins; debt is written off.
preconditions: position becomes liquidatable; liquidation handler wired

project: Opal Finance Protocol Smart Contract Security
title: LACK OF AUTHORIZATION CHECK IN SWAPFORGEM
value_at_risk: LP tokens held by the Omnipool and GEM rewards
exploit_path: 1) Anyone calls swapForGem(token, amountIn); it approves the Balancer vault and swaps the contract's tokens to GEM. 2) Attacker sandwiches the swap to profit from the price impact. 3) The contract's LP tokens are burned, causing loss to the pool.
preconditions: extraRewardPools configured

title: Invalid Proof Causes Early Return For Multiple Calls To mint()
attacker: any user able to submit a mint transaction
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls mint() multiple times in one transaction (for example via a multicall) with invalid pegin proofs. 2) botanix_mint_contract_checks iterates the logs; on the first invalid proof it returns Err early, so later mint events are not validated and their balances are not decremented. 3) The later mints credit the attacker with BTC that is not backed.
preconditions: multiple mint calls in one tx; at least one invalid proof

title: Bids only transfer collateral for the first token type
exploit_path: 1) Bidder submits a bid with a tiny amount of token A and a large amount of token B. 2) Bid validation sums collateral across all tokens and accepts. 3) The lock path only processes and transfers the first token (A). 4) The borrower is undercollateralized; defaults and keeps the loan.
preconditions: multi-token collateral accepted; lock path takes only the first token

title: [C-03] Premium could be stolen by fixed side participant
exploit_path: 1) Fixed-side participant withdraws ongoing during the vault. 2) The vault ends with zero earnings; variable holders burn for nothing. 3) The fixed participant later finalizes the ongoing withdrawals and then withdraws the variable share, capturing the premium.
preconditions: vault ends with zero earnings; fixed participant has an ongoing withdrawal

title: [C-02] Wrong index used when updating rates
attacker: any user of the affected market
exploit_path: 1) The loop extracts token = tokens[i] but calls the rate function with tokens[t] (the loop index) instead of tokens[token]. 2) A rate for the wrong token is stored. 3) Attacker trades/borrows against the corrupted rate.
preconditions: multiple tokens; rate update runs

title: [C-01] Uniswap v3 launch can be enabled without raising enough ETH
value_at_risk: the raise ETH and the Uniswap pool
exploit_path: 1) Attacker buys about 8.2M tokens to push unitPrice over thresholdPrice before enough ETH is raised. 2) Launch is committed and further buys are disabled; liquidity is funded from other tokens' ETH. 3) Attacker sells into the underfunded pool or exits before insolvency.
preconditions: launch gate reachable; attacker has capital

title: [C-01] Attacker can drain all ETH from IPSeed due to re-configuring `tokenId`
value_at_risk: all ETH in the IPSeed contract
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates/configures a tokenId with projectId still empty, setting only the Curve address and zeroed parameters, which yields a zero buy price. 2) Mints an arbitrary amount for free. 3) Reconfigures the same tokenId with real parameters. 4) Sells the minted tokens back to the curve, draining the contract's ETH.
preconditions: projectId remains empty; partial configuration allowed

title: User-controlled refund list allows sweeping any ERC20 balances held by the zap contract High impact finding
value_at_risk: any ERC20 balance held by the zap contract
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls zapIn with a minimal benign action and lists any token in assetsToRefundToSender. 2) The loop transfers the contract's entire balance of each listed token to currentZapSender. 3) Sweep leftovers from prior users or accidental transfers.
preconditions: zap contract holds stray balances

title: MetaVault Improperly Handles Last Redeem Claim Shortfalls
value_at_risk: the shortfall borne by later depositors
exploit_path: 1) A last-redeem shortfall occurs; claimAllocations accepts less than expected. 2) The share rate drops for the full shortfall. 3) Pending withdrawals were priced at the old rate; an attacker who withdraws before the drop exits at the stale rate, and future depositors fill the gap.
preconditions: a shortfall occurs; attacker can exit before the rate drop

title: Anyone who is approving BlueprintV5 con- tract to spend ERC20 can get drained because Payment::payWithERC20
value_at_risk: all ERC20 approvals granted to BlueprintV5
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves BlueprintV5 for payments. 2) Attacker calls payWithERC20(token, amount, victim, attacker). 3) safeTransferFrom pulls the victim's tokens to the attacker.
preconditions: victim has an outstanding approval to BlueprintV5

title: Incorrect assumption that one (1) Pendle Standard Yield (SY) token is equal to one (1) Yield To- ken when computing the price in the oracle
exploit_path: 1) For SY tokens whose redemption is below 1:1, 1 SY is not equal to 1 yield token. 2) The oracle multiplies the yield-token price by getPtToSyRate, overvaluing PT collateral. 3) Attacker deposits such PT and borrows against the inflated value.
preconditions: useSyOracleRate = true; SY with fee/slippage

title: No Token Separation Leading to Cross-Asset Withdrawal
value_at_risk: all underlying tokens in the wrapper
exploit_path: 1) Deposit TokenA and receive generic 18-decimal wrapped tokens. 2) Withdraw the same amount in TokenB (more valuable). 3) No per-token accounting prevents it; drain the more valuable reserves.
preconditions: wrapper in use (client says it is not)

title: Yield Theft via Permissionless Pool Creation Using Existing Vault Wrappers
value_at_risk: all pending yield in any vault wrapper
exploit_path: 1) Create a pool with assetB = the victim's vault wrapper. 2) Add minimal liquidity. 3) Swap on the pool; harvestAndDistributeYield calls pendingYield/harvest on the victim wrapper and donates the yield to the attacker's pool. 4) Remove liquidity and collect the donated yield as fees.
preconditions: a vault wrapper with pending yield exists

title: Decompression doesn't compare amounts for most cases, allowing escaping frozen state and stealing by delegate
attacker: a delegate with a tiny delegation
exploit_path: 1) Victim has 10K USDC compressed and delegates 1 USDC to the attacker. 2) Attacker calls transfer2 with a 1-ctoken account owned by the victim (0 transferred) and a second account owned by the attacker. 3) Decompression compares amounts only for ATA/compress-to-pubkey, so the rest of the 10K flows to the attacker.
preconditions: attacker is a delegate; compressed account is decompressed

title: Unreported realized losses let early USD3 withdrawers exit at a stale share
value_at_risk: the loss borne by remaining USD3 holders
exploit_path: 1) A borrower default is settled in MorphoCredit, reducing recoverable assets. 2) Until USD3.report(), redeem/withdraw still price shares with the stale totalAssets. 3) Attacker redeems before the report, receiving more than the post-loss pro-rata share; remaining holders absorb the loss.
preconditions: a realized loss exists; attacker holds USD3; report not yet called

title: Wallet Linking Trusts Client-Side Party Ownership Checks
value_at_risk: a Canton party identity and the assets it controls
exploit_path: 1) Authenticated user posts an arbitrary unclaimed party_id with provider canton-config. 2) The backend persists it without verifying ownership. 3) The attacker controls another party's identity in the app, potentially its Canton assets.
preconditions: KYC account; unclaimed party_id

title: Missing permissions check in withdraw and redeem functions in ERC4626i.sol
entry_point: ERC4626i.withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner) and ERC4626i.redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner), ERC4626i.sol#L457/L468
value_at_risk: All underlying assets in every ERC4626i vault; any holder's share balance
exploit_path: 1) Find a victim holding ERC4626i shares; 2) call redeem(victimShares, attacker, victim) (or withdraw(assets, attacker, victim)); 3) the custom implementation omits the solmate allowance check when msg.sender != owner; 4) victim shares are burned and underlying is sent to attacker; 5) repeat across vaults/owners.
preconditions: Victim holds shares; no approval from victim required

title: Missing Access Control In TermMorphoInterfaceFacet Allows Unauthorised Position Manipulation
entry_point: TermMorphoInterfaceFacet.morphoWithdraw/morphoBorrow/morphoSupplyCollateral (all functions except morphoSetAuthorizationWithSig lack caller validation)
value_at_risk: Morpho positions of users who authorized the Term facet; Morpho liquidation bonuses
exploit_path: 1) Victim authorizes the facet for normal Term use; 2) attacker calls morphoBorrow on the victim to max, directing borrowed funds to the facet; 3) the position is pushed toward liquidation; 4) attacker (or a partner) liquidates the now-unhealthy Morpho position and collects the liquidation bonus. Report also describes combining with TRF-51 to credit withdrawn user funds to an attacker-controlled aaveSupply position.
preconditions: Victim has authorized the facet; attacker needs liquidation capital and a liquidatable price move

title: TVL errors by including pending withdrawal assets
value_at_risk: Deposit pool TVL; all elyAsset holders
exploit_path: 1) Request withdrawal of X elyAssets: shares are burned immediately and the backing assets move to the unstaking vault; 2) getTotalAssetTVL still counts the unstaking vault balance, so TVL is unchanged while supply fell; 3) price = TVL/supply spikes; 4) withdraw remaining elyAssets at the inflated price (report example: 4e18 shares redeem 15e18 HYPE); 5) repeat with multiple accounts.
preconditions: Attacker holds elyAssets; a pending withdrawal (theirs or another user's) creates the supply/TVL mismatch

title: Wrong‑Offset Ed25519 instruction introspection enables forged approvals
entry_point: Enclave borrow instruction; previous-instruction Ed25519 introspection (Ed25519SignatureOffsets)
value_at_risk: Pool liquidity; unauthorized borrows against off-chain approvals
exploit_path: 1) Build a transaction whose previous instruction is a native Ed25519 verification with attacker-chosen offsets/instruction indexes; 2) place the expected signer pubkey, message hash, and signature bytes at the ranges Enclave later reads; 3) call borrow; 4) Enclave does not check the previous program_id, inline mode (0xFFFF), or offset bounds, so it accepts the forged approval; 5) borrow pool funds without the signer; 6) default or keep the funds, and the victim's nonce is consumed.
preconditions: Pool has borrowable liquidity; borrow path accepts off-chain approval via instruction introspection

title: Unauthorized Session Key Takeover via Missing Ownership Vali- dation
value_at_risk: Tokens locked under an active session key (lockedTokens tracked by session key, not wallet)
exploit_path: 1) Observe a victim's active session key/resourceLock; 2) call enableSessionKey with the same resourceLock; 3) sessionKeyToWallet[resourceLock.sessionKey] = msg.sender overwrites the owner because there is no existing-registration check; 4) claim the tokens the legitimate owner locked under that session key; 5) victim permanently loses the session.
preconditions: Victim has an active session key; attacker can read the resourceLock parameters

title: Invariant Violation and Fund Drainage Due to Axis Mismatch in PeggedSwap
entry_point: PeggedSwap._peggedSwapGrowPriceRange2D via swap (reverse direction, tokenIn > tokenOut)
value_at_risk: Aqua pool reserves, especially pools with asymmetric capacities
exploit_path: 1) Find a PeggedSwap pool with asymmetric capacities (report example: A capacity 1,000,000, B capacity 1,000); 2) swap the scarce token B for the abundant token A (reverse direction); 3) the code sets local x0=balanceB but normalizes by config.x0=capacityA; 4) the computed invariant is ~31.65 instead of 2.0; 5) the solver outputs a massive amount of A for a small amount of B; 6) sell/exit and repeat.
preconditions: Pool deployed with asymmetric capacities; reverse-direction swap enabled

title: Attacker can exploit the callback of the swapRouter to execute another swap request to steal the input token
value_at_risk: Input tokens of pending signed swap executions; receiver's output token
exploit_path: 1) Observe two signed swapExecs in the mempool that share the same receiver and output token; 2) frontrun the winning transmitter and call executeSR with the first calldata (the signature is valid, and exclusiveTransmitter is not checked against msg.sender); 3) msg.sender becomes the transmitter and controls the callback; 4) inside swapRequestCallback, reenter executeSR with the second exec; 5) pay the output once, but the pre/post balance check counts the first transfer, so both input amounts are released to the attacker; 6) receiver gets only the larger output.
preconditions: Two pending signed swaps with the same receiver/output token; mempool visibility

title: Price deviation for calm period detection is done by exponentiating, not mul-
value_at_risk: Strategy vault liquidity in Uniswap V3 pools
exploit_path: 1) Choose a pool whose twapPrice is far from 1 on a log scale (report example DAI/USDC at ~1e-12); 2) onlyCalmPeriods compares ticks multiplicatively, allowing up to ~31.8% deviation at d=1%; 3) flash-loan/manipulate the Uniswap price within that band; 4) deposit or harvest at the manipulated price; 5) unwind and drain part of the strategy's value. Report estimates profitability when strategy liquidity is >=~0.001 of other LPs (or 0.01 at 2.06% deviation).
preconditions: Manipulable Uniswap V3 pool; strategy liquidity relative to pool; flash loan

title: MoneyBrinter susceptible to stealth deposit
value_at_risk: Subsequent depositors' assets in the ERC-4626 vault
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits 1 share; 2) calls depositFor(address(vault), largeAmount) to inflate totalAssets without minting shares; 3) a victim deposit computes shares=0 because assets*(supply+offset) < totalAssets+1; 4) the vault still pulls the victim's assets; 5) attacker redeems the sole share and captures the donation plus the victim's deposit.
preconditions: Attacker is first depositor; a victim deposits afterwards

title: SharePrice can get manipulated

preconditions: Curve pool with enough liquidity to move spot; pending withdrawal; capital/flash loan

title: Reshu ing Gateway Assets Can Be Drained via Share Transfer FIXED AS OF 8392c1b3
value_at_risk: All recovered assets held in the ReshufflingGateway
exploit_path: 1) Call claimReshufflingGateway as a shareholder; 2) _hasClaimedReshufflingGateway[account] is set but the vault shares are never burned or locked; 3) transfer the shares to a fresh address; 4) call claimReshufflingGateway again; 5) repeat until the gateway's balance is drained.
preconditions: Attacker holds any vault shares; gateway is funded with recovered assets

title: Unauthorized Refund Due to Lack of Access Control
value_at_risk: Funds locked in Mayan TON order contracts
exploit_path: 1) Craft a SubRefund message with attacker-controlled trader/tokenIn/recipient/canceler/fee fields; 2) router_internal processes op::SubRefund without checking that the message sender is the order owner; 3) the order is refunded to the attacker's recipient; 4) repeat for open orders in status CREATED.
preconditions: An order exists in CREATED status; attacker can send the internal message

title: withdraw_collateral Ignores Open Position Locks, Enabling Uncollateralized Debt
entry_point: ReceiptVault.withdraw(user, ptoken_amount) called directly, bypassing MarginController.withdraw_collateral
value_at_risk: Collateral in Peridot receipt vaults; bad debt absorbed by liquidity providers
exploit_path: 1) Open a leveraged position (e.g. deposit 1,000 USDC, borrow 4,000, swap to ETH, deposit ETH); 2) pTokens for the USDC deposit are minted to the user, not the controller; 3) call ReceiptVault.withdraw(user, full pUSDC balance) directly; 4) the vault only checks user.require_auth() and a peridottroller health check that sees no local debt or sufficient pETH cross-collateral; 5) withdraw the 1,000 USDC collateral while the 4,000 debt remains; 6) default.
preconditions: Open position; markets not entered or pETH covers the debt; attacker keeps borrowed funds

title: ProxyAssetManager Single-Vault Binding Permanently Strands Swap-Sibling Funds
value_at_risk: vault_B principal; vault_A shareholders receive an unbacked windfall
exploit_path: 1) Operator configures vault_A and vault_B with the same ProxyAssetManager (required for swap_tokens); 2) vault_B deposits and later requests withdrawal; 3) return_funds reads the single stored vault_A and transfers all liquidity to vault_A, crediting vault_A.total_idle; 4) an attacker who holds vault_A shares before the return can redeem a pro-rata share of vault_B's misrouted funds. The attacker cannot trigger the misrouting; it happens in normal operation.
preconditions: Two-vault configuration; attacker holds vault_A shares at the time of a return_funds

title: BLS Rogue Key Attack Allows Executing Arbitrary Transactions
entry_point: BLS wallet processBundle(); wallet creation with forged BLS public key = -victim pubkey; aggregate signature verification
exploit_path: 1) Read the victim wallet's BLS public key on-chain; 2) create a wallet whose public key is the negation of the victim's; 3) aggregate public keys cancel to the point at infinity; 4) submit a bundle with a zero aggregate signature; 5) the verifier accepts it and executes arbitrary operations, including transferring the victim's assets.
preconditions: Victim wallet public key is on-chain; bundle verification does not reject rogue keys

title: [C-01] Anyone can steal all HoneyJar NFTs in HoneyJarPortal and exploit its allowances
value_at_risk: All NFTs owned by the portal or approved to it; ERC-20 allowances granted to the portal
exploit_path: 1) Call sendFrom with _from=HoneyJarPortal (or a victim) and to=attacker; 2) _debitFrom transfers based only on the supplied _from, without checking that msg.sender owns the token or is approved; 3) drain every NFT held/approved by the portal; 4) use the portal's allowances to pull ERC-20s.
preconditions: Portal holds or is approved for NFTs/tokens

title: You can deposit and withdraw simultaneously in the same block to manipulate exchangerate
entry_point: Omnipool deposit + LP token transfer + withdraw in the same block
exploit_path: 1) Deposit from address A; 2) immediately transfer the LP tokens to address B; 3) call withdraw from B in the same block; 4) the per-address same-block restriction is bypassed because the restriction follows the address, not the LP position; 5) manipulate exchangeRate and extract value from the pool.
preconditions: LP tokens are transferable; same-block deposit/withdraw

title: `RebaseReward` fails because of incorrect token handling
entry_point: RebaseReward.incentivize(address token, uint256 amount) + RebaseReward.getRewardForTokenId(uint256 tokenId)
value_at_risk: KITTEN rewards allocated to other veKitten holders
exploit_path: 1) Attacker holds a veKitten NFT; 2) sends 1 wei of a whitelisted non-KITTEN token via incentivize; 3) at epoch notification, _getReward deposits KITTEN for the tokenId; 4) attacker claims first and consumes the KITTEN earmarked for other tokenIds; 5) other holders' claims revert for lack of KITTEN.
preconditions: veKitten position; a whitelisted non-KITTEN token; reward epoch

title: Uniswap oracle manipulation to buy for a lower price

exploit_path: 1) Flash-loan referenceToken; 2) sell it into the Uniswap V2 pair to crash its price; 3) mint TokenBox paying paymentToken at the manipulated low reference price; 4) repay the flash loan; 5) sell or hold the cheaply acquired TokenBox.
preconditions: Manipulable Uniswap V2 pair; flash loan; TokenBox has value

title: Missing MOD_HASH validation
entry_point: Chia SEND_MESSAGE/RECEIVE_MESSAGE; statutes mutation; recharge auction

title: The `transferFrom()` in `OmoRouter.sol` has approval vulnerabilities
entry_point: OmoRouter.transferFrom(uint256 vaultId, address from, address to, uint256 amount)
value_at_risk: Any user's vault shares approved to the OmoRouter
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves the router to spend vault shares; 2) attacker calls transferFrom(vaultId, victim, attacker, allowance); 3) the router sub-calls OmoVault.transferFrom(from, to, amount) without checking that from == msg.sender; 4) the vault moves the victim's shares to the attacker; 5) attacker redeems.

title: Calling TermMaxMarket.setLsf leaks value to attackers via a sandwich attack

title: Inﬂation Attack Steals First Deposit

title: Broken access control in DestinationVaultMainRewarder:: getReward allows destination vault rewarders to be drained
entry_point: DestinationVaultMainRewarder.getReward(address account, address recipient, bool claimExtras), line 75
value_at_risk: All destination-vault rewards (WETH) held by the rewarders; report fork test estimates ~1-3 WETH per affected block
exploit_path: 1) Pick a victim account with earned rewards; 2) call getReward(victim, attacker, true); 3) the guard is `if (msg.sender != account && msg.sender != recipient) revert`; because msg.sender == recipient, the condition is false and the call proceeds; 4) rewards are migrated/claimed to the attacker; 5) loop over all rewarders and both balETH/autoETH accounts.
preconditions: Rewarder holds rewards; no allowance or role

title: Reentrancy in withdrawals
entry_point: EscrowBase.withdraw(address token, uint256 amount, bool unwrap)
value_at_risk: WETH held in the Bracket Fi escrow
exploit_path: 1) Deposit a small amount to have a usersBalance; 2) call withdraw(token, amount, unwrap=true); 3) the function unwraps WETH and sends ETH via msg.sender.call{value: amount} before decrementing usersBalance; 4) reenter withdraw from the ETH receive hook; 5) the unchecked balance subtraction underflows instead of reverting; 6) drain the contract's WETH.

title: Locked shares have undue access to historical rewards
value_at_risk: Historical USDC rewards already distributed by VeTranche
exploit_path: 1) Wait until rewards have been distributed (rewardsDistributedPerSharePerLockPoint > 0); 2) lock shares; 3) lastSharePoint[id] is uninitialized (0), not set to the current global index; 4) unlock/claim immediately; 5) the position is credited a share of all historical rewards, making later claimants underfunded.
preconditions: Rewards already distributed; attacker can lock shares

title: Unauthorized Withdrawal of Staked ETH via repayWithStakeToken Function
entry_point: repayWithStakeToken(uint256 poolId, uint256 stakeId, uint256 fee) (BlastOff staking)
value_at_risk: All ETH staked under any stakeId

exploit_path: 1) Use a token with a transfer hook (ERC777/callback); 2) call deposit; 3) shares are minted before transferFrom completes; 4) in the token callback, reenter deposit; 5) the second mint is based on the pre-transfer balance and over-mints; 6) withdraw/drain the pod.
preconditions: Pod accepts a reentrant token; attacker holds that token

title: Attackers can double their tokens by using locked deposits

exploit_path: Front-run the deployment and call the unprotected initialize() to grant yourself admin and upgrader roles.

exploit_path: amountOutMin is effectively unset, so the streamer swap can be sandwiched for the full slippage.

preconditions: capital to shape the contract balance; ability to land the last tx

title: Controller can overpay staked-asset redemptions when the share price exceeds 1
entry_point: Controller.verifyOrder() and Controller.redeem() on orders whose asset_token == stakedAsset
value_at_risk: AssetToken collateral paid out against StakedAsset redemptions (the redeeming side's backing pool); report does not state TVL
exploit_path:
1. Acquire X staked shares (StakedAsset) after convertToAssets(1e18) > 1e18, i.e. after rewards accrue.
2. Submit a redeem order with asset_amount = X (interpreted as shares by verifyOrder) so the order is priced at X * sharePrice underlying.
3. redeem() calls instantUnstake(order.asset_amount, payer, payer), which consumes X underlying assets, not X shares - only X/sharePrice shares are actually unwound.
4. Controller burns only order.asset_amount - assetFee asset tokens while the payer is paid collateral for the full X * sharePrice value, so the payer keeps the residual shares.
5. Repeat or sell the residual staking position; the loss lands on the protocol's asset-token backing.
preconditions: StakedAsset share price > 1 (any reward accrual); attacker holds redeemable staked shares; redeem path enabled

title: ERC-6492 allows draining of any wallet with SpendPermissionManager
value_at_risk: All assets in any SmartWallet that has a SpendPermissionManager set as owner
exploit_path:
1. Pick a victim SmartWallet that has a SpendPermissionManager as an owner and holds funds.
2. Craft a SpendPermission with account = an undeployed counterfactual address, spender = attacker.
3. Wrap it in the ERC-6492 magicWrapper; set prepareTo/factory to the victim wallet and prepareData to executeBatch(drain victim, deploy the counterfactual signer contract).
4. Call SpendPermissionManager.approveWithSignature(). SignatureCheckerLib sees no code at the signer, calls the attacker-supplied factory (the victim wallet's executeBatch), which drains the wallet and deploys the attacker's signer contract.
5. The ERC-6492 check then validates the signature against the freshly deployed attacker contract; the permission is approved and the attacker spends the allowance.
preconditions: Victim wallet deployed with a SpendPermissionManager owner (standard Coinbase Smart Wallet config); victim funded; attacker pays gas and deploys a throwaway signer per exploit

title: Cross-Function Reentrancy Allowing Drainage of the Reward Vault
value_at_risk: Shared reward vault (ETH) funding all delegator and validator rewards
exploit_path:
1. Deploy a contract, register it as a delegator and stake the minimum weight; wait out the minimum staking duration.
2. Call claimDelegatorRewards(); _reward() sends ETH to the attacker before lastRewardClaimTime/lastClaimUptimeSeconds are written.
3. In receive(), re-enter initiateDelegatorRemoval(); the removal path recalculates rewards from the still-stale timestamps and stores them in _redeemableDelegatorRewards.
4. Call completeDelegatorRemoval() to be paid the stored rewards a second time for the same window.
5. Amplify with many delegator positions (the report describes this) to drain the shared reward vault.
preconditions: Delegator registration available to the attacker (the report PoC registers an attacker contract); minimum stake and staking duration; reward vault funded

title: Possibility to use fraudulent Raydium pool to stake worthless LP Tokens and receive staking rewards for legitimate token
entry_point: stake instruction (programs/watt/src/instructions/stake.rs), RaydiumCPMMAccounts in remaining accounts
value_at_risk: Staking reward emissions for legitimate pairs (e.g. WattBONK/USDC)
exploit_path:
1. Create a worthless token (SCAM), wrap it to WattSCAM, create a WattSCAM/USDC Raydium CPMM pool and become the sole LP.
2. Call stake() with the legitimate WattBONK stake-context accounts but pass the WattSCAM/USDC pool accounts in the RaydiumCPMMAccounts remaining accounts.
3. The program never checks that the staked LP mint belongs to the pool implied by watt_mint, so user.liquidity for WattBONK increases.
4. Collect staking rewards for the legitimate pair while the staked LP is worthless.
5. Repeat with fresh pools; rewards are paid out of the shared emission pool.
preconditions: Attacker can create a Raydium CPMM pool permissionlessly; staking emissions active; no capital beyond a dust USDC side

title: Rewards can be stolen by transferring tokens to oneself
value_at_risk: Rewards held by ResolvStakingV2 for all stakers
exploit_path:
1. Stake into ResolvStakingV2.
2. Transfer the staked balance to yourself: _update() applies a negative checkpoint for the sender, then a positive checkpoint for the receiver before balanceOf is updated.
3. The second checkpoint reads balanceOf(user) at the pre-transfer (higher) value, so updateEffectiveBalance overstates the user's effective balance.
4. Repeat self-transfers to keep inflating effectiveBalance, then claim rewards at the inflated weight.
5. Other stakers receive proportionally less; in the limit the attacker takes all available rewards.
preconditions: Transfer enabled; staking rewards funded; attacker holds any staked balance

title: Attacker can steal all funds by repaying already repaid loans
value_at_risk: All lending-pool funds and NFT collateral held by the protocol
exploit_path:
1. Take a loan against an NFT and repay it normally (loan now has borrowedAmount == 0 but still resolves).
2. Take a new loan.
3. Call repay() with the OLD loan id; repayAmount is capped to borrowedAmount = 0, the loan is marked repaid and the NFT collateral for the old loan is returned again (BeraBond version needs a 1 wei msg.value to pass the zero-amount check).
4. Repeat steps 2-3: each cycle extracts an NFT for free / re-withdraws collateral while the protocol's funds back the new loan.
5. Iterate until the pool is drained.
preconditions: Attacker has one NFT to seed the cycle; lending pool funded; repay() accepts already-repaid loan ids

title: Incorrect comparison in claimRewards allows referrers to double-claim session rewards
value_at_risk: Referral reward pool held by SessionManager
exploit_path:
1. Register as a referrer (permissionless) and accumulate referral rewards across sessions 2, 3, 4.
2. Call claimRewards([2,3,4]); the loop uses sessionIds[i] < lastSessionId, so the stored checkpoint becomes the MINIMUM id (2) instead of the maximum (4).
3. Sessions 3 and 4 remain claimable; call claimRewards again with [3,4] and receive the same rewards repeatedly.
4. Drain the referral reward pool; honest referrers are left unpaid.
preconditions: Referrer registration; finished sessions with referral rewards; checkpoint logic as reported

title: Missing Check of Claim Destination Address in smartcontract.go
entry_point: SmartContract.ClaimAll(ctx, beneficiary) - permissionless, pays the signer
value_at_risk: All vested GINI tokens across every beneficiary's allocations
exploit_path:
1. Obtain a beneficiary address (it is a caller-supplied argument to ClaimAll; beneficiary identities need not be secret).
2. Call ClaimAll(beneficiary = victim) from the attacker's own identity.
3. The chaincode computes totalClaimAmount from the victim's vesting list, then calls TransferGiniTokens(ctx, signer, amount) with signer = GetUserId(ctx) = attacker.
4. There is no check that signer == beneficiary or that the beneficiary approved the signer, so the vested tokens are paid to the attacker.
5. Repeat for every beneficiary with claimable allocations.
preconditions: Vesting allocations exist and are claimable; attacker can submit a Fabric transaction (any enrolled identity)

title: The redeemShort function is available before the pool is closed
value_at_risk: Pool collateral / payoutToken reserves backing short positions
exploit_path:
1. Hold short-token shares in a pool that has not yet closed.
2. Call redeemShort() before the pool closes, when balanceChangePerShare is still 0.
3. payout = (cap - 0) * collateralMinted / relativeAmount, i.e. the maximum possible payout, and the caller's short shares are burned.
4. The caller receives the maximum payout early; the pool is left under-collateralised for the eventual close and for other short holders.
preconditions: Pool not yet closed; attacker holds short shares; payoutToken liquidity in the pool

title: Native funds are incorrectly transferred to the caller
entry_point: currency.rs transfer() - pays msg.sender instead of the `to` argument; reached from auction/mod.rs refund path
value_at_risk: Outbid bidders' escrowed native refunds; auction proceeds and royalties
exploit_path:
1. Find an auction with an existing bidder whose funds are escrowed.
2. Outbid them by the minimum increment; the outbid path calls transfer(to = previous bidder) but the helper pays msg.sender = attacker.
3. The attacker receives the previous bidder's refund on top of their own bid being escrowed.
4. Repeat across auctions; the same bug misdirects the winning bid and royalties to whoever triggers settlement.
preconditions: Active auction with an escrowed bid; attacker can outbid; native-token (AZERO) auctions

title: User can steal funds of other token depositors
value_at_risk: WETH held by the bonding curve from later buyers (report PoC: 2.99 ETH pool, 1.597 ETH stolen)
exploit_path:
1. Be the first buyer: buy a small amount of the token at the initial price (PoC: 0.089 WETH).
2. Wait for other users to buy up the curve toward MAX_WETH_RESERVE (PoC victim buys 2.9 WETH across several buys).
3. Sell the entire token balance just before the launch threshold; the curve pays out 1.686 WETH for a 0.089 WETH investment.
4. The last buyers are left with a claim on WETH that the contract no longer holds (PoC victim recovers 1.303 of 2.9 ETH).
preconditions: Attacker is early in the curve; later buyers add WETH; sell is enabled before DEX launch

title: Multiple Account Ownership Validation Vulnerabilities Across Pool Creation, Contribution, and Staking Systems Enable Fee Diversion and Unauthorized Access
value_at_risk: Launchpad pool allocations (free tokens) and staking-tier benefits; platform fee revenue
exploit_path:
1. contribute_usd1: pass your own token account as pool_usd1_vault and treasury_usd1_account; the program only checks the mint, not ownership, so the 'contribution' never reaches the pool but the contribution is recorded.
2. stake_usd1: pass your own account as usd1_staking_vault, so stake_usd1 records a stake without transferring tokens, granting higher allocation tiers.
3. Claim the pool allocation funded by honest contributors.
4. Optionally create pools with your own treasury accounts so fees return to you.
preconditions: Pool live with honest contributions; attacker can create token accounts with the expected mint

title: Aave and Lendle strategies allow unauthorized withdraws
value_at_risk: Entire BrinkVault TVL supplied through the strategies
exploit_path:
1. Call AaveStrategy.withdraw(type(uint256).max) directly from an EOA.
2. The strategy approves the reserve and calls IAave.withdraw(asset, _assetAmount, msg.sender) - the recipient is the caller, not the vault.
3. Aave redeems the strategy's aTokens and sends the underlying to the attacker.
4. Repeat against LendleStrategy and any other vault using these strategies until the strategy balance is empty.
preconditions: Strategy holds supplied assets; withdraw is externally callable

title: Raw Token Amounts Aggregated In Module-Level Reward Split
value_at_risk: Reward split between Symbiotic and EigenLayer adapters (protocol reward budget)
exploit_path:
1. Stake in a vault belonging to the module whose raw token units dominate the committee sum (e.g. an 18-decimal token in a committee with a 6-decimal token).
2. When distributeRewards() runs, the module split is computed from summed raw balances, so the over-weighted module receives a disproportionate share.
3. The attacker, as a staker in that module, captures above-fair rewards; the other module's stakers are diluted.
This is a yield misallocation, not a principal theft.
preconditions: Committee contains heterogeneous assets/decimals; attacker can stake in the favoured vault

title: C01. Investors funds can be drained using FrictionlessTransferManager
value_at_risk: All ERC-20 tokens that investors have approved to the TransferManager
exploit_path:
1. Deploy a malicious ERC-3643 token and register yourself as its agent (the attacker controls the token's compliance rules).
2. Create/accept a transfer offer where the malicious token is one side and a victim's approved token is the other.
3. confirmTransferOffer() only checks that msg.sender is an agent for one of the traded tokens; with the attacker as agent of their own token, the check passes.
4. The manager pulls the victim's tokens (previously approved to it) as the counterparty leg and delivers them to the attacker.
5. Repeat for every approved holder.
preconditions: Victims have outstanding approvals to FrictionlessTransferManager; attacker can deploy an ERC-3643 token and self-register as agent

title: [C-02] Option NFTs can be exercised by any account
entry_point: Option exercise flow (margin account ownership not checked against the ERC721 owner)
value_at_risk: Intrinsic value of in-the-money option NFTs held by other users
exploit_path:
1. Monitor for option NFTs that are in the money (strike vs current price).
2. Call the exercise function referencing the victim's option token id; the flow never verifies that the calling margin account owns the ERC721.
3. The exercise pays the option's profit to the attacker's margin account.
4. The victim keeps an option NFT whose payoff has already been consumed.
preconditions: An ITM option exists and is exercisable; attacker has a margin account

title: FlasherFTM - Unsolicited invocation of the callback (CREAM auth bypass)
value_at_risk: Assets and approvals held by FlasherFTM; fuji positions it is authorised to operate
exploit_path:
1. Call Cream's flashLoan with receiver = FlasherFTM and initiator = FlasherFTM (Cream echoes the initiator instead of msg.sender).
2. onFlashLoan's require(msg.sender == crToken && address(this) == sender) passes.
3. FlasherFTM executes the attacker-supplied FlashLoan.Info actions as itself, bypassing the isAuthorized gate on initiateFlashloan.
4. If FlasherFTM holds tokens/approvals or is authorised in fuji contracts, the attacker directs those operations to their benefit.
preconditions: Cream/Geist crToken reachable; FlasherFTM holds value or privileged approvals; attacker controls the info struct

title: Unstake function allows full withdrawal while maintaining staking position
value_at_risk: Staking reward emissions and the staked LP pool
exploit_path:
1. Stake 1000 LP tokens; user_stake_state.lp_token_amount = 1000.
2. Call unstake(amount = 1). The instruction transfers the FULL staked amount (1000 LP) from the vault to the user but only decrements the recorded stake by 1.
3. The attacker now holds the LP tokens back and still has 999 LP recorded as staked.
4. Keep claiming rewards on the phantom stake, and repeat the partial unstake until the recorded position is drained of real backing.
preconditions: Staking live; attacker has staked LP

title: Inaccurate share price due to lack of withdrawal tracking
value_at_risk: Vault principal and rewards belonging to other depositors
exploit_path:
1. Deposit, let rewards accrue, then withdraw everything; executeWithdrawal does not update ethWithdrawn or nETHMinted.
2. The share price keeps counting the withdrawn balance as still in the vault, so the next depositor mints fewer shares than fair (report example: 0.952e18 shares for 1 ETH).
3. When that depositor later redeems, the stale ratio pays them 1.024 ETH for a 1 ETH deposit.
4. An attacker can be that second depositor (or repeat deposit/withdraw cycles) and extract the difference from the vault's remaining backing.
preconditions: At least one prior withdrawal left the counters stale; rewards accrued; attacker deposits after the withdrawal

title: Incorrect withdrawal amount computation for variable participants
value_at_risk: Vault earnings and principal reserved for other variable participants
exploit_path:
1. Be a variable participant with a bearer balance.
2. After the vault ends, call vaultEndedWithdraw(); withdrawnStakingEarnings/withdrawnFeeEarnings are not reduced while vaultEndedStakingEarnings/feeEarnings are, so totalEarnings stays overstated.
3. Each subsequent withdrawal computes a share from the inflated total, paying out more than the participant is entitled to.
4. The vault runs out of funds before all honest withdrawals are served.
preconditions: Vault ended; multiple variable participants; attacker withdraws before the shortfall is visible

title: Using Uniswap spot price is subject to manipulation
entry_point: Uniswap V3 quoter used for withdrawal, borrow, repay and liquidation valuation
value_at_risk: Margin-trading pool liquidity and other users' collateral
exploit_path:
1. Flash-borrow and swap to move the Uniswap V3 pool price of the collateral token (report PoC doubles WETH from 4,000 to 8,000 USDC).
2. Deposit 1 WETH and borrow against the manipulated quote - the PoC borrows 7,000 USDC against 1 WETH.
3. Unwind the swap, leaving the position under-collateralised by the manipulation profit.
4. Default / let liquidation fail to recover; the shortfall is socialised to the pool.
preconditions: Flash liquidity on the pool; quoter read in the same transaction; borrow cap above true collateral value

title: Attackers can steal unclaimed rewards from GlpStrategy because the accounted balance does not include unclaimed rewards
value_at_risk: Unclaimed GMX WETH rewards sitting in the strategy
exploit_path:
1. Wait until GlpStrategy has harvested-but-unclaimed GMX rewards (not reflected in _currentBalance()).
2. Flash-borrow a large amount and deposit into the YieldBox asset backed by GlpStrategy; shares are minted before the harvest increases the accounted balance, so the attacker receives more shares than fair.
3. The deposit triggers the harvest, raising the strategy balance.
4. Withdraw the shares in the same transaction and receive a disproportionate slice of the previously unclaimed rewards.
5. Repay the flash loan; the loss is borne by existing depositors.
preconditions: Unclaimed rewards present; attacker has flash liquidity; strategy deposit/withdraw in one tx

title: Malicious Actors Can Claim Users' Auction Bids
entry_point: Recharge and surplus auction puzzles (target_puzzle_hash in the solution)
value_at_risk: Pending auction bids (BYC) and auction proceeds
exploit_path:
1. Monitor the Chia mempool for a bid spend whose solution does not bind target_puzzle_hash.
2. Submit a replace-by-fee spend of the same coin with target_puzzle_hash rewritten to the attacker's puzzle.
3. If the bid wins, the attacker claims the auction proceeds; if it loses, the refund goes to the attacker instead of the bidder.
4. Cost is only the RBF fee bump, historically cents on Chia.
preconditions: Mempool visibility; RBF accepted; victim bid spend does not assert an announcement

title: Anyone can call the PeripheryPayments sweepToken() stealing the protocol fees
entry_point: PeripheryPayments.sweepToken() inherited by BunniHub (no access control)
value_at_risk: All protocol fees accumulated in BunniHub, in every token
exploit_path:
1. Call sweepToken() on BunniHub, naming the token and the attacker as recipient - no access control.
2. The function transfers the requested token balance to the attacker.
3. Repeat for every token the hub holds, including fee tokens and any user funds in flight.
preconditions: BunniHub holds a token balance

title: Dutch auctions can be used to drain honest buyers' escrowed funds from the market
value_at_risk: Escrowed buyer funds held by the marketplace
exploit_path:
1. In a Dutch auction, call bidForNFT(); the auction settles immediately but the bid is still written to bestBidForListing.
2. The Dutch flow never deletes that stored bid.
3. Before listingEnd, call cancelBidForNFT(); the function refunds the recorded best bid in full.
4. The attacker keeps the NFT and gets the purchase price back; the marketplace pays out of other buyers' escrow.
5. Repeat until the escrow is empty.
preconditions: Dutch auction listing; attacker can bid and cancel before listingEnd; marketplace holds other buyers' escrow

title: Anyone can redeem from users and take the funds
value_at_risk: Any vault shares a user has approved to OmoRouter (standard redeem flow)
exploit_path:
1. Watch the mempool for a user's redeem() transaction (or simply know that approvals to the router persist).
2. Front-run with redeem(vaultId, shares, receiver = attacker, owner = victim); the router pulls the victim's shares via transferFrom and sends the assets to the attacker.
3. The victim's own redeem reverts or returns nothing.
4. Repeat for every outstanding router allowance.
preconditions: Victim approved OmoRouter for vault shares; attacker can front-run

title: FCFSMint() Can Be Called By Anyone, Not Only By Whitelisted Users
value_at_risk: FCFS-phase NFT allocation (2 per wallet) at salePrice
exploit_path:
1. Obtain a signer signature over keccak256(msg.sender, salt) - the contract only checks the signature, not whitelist membership.
2. Call FCFSMint() from any wallet, paying salePrice, and mint up to 2 NFTs per address.
3. Repeat from many addresses to take the FCFS allocation ahead of whitelisted users.
4. Profit only if the NFT resale value exceeds salePrice.
preconditions: FCFS minting active; attacker can obtain a signer signature (the report implies the signature gate is the only check)

title: Funds may be stolen by calling onMoreFlashLoan() directly
exploit_path:
1. Call LoopStrategy.onMoreFlashLoan() directly from an attacker contract, supplying the callback parameters that the market would normally provide.
2. Because the function never checks msg.sender == market, the strategy executes the attacker's instructions as if a flash loan had occurred.
3. Use the callback to move collateral or settle a position in the attacker's favour.
4. Exit with the collateral; the market's accounting is left short.
preconditions: LoopStrategy deployed and holding collateral; callback parameters attacker-controllable

project: Uniswap v4 Periphery and Universal Router
title: Accrued Fees Can Be Stolen
value_at_risk: Accrued swap fees on every v4 position managed by PositionManager
exploit_path:
1. Pick any tokenId with accrued fees (positions are enumerable).
2. Call the increase-liquidity path with liquidity = 0 for that tokenId.
3. PositionManager calls PoolManager.modifyLiquidity; the returned delta includes the position's accrued fees, credited to the caller's delta.
4. Call take() to collect the positive delta to the attacker.
5. Repeat across positions; the position owner's fees are gone.
preconditions: Position has accrued fees; PositionManager deployed with the unguarded _increase

title: Gateway's tokens can be drained
value_at_risk: All tokens held by the gateway, including funds from other users' fulfilled redemption requests
exploit_path:
1. Call redeemInstant() with a minimal/zero redemption of your own.
2. The function transfers the gateway's ENTIRE token balance to the caller instead of only the balance delta produced by the call.
3. The attacker receives other users' pending redemption proceeds.
4. Repeat whenever the gateway is refilled.
preconditions: Gateway holds tokens from fulfilled redemption requests

title: Order Vault Drain Via Incorrect Collateral Handling
value_at_risk: Shared GMX multichain order vault - report states >$4M at block 22019054 on Arbitrum
exploit_path:
1. Create a position with collateral larger than the relay fee (any small position works).
2. Call updateOrder() with a fee; _handleFeePayment finds the multichain balance insufficient and falls back to 'reduce the user's position collateral'.
