title: u128→u64 downcast during withdraw_liquidity corrupts share math and can cause division-by-zero
value_at_risk: Futarchy AMM base and quote reserves
exploit_path: 1) Attacker holds LP in a pool whose total_liquidity exceeds u64::MAX. 2) It deposits so that total_liquidity mod 2^64 is very small. 3) withdraw_liquidity casts both liquidity_to_withdraw and total_liquidity to u64 and passes them to get_base_and_quote_withdrawable. 4) The truncated denominator inflates base_to_withdraw/quote_to_withdraw. 5) Attacker withdraws far more than its pro-rata share. Variant: total_liquidity % 2^64 == 0 makes the division panic and freezes all withdrawals.
preconditions: Pool liquidity > 1.8e19 units; attacker has an LP position; deposit sized to control the truncated denominator

title: Anyone Can Drain Multichain GM Token’s Balance
value_at_risk: GLV/GM tokens or a bridged deposit belonging to another user
exploit_path: 1) A cross-chain deposit for a user is recorded by the bridge handler. 2) Attacker calls createGlvDepositFromBridge directly (the onlyController modifier is missing) and supplies the victim's deposit/account plus receiver = attacker. 3) The router creates the GLV deposit without a signature check. 4) GLV tokens are minted to the attacker.
preconditions: A bridge deposit is pending/recorded; attacker can name its parameters

title: Genesis rewards will be stolen
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes OLY so it holds a share of stakingVault. 2) Calls distributeEth() with zero value. 3) _distributeEthInternal uses address(this).balance when msg.value == 0, so it redistributes the genesis ETH reserve. 4) The ETH is split to stakers/validators/farms; the attacker's staking share captures part of it.
preconditions: TaxRouter holds genesis ETH; attacker has a staking position

title: Fake pool could drain all the pool's tokens
value_at_risk: All of a payout token's balance held by SilicaPools, shared across pools
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deploys FakeIndexer with decimals()=0, shares()=0, balance()=0. 2) Builds PoolParams{floor: target_balance, cap: target_balance+1, index: fake, payoutToken: victimToken}. 3) Calls collateralizedMint(params, 1) and startPool(params). 4) Calls redeemShort(params): relativeBalance and relativeAmount use attacker-chosen cap/floor, and payout = (cap - balanceChangePerShare) * collateralMinted / relativeAmount. 5) The contract transfers the whole payout-token balance. Report PoC: pool balance 395,501,040 -> 0, attacker 1 -> 395,501,041.
preconditions: Any pool holding the payout token; attacker needs 1 unit of collateral

title: Front-runners of Uniswap swaps can steal most funds
entry_point: UniswapSwapAssetManager.uniswapSimpleSwap (amountOutMin, poolFee, relayer are not in the proof)
value_at_risk: Value of a user's input note in the darkpool
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sees a victim's uniswapSimpleSwap args in the mempool or acts as its relayer. 2) Front-runs with the same note/proof but amountOutMin=0 and a poolFee whose Uniswap pool has almost no liquidity. 3) Adds liquidity at an extreme price in that pool. 4) The victim's swap executes against the attacker's liquidity at a terrible price. 5) Attacker keeps the note value minus the service fee.
preconditions: Mempool visibility or relayer position; attacker can add liquidity in the chosen pool

title: Attackers can use arbitrary TokenReserve accounts to undermine the protocol
value_at_risk: Fluid vault liquidity and other depositors
exploit_path: 1) Attacker supplies collateral and calls operate with a supply_token_reserves_liquidity account from a different, higher-exchange-price token. 2) In a borrow-only operation the liquidity program validates only the borrow reserve, so the fake supply reserve is accepted. 3) load_exchange_prices uses it, inflating exchange_rate and ratio_at_cf. 4) Attacker borrows more than its collateral supports. 5) It defaults or self-liquidates, leaving bad debt that the vault absorbs.
preconditions: Attacker has collateral; vault has borrow liquidity; borrow-only path skips supply-reserve validation

title: Missing Oracle Program Ownership Check Enables Unintended or Forced Liquidation
entry_point: activate_liquidation / execute_liquidation with an attacker-supplied chainlink_program
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deploys a fake Chainlink program returning price 0. 2) Calls activate_liquidation for a healthy LTT, passing the fake program (no program-ID check). 3) After the 5-minute cooldown calls execute_liquidation, which re-reads the fake price and marks the LTT liquidated. 4) If the liquidation pays the liquidator the collateral at a discount, the attacker takes it.
preconditions: LTT active; attacker can pass chainlink_program; liquidation must transfer collateral to the caller

title: Share inflation via donation enables repeated value capture in new pools
value_at_risk: New pool deposits, including the next depositor's principal
exploit_path: 1) Attacker is the first depositor with 1 unit and receives INITIAL_SHARES_AMOUNT jTokens. 2) Front-runs the victim's deposit by donating victim_deposit * INITIAL_SHARES_AMOUNT, which raises pool supply without minting shares. 3) The victim's deposit floors to 0 jTokens. 4) Attacker withdraws the entire pool supply, recovering the donation plus the victim's deposit.
preconditions: Attacker first in a fresh pool; victim deposit pending; withdraw fee 0 in the PoC

title: Malicious user can steal NFTs from anybody
value_at_risk: NFTs held by or deposited to the marketplace diamond
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls listItem(..., tokenId, price, transferNFT=false) for an NFT it does not own; only idToListed is checked. 2) The listing is recorded with seller = attacker. 3) Attacker calls delistItem(tokenId). 4) delistItem calls _transfer(address(this), address(this), seller=attacker, tokenId), which moves the NFT out of the diamond to the attacker. 5) Attacker owns the victim's NFT.
preconditions: The diamond holds the target NFT (from any prior listing/trade deposit)

title: Random task execution
value_at_risk: Victim's DSProxy funds and token approvals
exploit_path: 1) Victim builds a DeFi Saver recipe that calls an attacker-controlled contract (token, pool or callback). 2) During the flash loan the wrapper holds permission to execute actions through the victim's DSProxy. 3) The attacker's contract reenters executeAction() and injects arbitrary tasks. 4) The tasks transfer the victim's tokens or use its approvals to the attacker.
preconditions: Victim includes an attacker-controlled call in its recipe; flash loan active

title: Investors funds can be drained using FrictionlessTransferManager
value_at_risk: Tokens users have approved to the transfer manager
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deploys a fake ERC-3643 token whose isAgent(attacker) returns true. 2) Creates a bilateral transfer offer using that fake token against a victim who has a residual approval to the manager. 3) Calls confirmTransferOffer as the fake token's agent, which the manager accepts as sufficient authorisation. 4) Both legs execute, pulling the victim's approved real token; the attacker receives the funds.
preconditions: Victim has an outstanding allowance to the manager; attacker can deploy a token and create an offer

title: [C-01] NFT stolen due to wrong approval validation (Project self-injected exploit)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls the approval helper so that _isApprovedForAll[msg.sender][attacker] is set (the helper checks the wrong mapping). 2) With operator status it calls approve(attacker, tokenId) for a victim token. 3) Calls transferFrom(victim, attacker, tokenId). 4) The NFT transfers.
preconditions: The helper's wrong-mapping path is reachable from an external call

title: [C-03] Unrestricted `diamondCut` allows unauthorized facet modifications
value_at_risk: All assets and permissions controlled by the diamond
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls diamondCut with a facet cut that adds or replaces selectors. 2) Installs a facet exposing a function that transfers the diamond's tokens/ETH to the attacker. 3) Calls that selector. Because diamondCut is unrestricted, the attacker becomes the effective owner of the proxy.
preconditions: diamondCut reachable without access control on the deployed diamond

title: TradableStaking: shares accounting is corrupted
entry_point: TradableStaking.stake -> _stake (line 174: shares: uint64(shares) instead of userShares)
value_at_risk: Entire staking vault TVL and rewards
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes a small amount. 2) The Stake record stores the global `shares` counter instead of the user's `userShares`, so the attacker's position appears to own all outstanding shares. 3) It withdraws/redeems, receiving assets and rewards as if it owned the whole vault. 4) Honest stakers are left with unbacked positions.
preconditions: Vault has other stakers and a non-zero share supply

title: Fixed participants can claim more premium than expected
exploit_path: 1) Some fixed participants withdraw, which burns fixedBearerToken and shrinks fixedLidoSharesTotalSupply while variableSideCapacity is unchanged. 2) A remaining fixed participant calls claimFixedPremium. 3) sendAmount = claimBal / fixedLidoSharesTotalSupply * variableSideCapacity is inflated. 4) It receives more premium than its share; later claimants are underfunded.
preconditions: Fixed-side withdrawals occurred before the claim; attacker is a fixed depositor

title: mint(), initiateRedeem(), and redeem() lack access control
value_at_risk: Collateral (stETH and other assets) backing lvlUSD
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves LevelMinting to spend lvlUSD (residual allowance or an approval just mined). 2) Attacker calls initiateRedeem with order.benefactor = victim, order.beneficiary = attacker, lvlusd_amount = victim balance. 3) The contract burns the victim's lvlUSD and records the collateral owed to the attacker. 4) After the cooldown, completeRedeem sends the collateral to the attacker.
preconditions: Victim has an allowance to LevelMinting; redeemer-role check disabled or attacker passes it (the PoC sets checkRedeemerRole=false)

title: Anyone can call uniswapV3MintCallback() stealing the protocol fees
value_at_risk: All ERC-20 balances held by BunniHub, including protocol fees
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deploys a fake pool contract whose token0()/token1() return the real token addresses. 2) Calls BunniHub.uniswapV3MintCallback(amount0, amount1, abi.encode(fakePool, ...)). 3) The only check is msg.sender == decodedData.pool, which holds because the attacker is both caller and 'pool'. 4) The callback transfers amount0 of token0 and amount1 of token1 to msg.sender, with amounts chosen by the attacker.
preconditions: BunniHub holds token balances; callback is externally reachable

title: Vulnerability in fillLPOrder allows draining of reward tokens
value_at_risk: Reward tokens held by the orderbook
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates an LP order whose tokenAmountsRequested is set to the orderbook's current reward-token balance. 2) Sets frontendRecipient = attacker. 3) Self-fills the order: fillLPOrder assigns the entire tokenAmountsRequested[i] to frontendRecipient as fees. 4) Attacker later claims the rewards, draining the reward balance.
preconditions: Reward tokens are funded in the orderbook; attacker can create and fill its own order

title: Expired PT doesn't always redeems 1:1 for underlying token
value_at_risk: Lending markets that accept PT as collateral
exploit_path: 1) A Pendle PT trades below 1:1 near/after expiry (redemption through SY is not exactly 1). 2) The oracle still prices it at 1. 3) Attacker buys PT at the discount, supplies it as collateral at par, borrows against it, and defaults. Profit = discount minus borrow cost.
preconditions: PT depegs at/after expiry; a market accepts the PT at the oracle price

title: Users Can Use Flashloan to Increase Voting Power of Expired Positions and Execute Proposal for Their Benefits
exploit_path: 1) Attacker owns a veGUAN position whose lock has expired. 2) Flash-loans GUAN and calls increaseStakeAndLock, which adds stake without extending the lock (assuming the related Medium-01 is fixed). 3) Voting power counts the full stake even with remainingLockDuration = 0 because 1e18 is always added. 4) In the same tx it votes for and executes a proposal that pays it, then unstakes (block.timestamp == lockedUntil).
preconditions: Flash-loan liquidity for GUAN; a proposal in its voting window; council review does not block it

title: Missing checkpoint validation in MaturityAdjustedStaking::_processRewards allows infinite reward claiming
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes and claims to checkpoint N (lastProcessedCheckpoint = N, lastProcessedTime = now). 2) Calls claim(tokenId, 0): _processRewards sets lastProcessedCheckpoint = 1 and rolls lastProcessedTime back. 3) Calls claim(tokenId, 1), which hits fromCheckpoint == toCheckpoint and rolls lastProcessedTime further back. 4) Calls claim(tokenId) again: rewards from the rolled-back timestamp to now are paid a second time. 5) Repeat indefinitely.
preconditions: Staking contract with checkpoints and funded rewards

title: Incorrect Balance Accounting
value_at_risk: Bridged tokens in flight to other users
exploit_path: 1) Several users bridge the same token; tokens are delivered to LayerZeroProvider before their lzCompose messages execute. 2) Attacker bridges a small amount of the same token. 3) If the attacker's lzCompose executes first, it records the provider's entire remaining balance as the attacker's deposit. 4) The attacker's credit includes other users' tokens; later messages find nothing.
preconditions: Concurrent bridges of the same token; attacker's message ordered first

title: User Voting Shares Can Be Burned By Others
entry_point: VotingPool.update -> _update (anyone can update another user's position)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes. 2) Flash-loans pod tokens to push CBR down. 3) Calls update(victim) for each large staker; _update burns their shares because CBR fell since they staked. 4) Attacker's relative voting power and reward share rise; it claims the rewards. 5) Unwind the flash loan.
preconditions: Flash-loanable pod tokens; victims staked at a higher CBR

title: Transient swap routes can be set for other smart contract users to steal tokens
value_at_risk: Tokens redeemed by victim smart contracts (queued Safe txs, permissionless protocols)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls redeemWithRoutes with a fake vault address it controls and a malicious custom route; initTransientSwap stores the route in transient storage. 2) Inside the fake vault's callback the attacker triggers a legitimate redeem of a victim contract. 3) swapForQuote sees the transient route and uses it, returning nothing for the victim's tokens. 4) minBuyAmount is always 0 in the vault, so no slippage check stops it. 5) Attacker keeps the tokens.
preconditions: A victim contract's redeem can be triggered permissionlessly within the attacker's tx; transient route persists for the tx

title: transferFrom() allows arbitrary token transfers without approval
exploit_path: Title states transferFrom allows arbitrary token transfers without approval; if the implementation omits the allowance/owner check, the attacker calls transferFrom(victim, attacker, tokenId) for any token. Body is withheld, so the exact call path is unverified.
preconditions: Unknown (body withheld); assumes the standard ERC-721 entry point is affected

title: Multiple redeems of the same deposit are possible
value_at_risk: Tokens held by localPort (underlying and wrapped native)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates a deposit whose cross-chain call fails, so its status is Failed. 2) Calls redeemDeposit(nonce) repeatedly. 3) _redeemDeposit pays deposit.owner (the attacker) and never clears the status or amounts. 4) Each call withdraws the same underlying again, draining localPort.
preconditions: Attacker owns a failed deposit; localPort holds other users' deposits

title: Market close callback trusts collateral amount
value_at_risk: LP/stable liquidity of the trading pair
exploit_path: 1) Attacker opens a trade with a large collateral. 2) Issues a margin update that removes as much collateral as possible (paid back to it). 3) Issues a market close on the entire position. 4) The callback uses o.trade.initialPosToken (the original size) instead of the current collateral, and the (collateral + fees >= initialPosToken) branch treats it as a full close. 5) PnL is paid on the original size while the collateral was already withdrawn: free money.
preconditions: Upkeeper fulfils orders in issue order; price roughly unchanged

title: CryptoPunks can be stolen via mint frontrunning
entry_point: PNFTToken.mint (buys a CryptoPunk offered to the pool)
exploit_path: 1) Owner calls offerPunkForSaleToAddress(pool, price) and then mint(). 2) Attacker front-runs mint(). 3) The contract buys the punk and assigns the PNFT to msg.sender (the attacker), not the owner. 4) Attacker owns the punk-backed NFT.
preconditions: A pending offerPunkForSaleToAddress + mint; mempool visibility

title: A Liquidator Can Liquidate a Position With In initely Bad Price
entry_point: Liquidation path (same price logic as regular trades)
exploit_path: 1) Attacker has a position in a market. 2) It manipulates the liquidity size to closely match the liquidation size, producing an almost infinite price. 3) It liquidates a liquidatable position, taking the full collateral with the liquidation discount. 4) The residual is bad debt for the protocol.
preconditions: A liquidatable position; attacker can set/manipulate liquidity size

title: Attackers can front-run transactions to steal user funds after approving allowances
value_at_risk: Any user's tokens approved to AssetBridge
exploit_path: 1) Victim approves AssetBridge for token T. 2) Attacker front-runs the victim's stake call with stake(token=T, from=victim, to=attacker, amount). 3) The contract consumes the victim's allowance and mints liquidity tokens to the attacker. 4) Attacker unstakes for the underlying, or repeats on the unstake path if the approved token is the LP token.
preconditions: Victim's approval is mined before their call; mempool visibility

title: LoanLogic returns the USD value of total collateral in all tokens, not just the collateral token
value_at_risk: Other depositors' collateral in the ILM strategy
exploit_path: 1) Attacker deposits token A into the ILM and receives shares. 2) Gifts token C to the strategy via AAVE supply-on-behalf, inflating reported total collateral USD. 3) Victim deposits A and receives fewer shares than fair. 4) Attacker withdraws its shares, which are now worth more than its deposit. 5) Victim's remaining shares are unbacked/locked.
preconditions: AAVE V3 supply-on-behalf enabled; gift token has a price; strategy values total collateral

title: Anyone can steal anyones Patron NFTs
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls batchTransferFrom(victim, attacker, victim, tokenIds). 2) The extra `by` parameter is passed to _batchTransferFrom and used for the permission check instead of msg.sender. 3) Since by = victim (the owner), the transfer is authorised. 4) Every listed token moves to the attacker.
preconditions: None beyond gas; any token owner can be spoofed

title: Worthless `user_underlying_token` can be provided on `stake` to mint valid LP tokens
value_at_risk: Staking vault assets / LP redemption value
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates a worthless token mint. 2) Calls stake with user_underlying_token of that mint; the account is not constrained to vault.underlying_mint. 3) The program still mints valid LP tokens for the vault. 4) Attacker redeems the LP tokens for the vault's real underlying. Report notes fees_vault and pool_token_account must share the worthless mint, which it says is achievable via other missing constraints.
preconditions: fees_vault and pool_token_account can be made to use the attacker's mint

title: Incorrect comparison in claim validation allows non-winners to claim
value_at_risk: Prize pool for a completed round
exploit_path: 1) Attacker stakes in a round. 2) A winner_id is drawn. 3) validate uses the inverted comparison stake_id >= winner_id, so a non-winner's claim passes while the real winner may be rejected. 4) Attacker claims the prize. 5) The true winner cannot claim the same prize.
preconditions: A round has ended and a winner_id is set; attacker has a stake in the round

title: Anyone can call `uniswapV3MintCallback()` stealing the protocol fees (devtooligan, Jackson)
value_at_risk: All ERC-20 balances held by BunniHub, including protocol fees
exploit_path: Same primitive as finding 46, reported separately by electisec: attacker sets decodedData.pool to an address it owns, passes the real token0/token1 and arbitrary amounts, and the hub transfers them to msg.sender.
preconditions: BunniHub holds token balances; callback externally reachable

title: Any account can mint infinite amount of $GORPLES tokens to any compatible vault
exploit_path: 1) Attacker builds mint_gorples with mint_authority set to any key contained in config.contracts (the constraint only checks membership, not a signature). 2) Sets vault to its own associated token account with the GORPLES mint. 3) Mints an arbitrary amount to itself. 4) Sells into any pool/vault that accepts GORPLES.
preconditions: config.contracts contains a key the attacker can name; GORPLES has liquidity or redemption value

title: VAULT FLASHLOAN() FUNCTION CAN BE ABUSED TO DRAIN THE PROTOCOL
exploit_path: 1) Attacker contract calls flashLoan(token, amount, self, data). 2) In the callback it calls ChromaticRouter.addLiquidity(market, 1, amountReceived, owner=attacker): the borrowed tokens are deposited back into the vault as the attacker's liquidity. 3) It transfers only the fee to the vault. 4) balanceAfter >= balance + fee passes. 5) Attacker owns an LP position worth `amount` for the price of the fee and can withdraw it later.
preconditions: Vault has `amount` liquidity; flash-loan fee below the value of the LP position

title: Oracle’s _sanityCheck for prices will not work with slashing
exploit_path: 1) A slashing event causes a legitimate price drop larger than the allowed per-period decrease. 2) The price update reverts, leaving the stale higher price. 3) Attacker exits or arbitrages at the stale price before the oracle catches up. 4) Once the update lands, remaining holders bear the loss.
preconditions: Slashing event large enough to breach the sanity bound; stale window

title: Missing Validation (uniswapV3SwapCallback access)
value_at_risk: Tokens held by the swap contract
exploit_path: 1) Attacker calls uniswapV3SwapCallback directly, or reaches it through a receive() during native handling or by passing malicious contracts to swap(). 2) The callback does not verify msg.sender is a genuine Uniswap V3 pool. 3) It pays the caller-specified amounts to an attacker-chosen target.
preconditions: The contract holds tokens and the callback is externally reachable

title: Funding Rate Manipulation #1
exploit_path: 1) Attacker self-trades (or two colluding accounts) at extreme prices repeatedly. 2) updatePrice stores those hourly prices, so the funding rate is set arbitrarily. 3) Attacker holds the position that receives funding. 4) The average price used in liquidation can also be skewed to drain the insurance pool.
preconditions: Thin market; two accounts; funding/liquidation uses the stored prices

title: [C-01] Using Uniswap spot price is subject to manipulation
exploit_path: 1) Attacker flash-manipulates the Uniswap V3 pool that the on-chain Quoter reads (add/remove liquidity or swap). 2) quoteExactInput/quoteExactOutput return a mispriced collateral value. 3) Attacker borrows against the inflated collateral or withdraws excess. 4) It unwinds the manipulation and leaves bad debt.
preconditions: Flash liquidity; quoter used for withdraw/borrow/repay/liquidation; multi-swap quotes compound the error

title: [C-02] Underlying tokens of UniV3 Liquidity Position are unchecked
exploit_path: 1) Attacker creates a Uniswap V3 pool with two worthless ERC-20s it controls. 2) Mints a large position (liquidity is self-declared by the pool). 3) Stakes the position; stake() does not validate the pool's tokens. 4) Rewards are proportional to the inflated liquidity, so the attacker earns a disproportionate share. 5) Claims and exits.
preconditions: Rewards funded; pool creation permissionless; staking rewards priced by position liquidity

title: [C-01] Pending payouts excluded from total balance cause incorrect share calculations
entry_point: Staking pool totalOwed/finalizeUnstake (pendingPayouts excluded from balanceOf)
exploit_path: 1) transferPayout fails for some users, so amounts are recorded in pendingPayouts. 2) totalOwed/lockLiquidity still use balanceOf(this), which includes the pending amounts. 3) Early withdrawers are credited more than the free balance. 4) They exit with more than their share; later shares are unbacked.
preconditions: At least one failed transferPayout; pool with multiple stakers

title: Fraudulent Messages May Be Sent Through The Bridge
value_at_risk: Bridge ETH and vault tokens across chains
exploit_path: 1) Attacker sends a bridge message whose message.to is SignalService and message.data is sendSignal(attackerHash). 2) The bridge does not restrict to/data, so SignalService stores the attacker's hash under the Bridge sender. 3) Attacker generates a valid proof for that signal. 4) Processes a malicious message that transfers ETH from the Bridge or tokens from vaults to the attacker.
preconditions: Bridge accepts user messages without restricting to/data; attacker can call processMessage with a proof

title: Permissionless Markets Can Spend Global Rewards
exploit_path: 1) Attacker submits market parameters through the permissionless factory, choosing rewardToken and rewardAmount. 2) The manager calls safeTransferFrom(rewardWallet, marketAddress, rewardAmount), pulling from the shared reward inventory. 3) The attacker-chosen market is funded with treasury rewards; if the attacker controls the market's payout, it can route them to itself.
preconditions: Factory is granted proposer privileges; manager has allowance from rewardWallet

title: Malicious constructed Jupiter swap_data and remaining_accounts might cause payer to lose funds
value_at_risk: Payer's token account in the sponsored flow
exploit_path: 1) In a sponsored transaction both user and payer sign. 2) The user (attacker) supplies params.swap_data and ctx.remaining_accounts. 3) Nothing checks that the input token account belongs to the user rather than the payer. 4) The attacker binds Jupiter's authority to the payer's token account, so the CPI swaps the payer's tokens to the attacker.
preconditions: Sponsored flow where the payer signs; attacker controls swap_data and remaining_accounts

title: Flawed Precision and Scaling Logic in price()
value_at_risk: Outer protocols that consume the composite price
exploit_path: Inverted feeds multiply the accumulator by 10**assetDecimals * 10**feed.decimals / feedPrice on every iteration, so the scale compounds and the final price is off by orders of magnitude (or overflows). Non-inverted feeds keep a 36-decimal offset and truncate fractions. An attacker arbitrages any outer contract that trusts the price.
preconditions: A composite oracle configured with an inverted feed; an outer contract consuming it

title: Capped yAsset redemptions can overpay when the live price exceeds usdCap
exploit_path: 1) A yAsset trades above its usdCap (e.g. $1.03 vs $1.00). 2) Attacker mints proUSD against a fairly priced yAsset. 3) Unmints into the premium yAsset: the denominator is capped at $1.00, so it receives 100 units for 100 proUSD instead of ~97.09. 4) Sells the yAsset at $1.03 and keeps the difference. 5) Works for instant and queued redemptions.
preconditions: An enabled redemption yAsset trades above usdCap; attacker has capital to mint proUSD

title: Spot reserve price can be manipulated and used as an oracle output
exploit_path: lastprice derives the price from current Soroswap reserves, so an attacker can swap to skew reserves, call lastprice, and use the manipulated price in an outer lending/borrowing contract. Profit requires a consumer that acts on the price in the same transaction.
preconditions: An outer protocol consumes lastprice; attacker can move the pool

title: [H-04] Manager#buy, sell - No slippage protection leaves users vulnerable to front-running and sandwich attacks
exploit_path: Sandwich the user's swap because Manager.buy/sell pass no min-amount; the attacker captures the price impact.
preconditions: victim trade in the same block

title: Logic Flaw in `verify()` Function in `ChainlinkLightClient.sol` Contract
value_at_risk: bridge messages gated by the light client (not quantified)
exploit_path: approvedStorageRoots is never populated, so verify() takes the account-proof branch and skips storage-proof verification; forged storage values can be relayed to UserContract.
preconditions: a valid account proof for an approved state root; attacker supplies the storage proof

title: [H-01] IncentivePool#onlyClaimableTime - Modifier is bypassable
exploit_path: Stake the minimum to trigger _harvest() through stake/unstake before claimableTime, collecting rewards early.
preconditions: rewards funded for the current period

title: Oracle Lacks Update Cycle Verification
exploit_path: No oracle update-cycle check; a stale Navi price can be consumed by borrow/repay/liquidation.
preconditions: stale price still accepted

title: Can create lien for collateral while at auction by passing spoofed data
exploit_path: Spoofed lien data while collateral is at auction creates a lien against it, capturing the auction collateral.
preconditions: collateral is at auction

title: Incorrect tolerance for price reported by Chainlink Oracle (blockdev)
exploit_path: The Chainlink tolerance is mis-set, so a price outside the intended band is accepted and misprices trades.
preconditions: price deviates within the wrong tolerance

title: removeSession() doesn't remove data completely from installed policy modules
exploit_path: removeSession leaves enabledActionIds and the validator entry behind; a removed session key may still pass permission checks after re-install.
preconditions: session previously installed

title: Creating a token with a poisoned router
exploit_path: Token creator points the router at a malicious contract; buyers' swap input is diverted to the attacker.
preconditions: attacker creates the token

title: Position Overwritten At Claim Tick
exploit_path: A second claim at the same tick overwrites the stored position, letting the claimer take the position's value.
preconditions: position at claim tick

title: Disabled lender's loan configuration can be used by a borrower
exploit_path: Borrower uses a disabled lender's stale loan configuration to borrow on favourable terms.
preconditions: lender disabled but config readable

title: Stakers/vault depositors can be front-run and lose their funds
exploit_path: Front-run a vault deposit/withdraw to move the share price and dilute the victim.
preconditions: victim transaction visible

title: ETH deposited by the user may be stolen.
exploit_path: deposit()/mint() wrap msg.value but pullToken also pulls `amount` from the caller, leaving WETH in the router; anyone calls sweepToken to take it.
preconditions: a user deposited ETH and left WETH in the router

title: Order of execTransactionFromGnosis() and initialBalances() is reversed
value_at_risk: tokens pre-stored in the payroll contract
exploit_path: executePayroll records balances after pulling from the Safe; pre-stored tokens can be spent, enabling theft of stuck funds.
preconditions: stuck token balance present

title: Missing Threshold Leading to Possible Draining of Funds
exploit_path: Integer division makes cost zero when tokensToBuy*price < exchangeRate; the attacker buys tokens for nothing.
preconditions: small purchase size

title: Missing enforcement of route.destination check may allow fillers to solve intents on other supported chains
exploit_path: A filler fulfils an intent on a different supported chain with matching addresses and claims the reward.
preconditions: addresses match on another supported chain

title: Anyone can steal all funds from the market due to incorrect health accounting for pending pnl from difference of intent price and market price when multiple intents are used.
entry_point: entry point described in the report body (see exploit_path)
value_at_risk: entire collateral token balance of the market
exploit_path: 1) Attacker funds account1 and account2 with small collateral (e.g. 40 each). 2) account1 signs an intent to open a position at a price far above the oracle price but inside maxPriceDeviation (e.g. 120 vs 100). 3) account2 submits the intent; validate() counts only this intent's pending PnL, so account1 still looks healthy (40 - 20 = 20). 4) Repeat the same signed intent several times in the same epoch; each submission re-checks only the newest intent and ignores the earlier ones. 5) At settlement the combined PnL (3 x -20 = -60) leaves account1 deeply negative while account2 holds the offsetting profit. 6) account2 withdraws, draining the market.
preconditions: multiple intents pending for the same account in one epoch (no settlement in between); intent price within protocol maxPriceDeviation; two colluding accounts

title: Bridge Signals Can Be Forged to Drain the

title: ECDSA signatures can be trivially bypassed

preconditions: victim account uses PasskeyRegistryModule; attacker can submit the userOp

title: Reentrance can lead to loss of funds

title: Token approvals can be stolen in DAOfiV1Router01.addLiquidity()

title: First depositor inflation attack in stake_usdu_mint_susdu

title: Infinite mint/redeem possible through signature manipulation

preconditions: attacker can submit a multi-instruction transaction; attestation parser ignores index fields

title: If operatorFlag == false, attacker can steal all NFTs within the contract.

preconditions: operatorFlag == false; attacker can deploy an ERC777 token and pool; victim position present

preconditions: A funded fundraise vault; migrate callable by anyone

title: Unnecessary Reentrancy Protection In markFilled() Function Allows Fund Theft
entry_point: SolverNetInbox.markFilled (nonReentrant) via OmniPortal.xsubmit; open()/close() for reentry
value_at_risk: solver deposit / order escrow on the source chain
exploit_path: 1. Attacker opens order A and receives tokens on the destination chain. 2. While the solver's xsubmit(markFilled) is pending, reenter the inbox via a malicious token in open() or by closing an old order. 3. markFilled reverts on the nonReentrant guard; OmniPortal treats the failed message as executed and does not retry. 4. After fillDeadline+CLOSE_BUFFER, attacker calls close() and reclaims the source-chain deposit for order A.
preconditions: Pending markFilled message; malicious token or closable old order; deadline window

title: Ownership of ProxyAdmin May Be Transferred To Any Wallet
value_at_risk: all assets held by wallet proxies (ProxyAdmin can upgrade any wallet)
exploit_path: 1. Attacker creates/controls a BLS wallet. 2. Calls walletAdminCall with ProxyAdmin as target and transferOwnership(attacker) as calldata; the only check is that the first parameter equals msg.sender. 3. ProxyAdmin is owned by VerificationGateway, so the onlyOwner check passes. 4. Attacker owns ProxyAdmin and can upgrade any wallet proxy to a malicious implementation, then steal assets.
preconditions: Attacker can create a BLS wallet; ProxyAdmin ownership unchanged

title: [C-01] Cloning a `subGauge` can result in an uninitialized proxy
value_at_risk: rewards directed to a newly created subGauge
exploit_path: 1. Observe createSubGauge in the mempool. 2. Front-run the initialize call and initialize the clone with attacker-chosen stakingToken/governance. 3. Attacker controls the subGauge and can redirect/capture rewards deposited into it.
preconditions: Pending uninitialized clone; front-running window

title: Attacker can steal Staking reward
exploit_path: Same mechanism as index 10: _shortCircuitRewards=1 during flashMint prevents fee processing; staking inside the callback records shares without distributing pending fees; unstaking afterward captures them.
preconditions: flashMint enabled; V2 pool tokens; pending fees

title: Missing Access Control On V4/Pancake Callbacks
value_at_risk: tokens settled during an ongoing V4/Pancake swap; Reflex's captured revenue
exploit_path: 1. During the callback window, an attacker contract re-enters unlockCallback/lockAcquired. 2. The handlers check router callback state but not msg.sender, so the fake caller is treated as the swap context. 3. Router settles real tokens to the attacker contract; attacker extracts the arbitrage profit and returns just enough for the flow to finish. 4. Reflex captures zero revenue.
preconditions: Attacker contract in the callback window; router holds/settles tokens

title: Share Price In ation Attack
exploit_path: 1. Attacker fills the first batch to maxDepositBatchSize and becomes sole depositor at 1:1. 2. Withdraws almost all shares in two steps, leaving 1 wei. 3. Transfers assets directly to the strategy (no shares minted), inflating NAV per share. 4. A later depositor gets ~1 share for a large deposit; attacker exits the dust share and captures the value.
preconditions: Attacker has maxDepositBatchSize capital; victim deposit after manipulation

title: Malicious Users Can Steal All Staking Rewards From StakedCSX Due to a Logical Error
exploit_path: 1. Stake CSX. 2. Make repeated zero-value StakedCSX transfers; each triggers _beforeTokenTransfer -> _claimToCredit. 3. credit[token][account] += rewardOf(account) doubles the credit on every call because rewardOf already includes the existing credit. 4. Withdraw the inflated credits.
preconditions: Staked balance and accrued rewards

title: Lack of sender account check when handling SwapReference message
exploit_path: 1. Attacker sends an ft_transfer with a SwapReference message to the contract; ft_on_transfer does not check that the sender is a registered Ref V1/V2 contract. 2. Message opens/decreases/closes/liquidates the referenced margin account. 3. on_decrease_trade_return reduces the user's debt and adds assets while the attacker incurs no cost.
preconditions: Known margin account id; token transfer callback path

title: Incorrect subtraction leads to draining of the pool
exploit_path: 1. Attacker holds any liquidity position. 2. Calls removeLiquiditySingle for 1 wei. 3. The code uses `uint256 _changeInVirtualBalance = _prevVirtualBalance = _virtualBalance;` (assignment instead of subtraction), so the change equals the whole remaining pool balance. 4. Attacker withdraws all tokens from the pool.
preconditions: Any LP position; pool funded

title: Missing asset index check allows any token to mint shares
exploit_path: 1. Attacker deploys/uses an arbitrary ERC20 not registered in assetIndexes. 2. assetIndexes[token] returns 0, which equals USDC_SPOT_INDEX; _isAssetSupported(0) passes. 3. deposit() treats the token as USDC and mints shares at USDC value. 4. Attacker withdraws real USDC against the minted shares.
preconditions: Share token mintable; vault holds USDC; withdraw asset set

title: Bypassing Quarantine and Reusing the Same Report Allows Minting Uncollateralized stETH
value_at_risk: Lido stETH (unbacked mint against a reused 101 ETH report)
exploit_path: 1. Create a staking vault with 1 ETH and connect it. 2. Send 100 ETH directly (not via fund()) so inOutDelta is unchanged. 3. An oracle report writes 101 ETH into quarantine. 4. Disconnect, finalize using the same report, wait out quarantine, reconnect, withdraw 99 ETH, reconnect with 2 ETH, re-apply the old 101 ETH report, then mint 50 liability shares for free. 5. Repeat the disconnect/reconnect cycle.
preconditions: Vault creation (permissionless), 1 ETH capital, oracle report/quarantine timing (24h)

title: First Depositor Can Inflate Share Price to Steal Funds from Subsequent Depositors
exploit_path: 1. Deposit minimal amount to get shares. 2. Withdraw almost all, leaving 1 wei. 3. Donate assets directly to balanceContract. 4. updateNav recomputes pricePerShare from the inflated NAV; a victim deposit gets zero/few shares; attacker withdraws the remaining share and captures the value.
preconditions: Attacker is first depositor; victim deposit; updateNav called

title: BVM_ETH and MNT Deposited in Messengers Can Be Stolen
value_at_risk: BVM_ETH stranded in L2CrossDomainMessenger and MNT stranded in L1CrossDomainMessenger
exploit_path: 1. A user's cross-chain transfer fails, leaving BVM_ETH/MNT in the messenger awaiting retry. 2. Attacker initiates a cross-domain message whose target is the BVM_ETH contract and whose data is approve(attacker). 3. relayMessage executes the approve from the messenger. 4. Attacker transferFrom's the stranded BVM_ETH; same pattern for MNT on L1.
preconditions: Stranded failed relay messages; messenger holds the asset; target not blocked as unsafe

title: Anyone Can Drain The Multichain Balance
exploit_path: 1. Attacker sends a compose message with account set to a victim who has a multichain balance. 2. actionData is also attacker-controlled; the handler uses the victim's balance to perform a GM or GLV deposit. 3. Attacker sets themselves as receiver. 4. Victim's balance is spent, attacker receives the GM/GLV position.
preconditions: Victim has a multichain balance; attacker can send a LayerZero compose message (permissionless)

title: AMM price manipulation using openReversePosition
value_at_risk: liquidation profits from a manipulated AMM price
exploit_path: 1. Open a buy position, then immediately open a reverse position of the same size. 2. currentPositionNotional is fractionally larger than notionalToDecreaseBy, so decreasePosition runs and zeroes the position, but afterPositionUpdate does not save a zero-size position while the AMM has already been updated. 3. Repeat to push the AMM price. 4. Liquidate strong positions at the manipulated price for profit.
preconditions: Perp market with liquidity; capital for positions; liquidation opportunity

title: LMSR Saturation Enables Free Share Minting and Vault Theft
value_at_risk: market vault collateral (1 USDC per winning share at resolution)
exploit_path: 1. Wait for any market to reach delta/b >= 27 through organic trading, or create a market with minimum b=1 USDC and push it there yourself. 2. Call buy_shares with max_cost=0; cost_to_buy returns 0 because both before/after cost functions saturate. 3. Receive shares for free. 4. At resolution, claim 1 USDC per winning share from the vault.
preconditions: Saturated LMSR state; free-rider needs organic volume, self-funded needs ~30 USDC for b=1

title: Reentrancy attack on `Sales.take` can lead to draining funds
exploit_path: 1. An ERC777/ERC223 (or callback) token is the auction token. 2. During take(), a recipient's token transfer callback reenters take(). 3. taken(sale) is only set at the end, so the transfers repeat. 4. Repeat until the Sales contract is drained of that token.
preconditions: Callback token; a sale with a bid; attacker is a recipient (lender/agent/borrower)

title: Reentrancy attack to duplicate NFT tier to other contracts
exploit_path: 1. Attacker deploys a contract implementing onERC1155Received. 2. Transfers all MEME404 tokens to it. 3. During _mintTier, the callback reenters and transfers the tokens back to the attacker before minting completes. 4. Both the attacker and the contract hold the tier, minting NFTs without holding tokens.
preconditions: MEME1155 tier; attacker contract; mint in progress

title: Outbox double-consume (replay) via unbounded leafIndex in MerkleLib.verifyMembership
value_at_risk: token portals and any L2->L1 message consumer
exploit_path: 1. Obtain a valid Merkle proof for a leaf at index i (e.g. 5). 2. Call consume with an aliased index i + 2^depth (e.g. 13); verifyMembership only reads the low d bits, so the proof still verifies. 3. leafId = (1 << path.length) + _leafIndex differs, so the consumed check does not trigger. 4. Repeat to re-consume the same message: withdraw tokens from portals or re-execute privileged actions.
preconditions: A valid proof for a message (public or observed); tree depth known

title: Fee Payment Underflow Inflates Vault TotalValue
exploit_path: 1. A vault's fees exceed its value (e.g. after slashing). 2. Owner gifts ETH directly to the vault (bypasses inOutDelta). 3. voluntaryDisconnect and settleLidoFees withdraw valueToTransferToLido. 4. totalValue - feesTransferred underflows to max uint256; owner mints stETH against infinite collateral.
preconditions: Vault with fees > value (slashing), owner, direct ETH gift

title: Lack of validation in `_claim_tokens_from_vault` allows claiming tokens from incorrect sale event
entry_point: claim_tokens_from_vault.rs (no check that user_account belongs to token_sale_event)
exploit_path: 1. Participate in a cheap token sale and get a user_account. 2. During claim, pass the token_sale_event for a more valuable sale. 3. The program does not verify the user_account/sale binding, so it releases the expensive tokens.
preconditions: Two sales; a user_account from one; claim phase open

title: Users can drain `sol-staking` vault by providing their own `underlying_vault`
exploit_path: 1. Call stake() and pass an attacker-owned token account as underlying_vault. 2. The CPI transfers the user's SOL into the attacker's account instead of the protocol vault, but the program records a staking position. 3. Call unstake to redeem the position for real SOL from the pool. 4. Repeat until the pool is drained.
preconditions: Staking pool live; attacker owns a token account

title: currentStore.principal is not subtracted after it was withdrawn, allowing users to claim it again infinitely
exploit_path: 1. Stake tokens. 2. Call unstake; the contract transfers the principal but does not zero currentStore.principal. 3. Call unstake again and again; each call transfers the same principal. 4. Drain the contract's balance.
preconditions: A staked position; contract funded

title: Funds can be Drained from the Protocol by Liquidating an Account During an Asset Transfer
exploit_path: 1. Attacker controls Alice, Bob, Cynthia. 2. Alice submits a transfer granting Bob an in-the-money expired option and leaving Alice insolvent; managerData calls the attack contract. 3. Before Alice's risk check, the attack contract starts Alice's insolvent auction; Cynthia bids 100%, taking Alice's liabilities with no risk check. 4. Alice is now empty and passes the risk check; Bob settles the option and withdraws the fictitious profit.
preconditions: Attacker controls three accounts; option/auction support; managerData callback

title: [C-01] Locking collected ETH by triggering createPoolAndAddLiquidity twice
entry_point: createPoolAndAddLiquidity (no guard that tradingEnabled was true)
exploit_path: 1. After a token is fully funded and the first pool is created, donate enough tokens to the contract. 2. Call createPoolAndAddLiquidity again; tradingEnabled is already false but the function does not check it. 3. The second call consumes ETH collected for other tokens and locks it into the attacker's pool.
preconditions: A funded token; attacker donation; second call allowed

title: Unvalidated arbitrary calldata in eisenForwarder calls allows theft of user-approved aTokens
value_at_risk: aTokens of any user who approved the receiver
exploit_path: 1. A legitimate user approves the receiver to pull aTokens and the approval persists. 2. Attacker calls start with cfg.user=attacker, cfg.eisenForwarder=aWETH, and swapFlashToDepositCalldata=transferFrom(victim, receiver, balance). 3. The receiver executes the call, pulling the victim's aTokens. 4. withdraw(type(uint256).max) unwraps them to WETH and _sweep sends the underlying to the attacker; a 1 wei flash loan satisfies the flow.
preconditions: Victim's persistent aToken approval to the receiver; real Aave pool; 1 wei flash loan

title: All taker collateral and collected fees can be stolen by re-entering via `RFTLib.settle` to manipulate uniswap spot price when adding Maker liquidity
value_at_risk: all taker collateral and collected Uniswap fees held by the Ammplify diamond
exploit_path: 1. Attacker adds maker liquidity in a range and pays a small amount. 2. During RFTLib.settle, tokenRequestCB manipulates the Uniswap spot price. 3. PoolWalker.settle mints liquidity using amounts different from what the attacker paid; the mint consumes more value from the contract than the attacker supplied. 4. Attacker restores the price, waits out the JIT penalty, and withdraws; PoC nets ~$8,889 and can steal 90-99% of both token balances.
preconditions: Maker liquidity add; attacker is an RFTPayer; JIT penalty wait

title: Vault share-price manipulation
exploit_path: 1. Attacker holds or opens a position whose open_pnl benefits them. 2. Calls request_snapshot repeatedly; avg_open_pnl converges toward the current open_pnl because request_count has no limit. 3. pnl_per_token and the share price move in the attacker's favor. 4. Attacker deposits/redeems at the manipulated price.
preconditions: Open positions with PnL; capital; epoch snapshot mechanism

title: Arbitrary wrapData in EscrowHelper Allows Attacker to Steal User Funds
value_at_risk: any user's tokens approved to EscrowHelper
exploit_path: 1. Victim approves EscrowHelper (required by pullWrapDepositAndLock). 2. Attacker calls wrapAllDepositAndLock with wrapData = token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount). 3. address(token).functionCall(wrapData) executes the transferFrom as the helper. 4. Victim's full allowance is transferred to the attacker.
preconditions: Victim approval to EscrowHelper

title: Teleport should verify subaccount is tied to current borrower
attacker: holder (new borrower of a liquidated vault)
entry_point: teleport(uint toDeposit, uint toBorrow, address subAccount)
value_at_risk: previous borrower's collateral in a subaccount
exploit_path: 1. A collateral vault is liquidated; attacker becomes the new borrower. 2. Previous borrower still has a dangling allowance to the vault and a non-zero balance. 3. Attacker calls teleport with the previous borrower's subAccount; transferFrom pulls their funds into the vault/attacker position.
preconditions: Vault liquidated; dangling approval; previous owner still holds collateral

title: F-2024-1806 - Double Spending in castVotes() Function By A Malicious Actor - High
exploit_path: 1. Observe a signed castVotes payload. 2. Replay it repeatedly; the signature does not bind msg.sender and has no nonce. 3. Each replay executes the same series of calls, including transfers that consume the signer's allowances. 4. Drain the signer's approved tokens.
preconditions: A valid castVotes signature; signer has token approvals
